  states gate 8's absence and its reason for all four parity circuits
  (**G178**).

### G94 - ELK throws on a unity-gain op-amp self-loop with horizontally drawn passives on its net - and the "lateral" half of the first narrowing is contradicted at block scale

`[RAN]` elkjs **0.7.1 and 0.9.3** both raise

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Invalid hitboxes for scanline constraint calculation.
```

on `circuits/opamp-buffer.ts` - **the simplest circuit this repository owns** -
when `output_coupling_cap` is drawn horizontally. 3 runs of 3.

**Narrowed twice.** An exhaustive sweep of all 32 orientation assignments of that
circuit's five passives: **9 of 32 fail**, smallest failing set **one component**,
which is a **one-character change** to the layout input. A hypothesis test then
isolated two conditions that are **both necessary**: the op-amp's **output and
inverting input on one net** (the unity-gain self-loop) **and** a
**horizontally-drawn lateral hanging off that same net**. Removing either lays
out cleanly.

**A unity-gain buffer is among the most common analog idioms there is.**

**AMENDED 2026-10-19 by the second spike, and the amendment contradicts half of
the paragraph above.** `[RAN]` `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §5 reproduced
the identical exception on `oc-audio`, a **12-part declared `include()` block**
of `circuits/optical-compressor/` whose `circuits/optical-compressor/parts/audio-path.ts`
declares this entry's exact recipe, and swept all **2^8 = 256** orientation
assignments of its eight passives: **45 fail**, smallest failing set **two
components**.

| arm, on `oc-audio` | result |
| --- | --- |
| break the op-amp self-loop, leave everything else | **0 of 256 fail** |
| remove the lateral off the self-loop net, keep the loop | **32 of 128 STILL FAIL** |
| remove the lateral AND break the rheostat strap on `gain_terminal` | **31 of 128 still fail** |

**So the self-loop is necessary and the lateral is NOT.** *"Removing either lays
out cleanly"* above holds for the self-loop half and fails for the lateral half:
delete `attenuator_series_resistor` and a different horizontal passive takes its
place.

**WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT RESOLVE IT.** The first
narrowing was done on `opamp-buffer`; this one on `oc-audio`. **Whether the
block-scale result CORRECTS this entry or is a SECOND SUFFICIENT CONDITION in a
different circuit cannot be decided from either measurement**, and the spike
says so in terms. What both agree on: **breaking the self-loop lays out
cleanly** - a single test on `opamp-buffer`, and **all 256 assignments on
`oc-audio`**, which is the stronger of the two arms.

**AND THE PARENTS ARE WORSE THAN THEIR BLOCKS.** `[RAN]`

| | h-rails | v-bare | v-rails | self-loop cells |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WHOLE-optical-compressor`, 37 parts | **REFUSED** | ok | ok | 3 |
| its three declared blocks | 1 of 3 refused | 3 of 3 ok | 3 of 3 ok | |
| `WHOLE-pultec-three-band`, 76 parts | ok | **REFUSED** | **REFUSED** | 4 |
| its five declared sections | 5 of 5 ok | 5 of 5 ok | 5 of 5 ok | |

**`THREE_BAND_REFERENCE` refuses under BOTH vertical policies, including the
default, while every one of its five declared sections lays out.** Its four
self-loop cells are the strapped wipers of `RV_LO_CUT`, `RV_LO_BOOST`,
`RV_HI_Q` and `RV_MID`. **That strap is deliberate and declared, which is why
this shape is not rare here**: `[CODE]` `circuits/pultec/electrical/three-band.ts`
declares it at each pot - *"the wiper is tied to the cw end, so only the
ccw-wiper section carries current and the pot reads as a variable resistor"* -
and `circuits/transistor-preamp/parts.ts` states the same strap as a convention
across both preamp boards with its reason: *"every leg fails to its MAXIMUM
resistance - never open, never zero."* **A rule that refuses an op-amp or pot
self-loop refuses house style.** `pultec-mid` carries one of the four on its own
and lays out.

`[RAN]` **A single-flip sweep over all 18 blocks - 108 flips, one passive each -
produced ZERO failures**, which is the block-scale analogue of the 69-flip
result below. **The crash needs at least two horizontal passives.**

**It is ELK and not a wrapper artifact.** The pre-layout graph was extracted and
run through each build directly, with layout options read out of the skin rather
than retyped; both versions produce the identical exception, and both lay out the
working graph to identical geometry.

`[RAN]` **Scope: a single-flip sweep over the other four circuits - 69 flips -
produced zero failures.** Specific, not common, and reachable from an ordinary
idiom.

> **A STALE COPY OF THIS ENTRY'S BULLETS STOOD HERE AND WAS REMOVED
> 2026-10-20.** Task 14's amendment **extended** the Found / Evidence /
> Verified block rather than replacing it, so the entry carried the
> pre-amendment copy here and the complete one below - and a reader met the
> stale set first, which carries no *why it is open* and no *what would settle
> it*. The task **caught it and disclosed it in its report**, which
> `.superpowers/` being gitignored makes **not a record**: a defect found in the
> register is fixed in the register. The surviving block below is the complete,
> amended one.

**AMENDED 2026-10-20 BY TASK 14, UNDER CONTROLLER RULING R30: THE GENERATOR
REFUSES WITH A DIAGNOSIS, AND THE CRASH ITSELF IS NOT REACHABLE THROUGH THIS
DRIVER.** Task 12's review went looking for this entry's crash across **twenty
arms** beyond the production run of twelve declared blocks - every vertical
two-port node turned horizontal on all twelve, at both rotations, and each
circuit flattened to a single graph - and got **zero raises** (`docs/known-gaps.md`
**G185**). The reason is principled rather than lucky, and it is `docs/known-gaps.md`
**G180**'s caveat biting in the useful direction: this entry's crash is a
HITBOX computation, and this driver changed every one of its inputs relative to
the two spikes that measured it through `netlistsvg` - **boundary nodes are
zero-size here where `netlistsvg` drew 30x20 `inputExt` cells, node sizes are
the library's own micrometres rather than skin-scaled extents, and the
direction is `RIGHT` rather than the skin's `DOWN`.** So: **the crash is not
reachable through the production path, nor through any graph this repository's
own data produces.** It remains reachable only by hand-building an `ElkNode` -
which `tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts` already does, for a DIFFERENT
rejection: it raises a **`JsonImportException`**, an input-validity error (a
dangling edge reference), **never this entry's `IllegalStateException`.** The
raise-HANDLING is therefore genuinely exercised by a real `elkjs` rejection;
the raise this entry measured is not, by anything in the tree.

**WHAT THIS AMENDMENT DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say this entry was wrong, and
it does not say `elkjs` cannot crash this way. It says this driver does not
feed it the inputs that crashed the spikes' driver, measured over the circuits
this repository has.

**DECIDED: the generator REFUSES, with a diagnosis, and does not retry.** Four
reasons:

- **The criterion above is a defined outcome, and refusal is one.** Nothing in
  it asks for recovery.
- **A retry under different orientations would be the generator choosing a
  semantic property of the circuit**, which spec §1.5 assigns to a reviewed
  template or a reviewed rule and explicitly denies the backend.
- **The one mechanism anybody has proposed is measured wrong**, immediately
  above - *"constraining laterals on a self-loop net to vertical"* leaves 32 of
  128 `oc-audio` assignments still failing. An implementer who followed it
  would ship a non-fix. `CLAUDE.md`'s criterion-versus-mechanism rule applies
  exactly: the criterion binds, the mechanism was advice from someone who had
  not yet tried it, and the deviation is recorded here rather than silently
  worked around.
- **A silent retry would hide the dependency defect** - `docs/known-gaps.md`
  **G84**'s lesson one level down: the sheet would look fine and a backend that
  cannot draw a unity-gain buffer would never be reported.

**WHAT THE REFUSAL CARRIES, built by `tools/schgen/elk/diagnose.ts`'s
`diagnoseRaise`/`renderDiagnosis` and wired into `tools/schgen/elk/layout.ts`'s
`elkBackendFrom`:** the block and the backend's exact pinned version, the
exception's own sentence, **the self-loop cells** (`lib/schgen/elk/self-loop.ts`'s
`selfLoops` - the structural reading of the one shape this entry measured as
necessary, diagnostic only and never a rule: an empty result does not mean the
raise is unrelated to this entry's family, and a non-empty one does not license
a retry), the horizontal passives hanging off those nets, and **the exact
serialized bytes that produced the raise, printed verbatim.**

**THE INPUTKEY DECISION, STATED AND COSTED, PER THE BRIEF'S OPEN QUESTION.**
`tools/schgen/elk/layout.ts` already carried the serialized bytes as
`Mismatch.backend-raised.inputKey` since Task 12; Task 14's decision is to
PRINT THEM VERBATIM in the diagnosis rather than hash them. Three reasons: (1)
the bytes already exist on the value for free - `elkInputOf` computes them
once and `raised()` already carries them, so printing costs one more line and a
hash would cost the same to compute but more to USE; (2) a hash needs a
recovery path - a written artefact keyed by the hash - that nothing in this
tree builds, and building one for a case **G185**'s twenty-arm sweep found
**zero occurrences of** is untried machinery for an unobserved problem, which
is exactly what `CLAUDE.md`'s criterion-versus-mechanism rule declines to do on
no evidence; (3) **this entry's own `docs/known-gaps.md` G95 is why a hash is
the worse choice and not merely the costlier one** - *"the serialization is
deterministic; the circuit is not"* means the bytes already ARE the manifest's
key, with no collision between two different graphs and no instability for one
fixed graph, and a hash of them can only ever be a second identity for the same
thing - a second place a bug (truncation, a weak hash, the wrong line copied)
could make two different graphs agree or one graph disagree with itself. **The
cost, stated rather than hidden:** the diagnosis is as big as the graph - on
the largest declared block measured (`pt2399-core/pt-core`, **G189**: 151 wires
after canonicalisation), the serialized input runs to several kilobytes, and
that whole string lands in a thrown error's message. Accepted because a raise
is, by every measurement in this register, not a path any real block takes
today, so the cost is paid on an exceptional path rather than a hot one.

**WHAT WOULD MAKE THE CRASH REACHABLE AGAIN, AS A CRITERION RATHER THAN A
WARNING.** `docs/known-gaps.md` **G200** records that the staircase and the
doubling-back in this driver's drawings are properties of `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts`'s
edge model, and the edge model, the port sides and the node sizing are all live
questions. This driver's zero-raise result holds only as long as all three of
the following stay true, per the table in **G180**:

1. **boundary nodes stay zero SIZE** (not `netlistsvg`'s drawn 30x20 `inputExt`
   cell);
2. **node sizes stay the library symbol's own micrometre boxes**, never scaled
   to a skin's drawn extent;
3. **`elk.direction` stays `RIGHT`**, never reverted to the analog skin's
   `DOWN`.

A change to `graph.ts` that alters ANY of the three - on a block that ALSO
carries a self-loop with a horizontally-drawn lateral on that net, this
entry's own necessary condition - must re-run the arms this entry and **G185**
measured (the twenty-arm horizontal/flattened sweep, and the three `oc-audio`
arms: break the self-loop, remove the lateral, remove the lateral and the
rheostat strap) before trusting a zero-raise result again. Nothing in Task 14
re-runs that sweep on a changed graph builder, because nothing in Task 14
changes one.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` §4, 2026-10-19. **Amended from**
  `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §5, the same day. **Amended again** by
  Task 12's review (the twenty-arm sweep, recorded in **G185**) and by Task 14
  (the refusal-with-diagnosis decision, the inputKey costing, and the
  reachability criterion above), under controller ruling **R30**.
- **Evidence** the 32-subset sweep, the two-condition test, and the direct
  two-version run. A check that could have failed: 23 of 32 assignments succeed.
  For the amendment: the 256-subset sweep and the three-arm narrowing on
  `oc-audio`, the 2x3x3 parent runs, and the 108-flip sweep - each with a
  passing arm (0 of 256 after breaking the self-loop; 5 of 5 sections laying
  out) that could have come back the other way. **For Task 14's amendment:**
  the twenty-arm sweep is **G185**'s own evidence, re-cited rather than
  re-executed; `tests/schgen/elk/self-loop.test.ts` and `tests/schgen/elk/raised.elk.test.ts`
  drive `selfLoops`, `diagnoseRaise` and `renderDiagnosis` directly (a check
  that could have failed: a fixture with no self-loop asserts an EMPTY result,
  not an omitted one, and a fixture with the self-loop but a vertical passive
  asserts that passive is NOT reported horizontal), and a real `elkjs`
  rejection (a dangling edge, the same mechanism `tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts`
  already used) drives the full backend seam end to end.
- **Verified** RELAYED, both halves - the writer read both spikes' measurements
  and re-executed neither. **One exception, CONFIRMED by the writer:** the two
  strap declarations quoted above were read in `circuits/pultec/electrical/three-band.ts`
  and `circuits/transistor-preamp/parts.ts` directly. **For Task 14's
  amendment:** RELAYED for the twenty-arm sweep (Task 12's review, re-cited
  from **G185**). CONFIRMED for the diagnosis module, its wiring into
  `elkBackendFrom`, and every test named above - this writer wrote and ran all
  of them, and perturbed the wiring (below) rather than only asserting it.
- **Why it is open** it is a defect in a dependency the design proposes to
  adopt, and **the design has no value for the outcome it produces.**
  **Narrowed by Task 14:** the HANDLING half - what the generator does when
  the backend throws - is now decided and built; what stays open is the
  dependency defect itself (unfixed upstream, and this entry does not claim it
  is fixed) and §1.5's separate question below.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a generator must have a defined outcome
  when its layout backend throws.** The spec's §1.3 selector is three-valued -
  `not-applicable`, `applicable`, `generation-failed` - and **a block that reaches
  ELK and makes ELK throw is a further outcome it does not name.** Spec §5.3
  sharpens where that lands: `RealiseResult` is **two-valued** in the source,
  with 30 `mismatch(...)` call sites funnelling into one `ok: false`, so a
  `realise` that RAISES is outside that type entirely. **MET by Task 14:** a
  throw is `backend-raised`, with a diagnosis, never an escaped exception and
  never a silent `not-applicable` (**G84**). Separately, whether §1.5's
  orientation rule library can be required never to emit this shape - **NOT
  settled by Task 14** and stays open. **A second criterion, Task 14's own: the
  reachability conditions above** - boundary-node size, node sizing and
  `elk.direction` - **are what a later change to `graph.ts` must check against**
  before trusting a zero-raise result.
- **MECHANISM, and the first one is now MEASURED WRONG.** This entry suggested
  *"constraining laterals on a self-loop net to vertical"*. **On `oc-audio` that
  leaves 32 of 128 assignments still failing**, so a rule library built to it
  would ship a non-fix. The criterion above is what binds. **Untested
  replacement:** constrain the self-loop itself, which is the only arm that
  cleared a whole sweep - and it is untested as a RULE, because a strapped pot
  wiper is a deliberate convention here and a rule that refuses it refuses house
  style. **Task 14 proposes no mechanism for the dependency defect itself** - the
  decision is to refuse with a diagnosis, not to fix `elkjs`.

### G95 - ELK's output is a function of input cell ORDER, so a drawing is not a stable property of a circuit

`[RAN]` Three random shuffles of the same netlist - same components, same nets,
same partition - produce **three distinct drawings out of three, on 4 of 4
circuits**, none matching declaration order:

| circuit | distinct outputs | inter-net crossings across four orders |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer` | **3** | 32, 38, 23, 27 |
| `pultec-low-boost` | **3** | 73, 48, **139**, 61 |
| `pt2399-core` | **3** | 195, 290, 203, 276 |
| `transistor-preamp-lab` | **3** | 139, 56, 136, 140 |

**Reordering the `.capacitor(...)` calls in a circuit file would change every
generated schematic**, and move its measured quality by up to a factor of three
without changing the circuit. Aspect moves with it.

**Determinism for a FIXED input still holds** - 14 of 14 inputs gave one distinct
output over three runs, and an earlier session's probe regenerated byte-identical.
The two facts are compatible and must not be confused: **the serialization is
deterministic; the circuit is not.**

register still presented it as a measured 4"*.

moves when the declaration is reordered.

### G96 - ELK on five real repository circuits is worse than the representative probe on every axis

`[RAN]` Measured on the axes `generation-prior-art-third-pass.md` §3.5 used, so
the numbers compare directly. Its 25-part Pultec-SHAPED probe scored 15 inter-net
crossings, 1.72 bends per edge, 2.55 aspect.

| | real circuits, 14 successful runs | the probe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inter-net crossings | **16 - 195** | 15 |
| **bends per edge** | **2.19 - 3.27** | **1.72** |
| aspect | 1.37 - 5.19 | 2.55 |

**Not one of fourteen runs beats the probe on bends per edge**, the term the one
user study in evidence blames for unreadability. Crossings reach **195 on a
24-part circuit**. Aspect reaches **5.19:1** where the parent spec calls a 1.97
ribbon unusable.

**So the representative probe was the best case, not a typical one.** G91 records
the conflation that preceded this; this entry is the measurement that settles it.

**Degree is not the explanatory variable.** `pultec-low-boost` has the highest max
net degree (15) and middling crossings; `pt2399-core` at 13 has the worst.

**Rail symbols make it worse, consistently** - more crossings than the bare policy
on all five circuits. A `gnd` glyph is added and the ground net is still routed as
a long bus, so the symbol costs edges and saves none. §1.6's "power symbols"
candidate gets nothing from this front end for free.

**AMENDED 2026-10-19: "on every axis" is true of WHOLE circuits and false of
declared BLOCKS.** `[RAN]`
`docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §3 ran 18
declared blocks of 1 to 28 parts through the same converter and skin:

| on the best policy (`v-bare`) | 14 whole-circuit runs | 18 declared blocks | the probe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bends per edge | 2.19 - 3.27, **0 of 14 beat the probe** | **0.67 - 2.89, 6 of 18 beat it**, 12 of 18 at or below 2.00 | 1.72 |
| inter-net crossings | 16 - 195 | **0 on every block of 8 parts or fewer**, then 4, 5, 14, 16, 20, 28, 37 | 15 |
| aspect | 1.37 - 5.19 | 0.87 - **6.63** | 2.55 |

**So the axis that sharpened is bends per edge, and the axis that got worse is
aspect**: `pultec-mid` scores a good 1.77 on a **2716 x 410, 6.63:1** sheet and
`pultec-hi-boost` 1.66 on 4.70:1, where the parent spec calls a 1:1.97 ribbon
unusable. **Bends per edge and aspect disagree about those two blocks, and only
one of them is what a reader meets.**

**Size is a WEAK predictor of bends per edge, and the apparent effect is a
property of the POLICY.** `[RAN]` Spearman rho over the 18 blocks is **+0.57**,
falling to **+0.15** once port edges are excluded; under `h-rails` it is
**+0.92** and **+0.87**. A 28-part block (1.77) beats a 3-part block (2.00).
**Crossings grow faster than linearly in parts; bends per edge does not grow at
all.**

**The policy result holds and sharpens:** `h-rails` is worse on bends per edge
for **17 of 17** blocks that laid out, and it is the policy that makes
`oc-audio` crash (G94).

**RE-TAKEN 2026-10-20 BY TASK 17, AND THE HEADLINE AXIS OF THIS ENTRY CANNOT BE
COMPARED AT ALL.** `[RAN]` `tools/schgen/remeasure.ts` over all twelve declared
blocks, with every figure in
`docs/schematic/m1-remeasurement.md`. Of the five figures this entry's tables
publish, **two are the same quantity as this generator's and three are not**:

| axis | comparable? | what the re-take found |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **bends per edge** | **NO - G220** | the spike divides ELK's `bendPoints` by ELK's own spanning-chain edge count and this repository divides bends by maximal POLYLINES. **So "0 of 14 beat the probe" and "6 of 18 beat it" have no successor figure**, and this generator's 0.19 to 1.33 must NOT be set beside 1.72 |
| **inter-net crossings** | yes, in kind | 0 on the six blocks of 3 placements or fewer, then 1 at 8 parts, 7 at 9, 5 at 12, 7 at 16, 7 at 17 and 78 at 24. **The spike's *"zero on every block of 8 parts or fewer"* FAILS on `oc-power`**, the same 8-part block, at 1 crossing |

| wire length | **NO** | the skin's pixel against the 1.27 mm grid step |
| canvas / occupied area | **NO** | the spikes published a canvas in pixels and no area |

**AND CROSSINGS DO NOT GROW MONOTONICALLY IN PARTS HERE, which is the other half

### G97 - a declared functional group does not draw disjointly, and a repeated sub-circuit does not draw congruently

The schematic-authoring spec's §3.4 names three criteria this repository can make
**objective** where they are judgement calls elsewhere. `[RAN]` Two were measured
and **both answer no.**

**Functional-grouping disjointness** - the Pultec stand-in group is a declared set:

| circuit | members | bounding box | of canvas | non-members inside it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pultec-low-boost` | 8 | 1016x621 | **67 %** | **11** |
| `pultec-hi-boost` | 8 | 1412x566 | **61 %** | **11** |

**Congruence of repeated sub-circuits** - `transistor-preamp-lab` declares four
structurally identical bias legs. Drawn `jumper -> trim` offsets: `(-141, +153)`,
`(**+564**, +173)`, `(**-912**, +153)`, `(-147, +143)`. **One leg runs the
opposite direction from the other three.**

**The claim in §3.4 is not wrong - it is a claim about the MODEL, and these are
measurements of a DRAWING.** The model does declare the group and the repetition.
What is established here is that **a general engine given no template honours
neither**, which is precisely what makes those two criteria worth having.

**AMENDED 2026-10-19: CONGRUENCE FLIPS AT BLOCK SCALE.** `[RAN]`
`docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §6 laid the
same four declared bias legs out ALONE, `v-bare`:

| leg | canvas | jumper -> floor | floor -> trim | jumper top-left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `leg-upper` | 354x190 | (+107, +28) | (+54, +65) | (81, 22) |
| `leg-feedback` | 390x190 | (+125, +28) | (+54, +65) | (81, 22) |
| `leg-lowerA` | 378x190 | (+119, +28) | (+54, +65) | (81, 22) |
| `leg-lowerB` | 378x190 | (+119, +28) | (+54, +65) | (81, 22) |

**Every vertical offset identical, the internal vector identical, the starting
corner identical.** The single x difference is **predicted exactly** by
`6 * len(component id) + 5` - 107 / 125 / 119 / 119 for ids of length
17 / 20 / 19 / 19, **4 of 4 to the pixel** - which is the 0.6 em at 10 px
monospace the skin uses. **The blocks draw congruently and the drawn width of
the component's NAME is what separates them.**

**So the flat measurement above is not the general answer: at block scale an
untemplated engine DOES honour the repetition, and §3.4's claim that this
repository can make congruence objective is supported there and was not at flat
scale.**

**Two qualifications, and the first one is the one a template designer needs.**
`[RAN]` Under `v-rails` the congruence BREAKS: `leg-upper` runs from `VCC` and
gets a `vcc` glyph, `leg-feedback` runs from `COLLECTOR` and gets none, and the
two land at (91, 42) on 364x210 against (81, 22) on 390x190, with the internal
vector splitting +54 / +44. **Adding a rail symbol to one of two otherwise
identical blocks stops them drawing alike.** Under `h-rails` the four stay
congruent in shape while the canvas widths diverge further, 480 to 536.

**And the DISJOINTNESS half does not get an answer this way - it gets dissolved.**
Inside a single block disjointness is trivially satisfied, so a block-scale
measurement cannot pass or fail it. It remains measured only at flat scale,
where it answers no.

**RE-TAKEN 2026-10-20 BY TASK 17, WITH THE RAIL GLYPHS THE FOUR LEGS ACTUALLY
GET - AND CONGRUENCE HOLDS.** `[RAN]` `tools/schgen/remeasure-criteria.ts`. On
this pipeline the glyph is not a policy choice: `subgraphOf` puts every rail the
block touches in `g.rails` with its declared `RailSpec` and `anchorsToSymbols`
turns the block's own anchors into a power symbol for a rail and a global label
for every other boundary net. **The four legs genuinely differ in what they get,
which is this entry's own breaking condition:**

| leg | power symbols drawn | global labels drawn |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tp-leg-upper` | `VCC` / `power:VCC` at (17780, 1270) | `BASE` at (35560, 25400) |
| `tp-leg-feedback` | **none** | `COLLECTOR` at (17780, 1270), `BASE` at (35560, 25400) |
| `tp-leg-lower-a` | `GND` / `power:GND` at (35560, 25400) | `BASE` at (17780, 1270) |
| `tp-leg-lower-b` | `GND` / `power:GND` at (35560, 25400) | `BASE` at (17780, 1270) |

**All four place their three parts at the same three points** - `jumper` at
(7620, 3810), `floor` at (19050, 8890), `trim` at (25400, 19050), every one at
rotation 0 - **draw the same wire geometry, and bring their two boundary nets to
the same two anchor points.** The jumper-to-trim displacement is **(14, 12) grid
steps on all four.**

**THE STRUCTURAL REASON, so this is not read as luck:** a boundary net is a
ZERO-SIZE node in the graph ELK solves, and its glyph is attached at the anchor
the layout has already produced. **A glyph cannot move a layout it is placed
after.** Under `netlistsvg` the port was a 30x20 `inputExt` CELL that ELK laid
out like any other node, which is why adding one there moved the drawing.

**AND `6 * len(id) + 5` IS GONE, MEASURED AS A SPREAD RATHER THAN AS A NUMBER.**
The formula over the four jumpers' semantic ids - `upper_bias_jumper` (17),
`feedback_bias_jumper` (20), `lower_bias_a_jumper` (19), `lower_bias_b_jumper`
(19) - gives **107, 125, 119, 119**, which this entry matches *"4 of 4 to the
pixel"*. Its absolute output is in the skin's pixels and is not comparable; **the
SPREAD it predicts is dimensionless, and the measured spread is ZERO - 0 of 4.**

**THE DISJOINTNESS HALF IS RE-TAKEN AT SHEET SCALE, IN THIS ENTRY'S OWN THREE
COLUMNS, AND IT ANSWERS YES - ON A DIFFERENT SUBJECT.** `[RAN]` The five blocks
that draw, composed onto one A3 by seam B:

| block | members | its own extent | of the usable canvas | non-members inside it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| each of the four bias legs | 3 | 27 x 19 grid steps | **0.90 %** | **0** |
| `tp-leg-collector` | 2 | 13 x 17 | **0.39 %** | **0** |

Frame-box overlaps are **0 under both packers**, and `nonMemberContainments` -
the frame-box reading of the same criterion - is **empty on `mini`'s signal
sheet**, with the control that a frame grown to swallow the page reports every
symbol that is not its own block's.

**THE 67 % AND THE 11 ARE NOT COMPARABLE AND NOTHING WAS SUBSTITUTED FOR THEM.**
Their subjects are the Pultec stand-in groups of `pultec-low-boost` and
`pultec-hi-boost`; **neither network is in `PARITY_CIRCUITS` and no authoring
file in this repository declares either group.** The figures above are a
different subject and are not a before-and-after against those.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` §6. **Amended from**
  `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §6. **Re-taken** 2026-10-20, Task 17

- **Evidence** bounding boxes and offsets computed from the drawn geometry. At

### G98 - "wire through a symbol body" has two definitions and one manufactures 36 false defects

`[RAN]` Measured against netlistsvg's **declared** cell extents, ELK routes up to
**36** wires through symbol bodies on `transistor-preamp-lab`. Measured against
the **actually drawn** `<rect>`, **zero**, on every circuit and every policy.

**The declared extents are stale** because netlistsvg resizes a generic cell to
fit its ports without updating the group attribute. A control - netlistsvg's own
`common_emitter_full` example - reports 3 under both definitions, all three being
a transistor's own leads inside its circular glyph's bounding box.

**This is a worked instance of the G85 hazard the realization contract rests on**,
and it arrived **before any KiCad geometry exists.** G85 records that ~160
clearance refusals accreted pairwise because each step found the prior checks had
the same shape of blind spot - one obstacle category modelled against a second but
not a third. Here one obstacle category has two plausible definitions and the
wrong one is the one a reader would reach for first.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` §5.
- **Evidence** both measurements on the same drawings, plus the control.
- **Verified** RELAYED.
- **Why it is open** the obstacle-category matrix the spec's §1.4 requires has not
  been written, and this is an input to it.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: that matrix defines "symbol body" as DRAWN
  geometry, and states what it does with a glyph whose own pins sit inside its
  bounding box** - a transistor, in this repository, does.

### G99 - four of the five inputs a layout backend needs are now declared or derived by a reviewed rule; the residue is port direction below the circuit boundary, an ambiguous IC symbol, and net names

**REWRITTEN 2026-10-20 BY TASK 9 OF THE M1 SCHEMATIC-AUTHORING PLAN.** The entry
this replaces recorded five inventions an ELK spike harness had to make -
*"four of them have no home in the model and the design does not name one"* -
and set the criterion below. **Four of the five now have a home and the entry is
rewritten rather than deleted, because the criterion is not met: the residue is
real, it is measured, and G102 says the list of five was a lower bound.**

**THE CRITERION, CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED, because Task 9 did not author it and
nothing since has:**

> **CRITERION: every input a layout backend needs is either declared in the
> model or derived by a reviewed rule - none invented at the call site.**

**WHERE THE FIVE LANDED**

| the spike invented | where it is now | state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a **symbol** per kind | `lib/schgen/rules/symbols.ts`'s `symbolForKind` - a whitelist of four kinds that refuses loudly for the other seven, each with the reason the kind cannot answer - plus `part.symbol` in the model and a `ComponentOverride.symbol` in the authoring file for the residue | **settled** |
| a **pin-side partition** for an IC | `lib/schgen/rules/pin-sides.ts`, which reads every pin's side off the symbol's own `(at x y angle)` through the port's existing `pinSide()`, **on every path** | **settled** - a KiCad pin always carries an angle, so the geometry always answers (**G155**). The ELK backend reaches it as `sideOfPin(rot, pin)` rather than as `pinSidesFor`, which is the same rule and is what that module's own doc comment prescribes (**G182**) |
| a **drawn orientation** | `lib/schgen/rules/orientation.ts`, spec §1.5 step 2, holding one entry and returning `null` - which means step 3, not rotation 0 - everywhere else | **SETTLED AS A RULE, UNREACHABLE FROM THE IR - see G182**, and ruling **R29** settles it |
| a **rail convention** | `SchematicAuthoring.rails`, declared per net with its power symbol and `"ground" \| "supply"` | **settled** |
| a **port DIRECTION** | `SchematicAuthoring.portDirections`, declared per net | **settled at the circuit boundary, OPEN below it** |

**THE IC PARTITION IS THE ONE THIS ENTRY WAS SHARPEST ABOUT, AND THE RESULT IS
WORTH READING TWICE.** The spike split `pt2399-core`'s 16-pin PT2399 *"first half
in, second half out"* with *"no basis in the model at all"*. `Audio:PT2399` as
installed puts pins 1-8 at angle 0 and pins 9-16 at angle 180, so the library's
own answer is **eight left and eight right - the same split the spike guessed**.
That is not a vindication of the guess. It is the clearest possible statement of
why a guess that happens to agree is not evidence that it was derived: nothing
in the spike consulted the symbol, and the next IC would not have been so kind.

**AMENDED 2026-10-20 BY TASK 12's REVIEW, AND THE AMENDMENT IS ABOUT THIS ENTRY'S OWN JOB.**
This is the INVENTORY entry - the one a later agent reads to learn what a layout backend needs -
and its criterion is about the layout backend specifically. **That backend now exists, and it
cannot reach two of the three rules in the table above**, because `pinSidesFor(kind, symbol)` and
`preferredOrientation(kind, context)` both key on `ComponentKind` and a `BlockSubgraph` carries
`IrPart`s, which have no kind. **G182** has the measurement, the consequence and the three
mechanisms. The two halves land very differently and the table above now says so:

- **the pin-side half costs nothing.** `pinSidesFor` is `sideOfPin(0, pin)` per pin and reads
  `kind` only to compose one refusal message; `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts` calls `sideOfPin(rot,
  pin)` - the identical expression from the identical exported function in the identical reviewed
  module - and `pin-sides.ts`'s own doc comment **prescribes** exactly that: *"the rotated side is
  `sideOfPin(rot, pin)` at drawing time and is deliberately not baked in here."* **Nothing is
  invented and this row stays settled**, which is why the amendment to it is a pointer rather than
  a downgrade;
- **the orientation half does NOT run at all.** Every ELK node is built at rotation 0 - the
  library's own frame - so spec §1.5's step-2 rule library has no effect on any drawing, and step 3
  is unavailable too because `FIXED_POS` needs a rotation fixed before the graph exists. **A reader
  who starts here must not conclude that row is closed.** Controller ruling **R29** (plan, Task 13)
  settles it: the orientation map is carried as derived data from `from-network.ts` onto
  `BlockUnit` and the ports are fixed at that rotation, which is **G182**'s mechanism 2. The
  measurement that decided it: of 102 parts, **73 `null`, 28 rotation 0 and exactly ONE rotation
  180.**

**WHAT IS STILL RESIDUE, measured.**

1. **PORT DIRECTION FOR A CROSSING NET THAT IS NOT A DECLARED PORT.**
   `portDirections` is required for every net `Network.ports` binds - a missing
   one refuses by name - and a net that leaves a BLOCK without leaving the
   CIRCUIT has no direction anywhere. `transistor-preamp` has two:
   `BYPASS_JUMPED` and `BYPASS_CAP`, which cross between the emitter-bypass leg
   and the stage block because `emitter_bypass_cap` is declared outside `LEGS`.
   `optical-compressor` has one, `VBIAS_RAW`, which crosses from the power block
   to the sidechain block because U2's two sections serve two blocks. Three nets
   of 51 declared interface ports, and nothing says which way they point.
2. **"AN IC WHOSE SYMBOL IS AMBIGUOUS" WAS A CATEGORY ERROR AND IS NOT A
   RESIDUE.** This entry's original worry was an IC whose symbol does not say
   which pins are an interface in and which out, and Task 9 first answered it
   with a refusal in `pinSidesFor` for a symbol giving fewer than two distinct
   sides. **The Task 9 review proved that wrong and the refusal is deleted**
   (**G155**): a KiCad pin always carries an `(at x y angle)` and an angle always
   yields a side, so the geometry always answers which EDGE a pin sits on, and a
   one-sided glyph is a definite answer rather than an ambiguous one. The
   question the worry was really about - which pins are IN and which OUT - is a
   DIRECTION, it lives in `portDirections` and `InterfacePort`, and its gap is
   residue 1 above and nowhere else. The refusal never fired on the motivating
   part either: `Audio:PT2399` gives two distinct sides.

   What survives from it is a defect the refusal was camouflaging and that is now
   fixed: a declared pin side used to reach a `CircuitSpec` without ever being
   compared against the glyph's geometry. **G155** carries both halves.
3. **NET NAMES**, which is a SIXTH invention this entry did not have. See
   **G150**: the IR requires UPPER_SNAKE and 31 nets across two of the four
   parity circuits are not, so something between a model and a KiCad label has
   to rename them and no reviewed rule does.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` §0 and `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md`

- **Evidence** `bun tools/schgen/authoring-census.ts`, which is COMMITTED so a

### G100 - drawing a circuit as its declared blocks beats drawing it whole on every axis measured, and the mechanism is that the blocks have FEWER EDGES

`[RAN]` `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §4
is the paired control neither earlier pass could make: the same circuit, the same
converter, the same policy and the same skin, with the ONLY difference being
whether ELK saw it whole or one declared block at a time.

| `optical-compressor`, `v-bare` | parts | aspect | inter-net crossings | edges | bends/edge | wire length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **whole** | 37 | 4.05 | **293** | 139 | **3.18** | **159 967** |
| `oc-power` | 8 | 3.11 | 0 | 20 | 2.70 | |
| `oc-audio` | 12 | 1.48 | 28 | 37 | 2.89 | |
| `oc-sidechain` | 17 | 1.81 | 20 | 39 | 2.51 | |
| **its three declared blocks** | 37 | worst **3.11** | **48 total** | 96 | **2.70** | **35 070** |

**6.1x fewer inter-net crossings, 4.6x less wire, and the worst block's aspect is
better than the whole's.** `v-rails` gives the same shape: 267 -> 47, 3.27 ->
2.68, 5.04 -> 3.14. **And the 76-part `THREE_BAND_REFERENCE` goes from REFUSED
under both vertical policies to five drawings that all complete** (G94).

**THE MECHANISM, which is why this is not a lucky result.** `[RAN]` **The three
blocks carry FEWER EDGES THAN THE WHOLE - 96 against 139.** The parent's maximum
net degree is 19 and no block's exceeds 7, so a ground fanning to nineteen pins
across one sheet becomes four smaller fans, **and the edges that disappear are
the ones that were crossing everything.** Decomposition does not route the same
graph better; it hands ELK a smaller graph.

**AND IT IS NOT UNIFORMLY A WIN PER BLOCK.** Under `h-rails`, where the 76-part
whole does lay out, the whole scores 373 crossings / 3.56 bends per edge /
8.37:1 and the five sections total 239 / 3.37 / worst 4.05 - a real but much
smaller gain, **and the 28-part `pultec-mid` at 3.73 is WORSE than its own
parent.** The win is in the totals and in whether the thing completes at all.

**What does NOT improve is everything the flat spike's readability complaint was
about:** a 12-part block still has 28 crossings, two 17-part blocks are 4.5:1 and
4.7:1 ribbons, the capacitor banks are still out of frequency order, and the
interface ports still land mid-sheet (G99). **Block scale removes the
catastrophe and leaves the complaint.**

**THE MECHANISM WAS RE-TAKEN 2026-10-20 BY TASK 17 AND IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE ON
THIS BACKEND. THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING IN THE RE-MEASUREMENT.**

> **CORRECTED AT FIX ROUND 1, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE REFUTATION STRONGER
> RATHER THAN WEAKER. READ THIS BLOCK BEFORE THE FIGURES.** Round 1 reported
> **1.000x** - *"the decomposition removes ZERO edges"* - and that figure was an
> artefact of its own probe. `flatSubgraphOf` spread `{...c, blocks}` and **never
> rebuilt `c.unitBlock`**; `labelledNets` reaches `blockOfPin`, which reads
> `unitBlock`, so the "flat" subject was still told that `BASE` and `OUT_PRE`
> span several blocks - and `lib/schgen/ir/classify.ts:47` labels every net with
> `blocks.size > 1`. A labelled net becomes `external`, and an external net
> becomes a boundary NODE. **So the flat side was handed a boundary node for
> exactly the nets the split created: it inherited the decomposition it was the
> control for**, and 1.000x was one artefact cancelling another. **The finding
> is unchanged and its direction is now worse for the spike: decomposition does
> not merely fail to shed edges, it ADDS them.**

`[RAN]` `tools/schgen/remeasure-edges.ts`'s `edgeCensus`, with the probe fixed -
**the genuinely flat subject is the circuit declared as ONE block**, so no net is
multi-block and only a rail or an off-sheet net gets a boundary node:

| circuit | genuinely FLAT | its declared blocks | ratio | direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optical-compressor` | 43 nodes, **69 edges** | 3 blocks, 53 nodes, **72 edges** | **0.958x** | **ADDS 3** |
| `transistor-preamp` | 34 nodes, **48 edges** | 7 blocks, 53 nodes, **53 edges** | **0.906x** | **ADDS 5** |

**So *"decomposition does not route the same graph better; it hands ELK a smaller
graph"* is not merely unsupported here - it is backwards.** The blocked
declaration hands ELK a graph with MORE edges than the flat one.

**THE PER-NET RULE, AND IT IS SHOWN AGREEING WITH THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN
ASSERTED.** `edgesForNet` makes a net of degree n into n - 1 chain edges. Under
the BLOCKED declaration a net crossing k blocks is labelled, so it is external in
each of them and gains a boundary terminal in each: it contributes
`(U + k) - k = U`. Under the FLAT declaration the same net is internal unless it
is a boundary net of the subject, so it contributes `U - 1`; a boundary net of the
subject contributes `U` on both sides and cancels. **So blocked minus flat is
exactly the number of nets that (1) cross a block boundary inside the subject,
(2) are not rails, (3) are not off-sheet, and (4) do not leave the subject:**

| subject | the governing set | predicted difference | measured difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `optical-compressor`, whole | `OUT_PRE`, `VBIAS`, `VBIAS_RAW` | **3** | **3** |
| `transistor-preamp`, whole | `BASE`, `BYPASS_CAP`, `BYPASS_JUMPED`, `COLLECTOR`, `EMITTER` | **5** | **5** |
| the five-leg union | **empty - and only because of clause (4).** The crossing non-rail nets touching it are `BASE` and `COLLECTOR`; both reach `tp-stage`, so both leave the subject and cancel | **0** | **0** |

**ROUND 1 STATED A RULE WHOSE REFUTATION ROUTE COULD NOT FIRE, AND THAT WAS
WORSE THAN STATING IT FLATLY.** It said the difference is one edge per
*"multi-block net that is neither a rail nor a labelled net"*, and asserted these
two circuits had none. **`lib/schgen/ir/classify.ts:47` labels every net with
`blocks.size > 1`, so that set is EMPTY in every circuit this IR builds** - the
claim was a property of `labelledNets` wearing a measurement's clothes, and round
1's sentence *"nothing establishes that no such circuit exists"* was false:
**`classify.ts:47` establishes it.** The sentence is withdrawn. The governing set
is the one in the table above - the four clauses, not the two round 1 named -
which is non-empty on both whole circuits and **empty on the five-leg union
ONCE THE FOURTH CLAUSE IS APPLIED, where the same rule correctly predicts
equality.** That is the refutation route firing in both directions on real
subjects.

**AND ROUND 1's OWN SENTENCE NAMED TWO OF THE FOUR CLAUSES, WHICH MADE ONE
PUBLISHED FIGURE FALSE AS LITERALLY STATED - fix round 2, item B.** It said
*"crossing and not rails"*. The code tests `!rail && !offSheet` - three clauses -
and a SUBJECT adds a fourth, *does not leave it*. On the five-leg union the
THREE-clause set is **`{BASE, COLLECTOR}`, not empty**, and
`docs/schematic/m1-remeasurement.md` printed a bare *"none"*: **the predicted
difference was right and the set named was wrong.** **ONE VOCABULARY, used
throughout:** a set is named by the number of clauses IT has - **three**
circuit-wide, **four** for a subject - and round 1's defect was a **two-clause
SENTENCE** describing a set that always had more clauses than it named.
`governingNetsOf` now computes all four clauses and
`tests/schgen/remeasure-edges.test.ts` asserts the three-clause set and the
four-clause set SEPARATELY on that union, so the difference between them is a
check rather than a caveat. **Clause (3) is unexercised by any declaration here** -
`buildCircuit` hard-codes `offSheet: new Set()` (`lib/schgen/ir/build.ts:152`) -
and `[RELAYED]` the review drove it by hand: with `BASE` off-sheet the measured
difference is 4, the code predicts 4, and round 1's two-clause SENTENCE predicts
5. **So the code was already right about a case the published sentence was
already wrong about.**

**THE RULE's SCOPE, AND THE FALSIFIER - AND THAT A FALSIFIER EXISTS IS A GOOD
RESULT RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** Round 1's form could not be refuted at all; this
one can, **and the review found the circuit where it fails.** The condition: **a
circuit that declares a BUS block touched by a non-rail net that also reaches a
non-bus block.** `edgeCensus` drops `rendering.kind === "bus"` blocks from BOTH
sides while their units keep their own block ids, so such a net costs a boundary
terminal on both sides and cancels - while `crossingNonRailNets` still counts it.

`[RELAYED]` **The review re-declared `tp-leg-upper` as a bus block and changed
nothing else:** baseline blocked 53 edges / flat 48 / difference 5, predicted 5,
AGREES; with the bus block, **blocked 48 / flat 44 / difference 4, predicted 5,
DISAGREES.** These are the review's driven figures and this writer did not
re-execute them. `kind: "bus"` is a real authoring option - declared at
`lib/schgen/ir/types.ts:145`, validated at `lib/schgen/ir/validate.ts:89`,
rendered by `lib/schgen/render/bus.ts` - so this is a reachable declaration and
not a hand-built object.

**SO THE SCOPE IS: the prediction holds for a circuit with no bus block, which is
all four of this repository's.** `[RAN]` Measured here - `opamp-buffer` 1 block,
`optical-compressor` 3, `pt2399-core` 1, `transistor-preamp` 7, **every one of
the twelve `auto` and zero `bus`** - and asserted in
`tests/schgen/remeasure-edges.test.ts`, so a circuit that starts declaring one
turns that check red rather than letting the prediction quietly go wrong. **No
figure published in this entry is affected**, because no subject measured has a
bus block.

**WHETHER `edgeCensus`'s BUS HANDLING IS ITSELF A DEFECT IS UNDETERMINED, AND IT
IS RECORDED AS UNDETERMINED RATHER THAN GUESSED.** Dropping a bus block from both
sides while its units keep their own block ids is **at least an inconsistency**:
the census excludes the block from the comparison and `blockOfPin` still reports
its units as living in it, which is what makes a net touching it look like a
crossing to one half of the machinery and not to the other. **Which end is wrong
is not a fix round's call** - the census could exclude those units from the
crossing count, or the rule's scope could simply exclude bus-declaring circuits,
and those two disagree about what the measurement is of. **What would settle it:
a circuit in this repository that declares a bus block, so the question has a
real subject** - `pt2399-core` is the candidate its own authoring file discusses
and declines, for the reason **G160** records (declaring `bus` means authoring bus
groups for nineteen non-rail nets, *"choosing a grouping this task has no
criterion for"*). **MECHANISMS, both untried and they are alternatives rather
than a plan:** have `edgeCensus` re-key a dropped bus block's units the way
`flatSubgraphOf` re-keys the flat probe's, which makes the two halves agree; or
leave the census alone and narrow the rule's stated scope, which is what this
entry does today. **Nothing here chooses, and `edgeCensus` is byte-identical.**

**WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT TOUCHED, SAID EXACTLY, because fix round 2 reported
`crossingNonRailNets` as untouched and that was not literally true.** `edgeCensus`
is byte-identical and the bus prediction it feeds is still 5 against a measured 4,
so the falsifier above is live. **`crossingNonRailNets` WAS rewritten** - to
delegate to a shared `crossingNets` helper so that `governingNetsOf` could reuse
it - and that refactor **silently changed its sort from the default
`Array.sort()` to a `localeCompare` comparator nothing had asked for.** Membership
and every published list were unaffected, which is why it passed; but both lists
are compared with `toEqual` and the two orders differ (`["AB", "A_B"]` orders one
way under each), so it was a latent behaviour change riding in a refactor. **Fix
round 3 reverted the sort** and `tests/schgen/remeasure-edges.test.ts` pins the
order - **but see G236: round 3's pin could not catch the comparator it named**,
because both published lists are fixed points of both orders. The check that does
catch it is a fixture, added at fix round 5.

**WHAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE IR RATHER THAN AN OUTCOME, stated plainly because it
is the load-bearing half.** That a cross-block net is ALWAYS labelled, and
therefore always gains a boundary node in each block it touches, is
`classify.ts:47` and not a measurement. **The edge addition is therefore a
consequence of this generator's labelling rule, not of decomposition as such** -
and that is a sharper statement than round 1's, because it names the mechanism
that produces the result instead of a set that cannot exist.

**ONE SUPERSEDED READING IS KEPT AS A NAMED SUBJECT, AND IT IS NOT A BASELINE.**
`BoundarySource = "declared-blocks"` reproduces round 1's figure - 46 nodes / 72
edges and 39 / 53, exactly the blocked totals, **1.000x** - and it is retained
because it isolates one quantity exactly: whether a boundary node replaces the
chain edge a split removes. It does, to the edge. **Nothing may quote it as a
flat baseline**, and the node counts are what give the artefact away: 46 against
the flat 43, and 39 against 34, differing by exactly the governing set's size.

**THE ABSOLUTES 139 AND 96 ARE NOT COMPARED AGAINST 69 AND 72.** The spike's edge
count came out of `netlistsvg`'s converter and nothing establishes that it builds
a net's edges the way `graph.ts` does. **What is the same CLAIM is the ratio**,
and the ratio is **0.958x on `optical-compressor` and 0.906x on
`transistor-preamp` - on the wrong side of 1 for the spike's mechanism.**

**AND THE 6.1x ITSELF IS NOT RE-DERIVABLE, which is controller ruling R38.** All
three `oc-*` blocks are refused by the post-layout gates, so there is no composed
side for this circuit at all; `oc-power` fails `checkLayout`, `oc-audio` fails
the snap-collapse obligation and `oc-sidechain` fails the port-coordinate
obligation. **The 6.1x is reported NOT-COMPARABLE and was not approximated,
scaled, or turned into a fraction against another circuit.** What was measured
instead, on the five blocks that do draw, is in **G105**.

**ONE PART OF THIS ENTRY IS UNAFFECTED AND WORTH SAYING SO:** the per-block
crossing figures it quotes for `oc-power`, `oc-audio` and `oc-sidechain` - 0, 28
and 20 - were re-taken and come out **1, 5 and 7** on this backend, at the
`backend-output` stage. The direction is favourable on two of the three and
unfavourable on the smallest, and none of the three is a drawing.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §4, 2026-10-19. **Mechanism
  re-taken** 2026-10-20, Task 17 Step 3.
- **Evidence** both parents emitted through the same machine-extracted converter
  as the blocks, with **15 of 15** of the first spike's whole-circuit inputs

  changed no behaviour, and a partition check passing 54 of 54 and failing 54 of

  better than its blocks, and under one policy one block does score worse than
  its parent. **For the corrected re-take:**
  `tests/schgen/remeasure-edges.test.ts` asserts both circuits' flat and blocked
  counts, the DIRECTION (`ratio < 1`, which is the half round 1 got backwards),
  the governing net lists by name, and **the prediction against the measurement**
  on three subjects - two where it predicts a difference and one where it

  exactly how round 1's version passed; and the fix itself is driven - the same

- **Verified** RELAYED for the spike's own table. **CONFIRMED for the corrected
  edge census and for the three re-taken per-block crossing figures** - this
  writer re-measured 69 and 48 independently after the review reported them and
  **agrees to the edge on both circuits**, including the two governing net lists.
  **The defect in round 1's probe was found by the review, not here**, and the
  correction is this writer's.
- **Why it is open** it is a measurement, not a defect. **It was the strongest
  evidence in the repository for the architecture's block seam, and the
  re-measurement weakens it**: the headline ratio is not re-derivable on this

- **What would settle it** nothing. **A caution instead, now three times over.**
  These are blocks in ISOLATION, each on its own canvas; **the totals add
  crossings across three sheets, and a mechanism that put them on one sheet would

  measurement supports. **AND THE EDGE ADDITION IS SPECIFIC TO THIS GENERATOR's
  LABELLING RULE** - `lib/schgen/ir/classify.ts:47`, which labels every
  multi-block net - rather than to decomposition in general. That is the one
  place a later reader is most likely to over-generalise, and it is also an
  OBSERVATION this task does not resolve: **whether labelling every multi-block
  net is right for the generator is a design question, not a defect**, and
  nothing here changes `classify.ts`. **What would settle THAT: a stated reason
  why a net crossing a block boundary needs a label in every block it touches,
  or a measurement of what is lost if it does not.** Neither exists.

### G101 - block size has a CEILING near 9 parts and, under the tested frontend, an interface cost that dominates a very small block

> **CAVEAT ADDED 2026-10-19, AND THE REASON IT WAS MISSING IS ITSELF THE
> FINDING. BOTH FIGURES BELOW WERE MEASURED THROUGH A FRONT END THE GENERATOR
> WILL NOT USE.** Both spikes drove ELK through `netlistsvg` at `d3518f1` with
> its pinned elkjs 0.7.1; the M1 plan's backend replaces that code path
> entirely. So:
>
> - **the ceiling's SHAPE survives and the number nine does not.** The shape -
>   crossings are zero up to some size then grow, and below that size the count
>   stops moving when the source file is reordered - rests on comparisons taken
>   under identical conditions on both sides, so a skin that inflates crossings
>   inflates both. The number is read off crossing counts that depend on node
>   sizes and on the port constraints the skin declared;
> - **the floor is ENTIRELY the skin's and is UNMEASURED for the new backend,
>   not 4.** `[CODE]` A port became a drawn cell only because `netlistsvg`
>   emits a 30x20 `inputExt` glyph for it. A backend that emits no port glyph
>   has a different floor, or none. The earlier reading that *"a floor exists
>   however the boundary is drawn"* is an argument, not a measurement.
>
> **HOW THIS CAVEAT CAME TO BE MISSING, recorded because it is a register
> failure and not only a measurement caveat.** The contamination was found on
> 2026-10-19 and scoped in the child spec and the M1 plan **in a change that
> touched neither this file nor this entry** (`1dad94b`, *"The skin
> contamination is scoped rather than re-measured"*, two files). **So for a day
> the spec said the floor was unmeasured while this register still presented it
> as a measured 4** - and the child spec's revision 4 then asserted that this
> entry *"holds them with their caveats"*, which was checked and was not true.
> **A caveat recorded in a design document and not in the register is not
> recorded**, which is this file's own opening rule pointed at itself. What
> survives unchanged is the finding's portable half: **block granularity trades
> internal routing complexity against interface complexity**, which depends on
> neither number.

`[RAN]` `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §9
and §7, over 18 declared blocks of 1 to 28 parts.

**THE CEILING, from two independent measures that agree.**

- **Inter-net crossings are ZERO on every block of 8 parts or fewer**, then 4, 5,
  14, 16, 20, 28, 37 - and 293 on the 37-part parent.
- **Crossing count is invariant under declaration-order shuffling at 9 cells and
  moves 22-29 at 13** (G95).

**So below about nine parts a block's measured quality is a property of the
BLOCK, and above it the measure is partly a property of the order somebody typed
the components in.** It is **not** the size at which drawings become good:
`leg-upper` at three parts has zero crossings, a congruent layout and three
legibility defects a reader trips on.

**THE FLOOR, and it is the price of a fine cut.** A declared port is not free
annotation - `[CODE]` netlistsvg emits it as a 30x20 `inputExt` CELL and ELK
lays it out like any other node.

| block | parts | port glyphs as share of cells | bends/edge, port edges | bends/edge, internal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standin-mid` | 1 | **0.67** | 1.00 | - |
| `standin-low-boost` | 2 | **0.60** | 1.50 | - |
| `oc-power` | 8 | 0.33 | 2.71 | 2.67 |
| `pultec-low-cut` | 9 | 0.18 | **3.12** | 2.12 |
| `pultec-hi-cut` | 13 | 0.13 | **2.91** | 2.27 |
| `pultec-mid` | 28 | 0.10 | 2.00 | 1.75 |

**Port glyphs are 10-67 % of a block's cells, a 1-part block's drawing is
two-thirds boundary, and the boundary is the bendy part**: port edges carry more
bends per edge than internal edges on **every one of the 8 blocks of 8 parts or
more** and on the parent, by up to 1.5x. Of the seven smaller blocks with both
kinds of edge, five are equal and one is lower.

**THE TWO BOUNDS ARE CLOSE TOGETHER, and that is the finding.** The size at
which a block draws predictably is near the size at which the drawing is mostly
boundary. **Cutting finer trades crossings for boundary**, and a third cost
comes with it: `[RAN]` labels running past the right-hand canvas edge affect **26
of 53 block drawings against 5 of 14 whole-circuit drawings** (worst overflow
13 px), because the canvas shrinks with the block and the component ids do not.

**One check that could have failed and did not:** across the 18 blocks there are
20 single-pin nets and **every one is a declared port, zero undeclared**. A block
cut by `include()`, by `OWNERSHIP` or by a stand-in's `boundary` does not leave a
net hanging that its declaration does not name.

**BOTH BOUNDS RE-DERIVED 2026-10-20 BY TASK 17, AND THE DECISION IS WRITTEN.**
`tools/schgen/remeasure.ts`'s `BLOCK_SIZE`, with
`docs/schematic/m1-remeasurement.md` as the working:

```
ceiling: 3           placements, measured on this backend
floor:   "unmeasured"
```

**THE CEILING IS 3 AND NOT 9, AND BOTH OF THIS ENTRY'S TWO INDEPENDENT MEASURES
AGREE ON IT - as they did at 9.** `[RAN]`

- **crossings are zero at 2 and 3 placements and non-zero from 8 up.** The
  spike's *"zero on every block of 8 parts or fewer"* FAILS on `oc-power`, the
  same 8-part block, at **1** crossing in declaration order;
- **the crossing count is invariant under declaration reordering at 2 and 3 and
  moves at 8 and every larger size measured** - `oc-power` 1, 3, 2, 2 against the
  spike's 0, 0, 0, 0 on the same block. **G95** carries the full sweep.

**Sizes 4 to 7 have no declared subject and are unmeasured**, so 3 is the largest
size where invariance was MEASURED rather than the largest where it might hold.
Of the spike's seven sweep sizes, **five have no declared subject in this
repository at all** and ruling **R40** forbids constructing one.

**THE FLOOR IS UNMEASURED BECAUSE THE QUANTITY DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS BACKEND.**
`[RAN]` **All 38 boundary nodes of all 12 declared ELK blocks have width 0 and
height 0.** The worst port-glyph share is `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` at **66.7 %**
of graph cells. **That falls inside the spikes' published 10-67 %, and a RANGE
OVERLAP is all that is: no per-block share was compared against any spike row, so
nothing here is a reproduction verdict.** The spike's own per-block shares are for
blocks this repository does not declare - `standin-mid` at 0.67, `pultec-low-cut`
at 0.18, `pultec-mid` at 0.10 - so there is no row-to-row comparison to make. What
the overlap does establish is that the share is the same ORDER of quantity on both
frontends;
**but a block whose cells are two-thirds boundary has a drawing with no boundary
AREA at all.** The share is the interface cost's size in the graph ELK solves,
which is the relationship §1.8 revision 4 says to name, and **nothing measured
here finds a floor.** The earlier *"a floor exists however the boundary is
drawn"* remains an argument rather than a measurement.

**AND THE TWO BOUNDS ARE NO LONGER CLOSE TOGETHER, WHICH WAS THIS ENTRY'S OWN
FINDING.** *"The size at which a block draws predictably is near the size at
which the drawing is mostly boundary"* rested on a ceiling of 9 against a floor
of 4. **There is no floor to be near.** What a small block still costs is §1.6's
cross-sheet mechanism - one glyph per crossing net, drawn at the block's own
anchor and therefore inside its own extent (**G208**) - and that cost is glyphs
and eye-travel rather than ink. **The third cost this entry names, labels
overflowing the canvas edge, was not re-measured** and is not claimed either way.

**WHICH COST IS BEING PAID: THE CEILING's, on 7 of the 12 declared blocks.** Above
the ceiling the measured quality is not a property of the circuit - the crossing
count moves with declaration order by up to **3.0x** (`oc-power`, 1 to 3; the
largest absolute swing is `pt-core`'s 39 to 78) - so §3.3's four measures over
`ob-buffer`, `oc-power`, `oc-audio`, `oc-sidechain`, `pt-core` and `tp-stage` are
partly measurements of a serialization. **`BLOCK_SIZE` REFUSES NOTHING** (plan
decision **D1**): `blocksOutside` names those six and the generator still draws
them.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §9, §7 and §2.1, 2026-10-19.
  **Both bounds re-derived** 2026-10-20, Task 17 Step 5; **the decision written**
  at Step 9.
- **Evidence** the 18-block table, the shuffle comparison, and the port-edge
  split computed from each input's own `ports` declaration. Checks that could

- **Why it is open** it is a measurement that constrains a decision nobody has

- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a block-size decision names both bounds
  and says which cost it is paying** - above the ceiling the measured quality is

  **THAT CRITERION IS NOW MET**: `BLOCK_SIZE` names a measured ceiling of 3, a
  floor of `"unmeasured"`, and the ceiling's cost on 7 of 12 blocks.
  **CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE FIGURE, now in both directions.** The

  of the pipeline's accepted output: 7 of the 12 subjects are layouts the gates

### G102 - three harness checks in the ELK spikes could not have failed on the fixtures they were built against, and one of them had never drawn the part it was wrong about

`[RAN]` `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §0
reports three defects in spike harnesses, and **the general form is what earns
an entry: a check or a converter that cannot be exercised by its own fixtures
looks exactly like a correct one.** All three were found by widening the
fixtures or by reading the code, never by a failing run.

**1. A converter bug that had never fired.** The first spike's converter maps a
diode's pins to the skin ids `A`/`B`. A scan of netlistsvg's own
`lib/analog.svg` skin - in that checkout, not in this repository - prints
`diode_v | alias: d_v | pids: +,-`; **`A`/`B` belong to the resistor, capacitor,
inductor and crystal templates.** **None of the first spike's five circuits
contains a diode**, so the bug was invisible and nothing that spike measured
could have caught it. Two blocks in the second spike do, and ELK refuses the
input outright: `JsonImportException: Referenced shape does not exist:
reverse_polarity_diode.A`. **Until the second spike, this repository's ELK
evidence had never drawn a diode.**

**2. A mutation arm too weak to prove the check it guards, in BOTH spikes.** The
partition check compares net CONTENTS ignoring net NAMES. Its mutation moved one
pin to a FRESH net - and on a small block that leaves the multiset of groups
unchanged, so **27 of 54 mutated rows still reported SAME**. Merging the pin onto
an EXISTING net instead gives **54 of 54 DIFFERENT**. **A pin moved to a
brand-new net is invisible to this check in both spikes**, and that check is the
evidence G99 rests on.

**3. A measurement column that reports 0 because it cannot report anything
else.** `[CODE]` `measure.py`'s `labels_past_right_edge` compares a `<text>`'s
LOCAL `x` against the absolute canvas width and reports **0 on all 56 drawings**.
`[RAN]` No recorded figure rests on it - the first spike's "5 of 15" came from
`labels.py`, which accumulates the transform, and a re-implementation reproduces
**5 of 14** on that spike's own outputs. **A dead column beside live ones reads
as a clean result**, which is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` names: a skipped check
must never look like a passing one.

**Why this is not scratch-harness trivia.** Both harnesses are throwaway and
uncommitted and a bug in one is not evidence about ELK - but **the measurements
they produced are now in this register** (G94 through G101), and the three
defects say what those measurements' blind spots are. **The pattern is also the
G85 pattern arriving a layer earlier**: a check grown against one fixture set has
the shape of that set, so a new input class is the condition that exposes it.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §0, H1, H2 and H4, 2026-10-19.
- **Evidence** the skin scan printing the diode's real pids, ELK's own refusal
  message on an unpatched diode block, the 27-of-54 against 54-of-54 mutation
  comparison, and the `overflow.py` re-implementation reproducing the first
  spike's recorded 5. **A check that could have failed: the patched converter
  regenerates all 15 of the first spike's inputs byte-identical**, which is what
  establishes the diode patch is inert on everything measured before it.
- **Verified** RELAYED.
- **Why it is open** the harnesses are uncommitted scratch, so there is nothing
  here to fix. **It is recorded because the next agent to build a converter or a
  measurement harness for this work will reach for the same fixtures**, and
  because G99's evidence has a stated blind spot now.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a harness check is exercised by a
  fixture that makes it fail, and a fixture set that cannot exercise a code path
  is reported as not exercising it rather than as passing.** For a converter:
  **every component kind it can emit is drawn by at least one fixture** - the
  diode bug needed only that. **MECHANISM, untested:** a per-kind coverage count
  printed beside the partition check's result.

### G103 - ELK emitted one non-axis-aligned wire segment, where two earlier passes recorded zero on every drawing

`[RAN]` `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §2.
The first spike measured **0 non-axis-aligned segments on every one of 14
drawings**, and the second measured 0 on every one of **53 block drawings**. On
the parent `WHOLE-optical-compressor__v-bare` there is **one**: a segment from
(1770, 472) to (2290, 682) on `net_22`, carrying exactly
`sidechain_led_sense_resistor.B` and `sidechain_vactrol_led.-`.

**Why this matters at all: a schematic is orthogonal by convention**, so a
diagonal is not a cosmetic defect in a KiCad emitter - it is geometry the
realization contract has no rule for. **67 of 67 drawings were clean and one was
not, which is the difference between an invariant and a tendency.**

**THE ATTRIBUTION IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS, and the spike says so.** That net
ends on a **diode**, and the diode symbol mapping is exactly the converter patch
G102 records - so the segment may be an artifact of a one-line harness patch
rather than ELK behaviour. Against that: `oc-power` and `oc-sidechain` both draw
diodes with zero diagonals.

- **Found** `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §2, 2026-10-19.
- **Evidence** a segment-angle classifier run over 67 drawings, after the first
  spike's version of it was corrected for counting zero-length segments as
  diagonals; it returns 0 on 66 and names the coordinates and the net on the
  one.
- **Verified** RELAYED.
- **Why it is open** undiagnosed. **It is recorded undiagnosed rather than
  omitted**, because an invariant that holds 66 times and fails once is the kind
  of thing a later reader must not re-establish from scratch.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: whether ELK can emit a non-axis-aligned
  segment at all is answered, not assumed** - the realization contract (spec
  §1.4) needs a rule either way, and "it never happens" is currently a 66-of-67
  claim. **MECHANISM, untested:** re-run that one parent with the diode mapped to
  its correct pids and with the diode removed, which would separate ELK from the
  patch.

### G105 - the 6.1x block-decomposition gain is an UPPER BOUND, because 43 of the 139 edges became block-interface connections that nothing has drawn yet

**The number this program's schematic architecture rests on hardest is
`docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md` §4's paired control, registered as G100:**
the same 37-part `optical-compressor` at `v-bare` gives **293 inter-net crossings
drawn whole and 48 drawn as its three declared blocks** - 6.1x - with wire length
159 967 against 35 070.

**THE MECHANISM G100 STATES IS WHERE THE PROBLEM IS, NOT A SEPARATE CLAIM.** The
gain is explained by the blocks carrying **fewer edges than the whole: 96 against
139.** A second independent review of the child spec asked the obvious question
nobody had: **where did the other 43 edges go?**

**They did not stop existing. They became connections BETWEEN blocks** - which is
what decomposition does, and is legitimate - **and nothing in the measurement or
in the spec represented them.** Each block was drawn on **its own canvas**, so the
43 edges were drawn nowhere at all and counted as removed.

**The spike said so itself, before the review asked**, `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md`
§11, verbatim:

> *"Seam B, and how block drawings would be composed onto one sheet. Each block
> was drawn on its own canvas. The totals in §4 add up crossings across three
> sheets; **a mechanism that put them on one sheet would add its own.**"*

**So 6.1x BOUNDS the improvement from above. Composition can only spend it
down**, and a reader quoting 6.1x without that sentence is quoting a bound as a
result. **A result below 1x after composition is possible** and would be a
finding about seam B rather than a failure of the measurement.

> **THE FOOTER BELOW IS THE ORIGINAL 2026-10-19 ONE AND IT PRE-DATES THE
> RE-TAKE. DO NOT STOP HERE: the entry continues, the premise it rests on has
> been measured false on this backend, and the second footer at the end of the
> entry is the current one.** It is kept rather than deleted because it records
> who found the gap and on what evidence, which the re-take does not supersede -
> but a reader who left at this line would leave believing 43 edges went missing.

- **Found** 2026-10-19, in a second third-party review of
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-schematic-authoring-design.md`, recorded as

  in the spike** and had not been joined to the headline figure anywhere.
- **Evidence** G100's own edge counts (96 against 139) and the block spike's §11,

  was computed from the two edge counts the spike reports rather than asserted -
  if the blocks had carried the same edge count as the whole, the review's
  question would have had no subject and the 6.1x would have been a routing
  result rather than a decomposition one.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - the controller read §4's table and §11's limitation
  list in the spike, and quoted §11 rather than paraphrasing it.

**THE RE-TAKE IS BELOW AND IT CHANGES THE PREMISE, NOT ONLY THE FIGURE.** Read on
before quoting anything above.
**THE INTEGRATED MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN 2026-10-20 BY TASK 17, ON A MUCH NARROWER
SUBJECT, AND THE 43 EDGES TURN OUT NOT TO EXIST ON THIS BACKEND.** Two separate
results, and they must not be read as one:

**1. There are no missing edges - there are ADDED ones.** `[RAN]` **G100**'s

property of `netlistsvg`'s edge model and not of this generator's.** Here every
boundary net is represented in every block's graph, and representing it costs an
edge per block rather than saving one.
