  mechanism proposed is measured above as unwritable - `rail-row` never crowds a
  field at any value length, so the test could not have failed.

### G164 - the obstacle matrix's `FRAME_DERIVED` reason named the wrong function for four tasks, and the arrival alarm is what found it: there are TWO `drawnBoxes` and nothing sizes a frame from the one eleven cells cited

`tests/schgen/render/obstacle-matrix.test.ts`'s absence alarm fired on the
commit that ported `render/frames.ts` and `render/sheet-check.ts`, naming both:

```
error: these have ported, so every cell whose reason names them (the FRAME_DERIVED and within-one-block cells of obstacle-pairs-*.ts) must be re-read against the real code and NOT_IN_THIS_TREE updated in the same change
- []
+ [
+   "frames.ts",
+   "sheet-check.ts",
+ ]
```

**Both rows rang, which is the first time G132's `portedAs` fix has caught a
real arrival** - `sheet-check.ts` is the kebab-case spelling the old guard could
not see.

**THE RE-READ CHANGED THE REASON RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT.** `FRAME_DERIVED`
said: *"`drawnBoxes` (lib/schgen/render/drawn-extent.ts) returns every box a
block layout draws — `scene.texts`, `scene.bodies`, `scene.pinTexts` and the
bounding boxes of `scene.segments` — and `boundsOf` unions them, and that union
is what a frame is sized from."* **Nothing sizes a frame from that function.**
`render/frames.ts` declares a SECOND, private `drawnBoxes(symbols, parts)`, and
the two do not return the same thing:

| function | unions |
|---|---|
| `drawn-extent.ts`'s `drawnBoxes(g, layout)` | `scene.texts`, `scene.bodies`, `scene.pinTexts`, and segment bounding boxes |
| **`frames.ts`'s private `drawnBoxes(symbols, parts)`** | **`scene.texts` and `scene.bodies` only** |

What a frame is actually sized from is `blockContent`'s own union: the placed
`LibSymbol.boxes` of every placement, every wire END as a degenerate box, and
that second `drawnBoxes`. So **`pinTexts`, `strokes` and `crosses` are in no
extent any frame is sized from** - and three cells said in so many words that
they were (`pin-number`/`frame-border` and `pin-name`/`frame-border` cited
`scene.pinTexts`; `frame-border`/`no-connect-marker` cited it as *"where a
no-connect marker's box is"*). Two more (`wire`/`frame-border`,
`pin-line`/`frame-border`) cited `scene.segments`, which is the other function's
route.

**THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES, BY A DIFFERENT AND STRONGER ARGUMENT.** `frameSize`
grows the content extent by `4 * GRID` and `contentOffset` insets the content by
`2 * GRID`, so every frame is clear by **at least 2.54 mm on all four sides**
(more at the top, by the title band). Measured against that margin, each
un-unioned category is bounded by geometry the union DOES cover:

| category | how far it reaches past something unioned | against 2.54 mm |
|---|---|---|
| pin number / offset-0 pin name | 1.905 mm either side of the pin line (`unitText`'s `along(tip, dx, dy, p.length, (3 * GRID) / 2)`) | inside |
| no-connect marker | 0.635 mm around a pin end (`at ± GRID / 2`) | inside |
| DNP cross | at most 0.762 mm past its own body, on a pin-free axis (`CROSS_BOUND`) | inside |
| interior graphic (`strokes`) | nothing - `LibSymbol.boxes` is `unitBoxes`, graphics plus both pin ends | inside |

**THIS SETTLES THE CELL ROUND 1 RECORDED AS UNCOVERED.**
`frame-border`/`dnp-cross` said *"the two reasons' escape clauses meet in
exactly the uncovered case, and that is why this cell is the thinnest of the
frame row"* - no `drawnBoxes` unions `scene.crosses`, and a cross overhangs by
0.762 mm. The first half is still true; the conclusion is not, because 0.762 mm
is inside a 2.54 mm margin. **That is the one place where the arrival made a
cell stronger rather than merely re-worded**, and it is the kind of result the
alarm exists to produce.

**TWO MORE REASONS WERE FALSIFIED BY `sheet-check.ts`, AND ONE OF THEM AT ITS
CONCLUSION.**

1. `NO_FLAG_PRODUCER` opened *"NOTHING IN THIS TREE PRODUCES A `flag: true`
   PowerSymbol"*, naming `render/frames.ts` as the absent producer. That module
   has landed and `flagsContent` is that producer: per flagged rail it emits the
   rail's own symbol and a PWR_FLAG **at the same point**, and `layoutSheet`
   carries both into the sheet's `powers`. The sentence is **deleted**, not
   softened. What survives is narrower and still load-bearing: **no BLOCK anchor
   ever becomes a flag**, because `anchorsToSymbols` hard-codes `flag: false`
   and so does `anchorExtent`'s measurement-only symbol. Task 7 falsified this
   constant's ENUMERATION (**G134**); Task 6b falsified its CONCLUSION, which is
   the reverse.
2. The `pin-line`/`pwr-flag-glyph` cell said *"no flag reaches a
   `ClearanceScene` here yet."* One does now: `sheet-check.ts`'s `clearance`
   passes `[...scene.powers, ...scene.labels]` as `ClearanceScene.anchors`, a
   `PowerSymbol` satisfies `AnchorPoint` structurally, and
   `sceneClearanceProblems` never reads `flag`. The check is live; it has never
   fired, because a flag lives alone in the flags frame with no placement beside
   it.
3. The `body`/`body` cell's *"the sheet-level caller that would compare them
   (`render/sheetCheck.ts`) is not in this tree"* is now about WHICH check
   catches the cross-block case rather than about a gap: `bodyOverlaps` places
   every block's `LibSymbol.boxes` in sheet coordinates and runs `boxesOverlap`
   over all pairs across blocks.

**WHAT WAS DONE WITH THE TWO ROWS, and it is not a deletion to make a test
pass.** Both moved into `SETTLED_ARRIVALS`, which asserts each module is
**PRESENT** - the same move Task 7 made for `blocks.ts` and `templates`
(**G134**). `NOT_IN_THIS_TREE` is now empty, and the test that iterated it is
**inverted rather than removed**: it asserts the list IS empty and says that a
later row must carry `portedAs` and re-arm the arrival filter. A new test
closes **G132**'s first open item for the names that remain: every
`SETTLED_ARRIVALS` key ending in `.ts` must be a basename
`tools/schgen/port-manifest.json` actually writes under `lib/schgen/render/`, so
a key spelt the pedals way makes that test fail instead of making the presence
check unable to fire.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 6b, Step 2, by the alarm firing and then reading
  `$SCHGEN_SOURCE/render/frames.ts` against the cells.
- **Evidence** the alarm's own red output, quoted above, which is a check that
  could have failed and did. The two-`drawnBoxes` finding is a read that could
  have gone the other way:
  `grep -n "drawnBoxes" lib/schgen/render/frames.ts lib/schgen/render/drawn-extent.ts`
  -> a private `function drawnBoxes(symbols: SymbolResolver, parts: SceneParts)`
  in the first returning `[...scene.texts, ...scene.bodies].map((n) => n.box)`,
  and an exported `drawnBoxes(g, layout)` in the second returning
  `[...scene.texts, ...scene.bodies, ...scene.pinTexts].map(...).concat(segments)`.
  Had `blockContent` called the exported one, eleven cells would have needed no
  change. The margin arithmetic is over `frameSize` and `contentOffset` as
  landed: content `minX` maps to `at.x + 2 * GRID + (minX - gridFloor(minX))`
  and frame `maxX` to `at.x + gridCeil(maxX) - gridFloor(minX) + 4 * GRID`, so
  both horizontal clearances are `>= 2 * GRID`; vertically the top adds
  `bandHeight` as well. The matrix test is **10 pass / 0 fail / 71 expect()
  calls** after the re-read, with the cited-identifier pin moved 91 -> 102 and
  `namesOffset` classified as a `PinTextStyle` field.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer drove the alarm red, read both
  `drawnBoxes` definitions and `frameSize`/`contentOffset` directly, and ran the
  re-read matrix test.
- **Why it is open** the margin argument is arithmetic over source, not a test:
  it is the same standing of evidence **G125** records for 95 of the 105 cells,
  and nothing in the tree fails if `frameSize` stops adding `4 * GRID`.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION:** a check fails when a frame stops
  leaving `2 * GRID` of clearance around its content, so the eleven cells'
  reason rests on something that can break rather than on a reading.
  **MECHANISM**, untried: a test over `frameSize`/`contentOffset`/`frameAt`
  asserting that for a given `FrameContent` the placed content box is inset by
  at least `2 * GRID` on all four sides - note that `render/frames.test.ts` is a
  ported file and this would be a hand-written sibling, so **G123**'s cost
  (nothing byte-checks a hand-written test) applies to it.

### G165 - the first schematic this repository has emitted through its own pipeline, looked at: the frame-title collision is gone, both whole-sheet guards ran clean on a frame-bearing scene, and one of them has a blind spot the perturbation found

**G131** and **G136** both end on the same sentence - *"nothing in this repository has yet
emitted a generated schematic through its own pipeline"*. It has now. `generate` built the ported
`mini` fixture, `writeGeneration` wrote it, `exportPdf` drove `kicad-cli` 10.0.5, and the three
pages were converted at 170 dpi and read.

**WHY THE DESIGN IS A PORT AND NOT ONE WRITTEN HERE.** The fixture is
`digital-pedal-platform`'s own `__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts`, ported and declared diverged.
An agent may never author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it produces, and *"look at it
and say whether it is any good"* is such a criterion - so the arrangement being judged is one this
repository did not choose. Every position in the pictures below comes from `layoutSheet` and the
templates; nothing was nudged.

**WHAT CAME OUT, measured by `layoutSheet` itself:**

| sheet | paper | symbols | wires | power symbols | labels | junctions | no-connects | frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `power` | A4 | 8 | 17 | 13 | 1 | 7 | 0 | 4 |
| `signal` | A3 | 11 | 39 | 12 | 17 | 5 | 3 | 7 |

**WHAT THE POWER SHEET LOOKS LIKE.** Four dashed blue frames in one row across the top of a
landscape A4, each titled in blue inside its own top-left corner.

- **3V3 regulator** - U1 `AMS1117-3.3` as a filled rectangle in the middle, pin 3 `VI` entering
  left, pin 2 `VO` leaving right, pin 1 `GND` dropping out of the bottom with the word GND set
  vertically inside the body. C1 `10u` hangs off the input node down to a ground arrow, C2 `22u`
  off the output node down to another, and U1's own ground pin to a third. The input rail runs
  left into a `VIN` arrow and the output right into a `3V3` arrow, both lying on their sides
  because the anchor is horizontal. Textbook, and exactly what a person would draw.
- **3V3 decoupling** - C3 and C4, both `100n`, side by side between a short top bar carrying a
  `3V3` arrow and a short bottom bar carrying a `GND` arrow. The arrow sits over the LEFT cap
  rather than between them, which looks slightly lopsided and is the row's first tap.
- **VIN sense divider** - R1 `10k` down from a `VIN` arrow to the tap, R2 `10k` from the tap down
  to `GND`, C5 `100n` shunting the tap to the same bottom node, and the tap carried right into a
  `SENSE` global label with `[2,3]` printed beside it - the intersheet page reference, correct:
  SENSE appears on sheets 2 and 3. Junction dots at the tap and at the bottom node.
- **Power flags** - two columns, each a rail symbol and a `PWR_FLAG` pointing the opposite way at
  the same point: `PWR_FLAG` over `GND`, and `VIN` over `PWR_FLAG`. This is `flagsContent`, and
  it is the producer **G164** records as having falsified `NO_FLAG_PRODUCER`.

**WHAT THE SIGNAL SHEET LOOKS LIKE.** Seven frames in one row across a landscape A3.

- **Input connector** - J1 `Conn_01x04` on the RIGHT, four pins fanning LEFT into `VIN`, `SENSE`,
  `SIG_IN`, `GND` labels with their page refs outside them. The connector sits on the right and
  the signals leave to the left, which is the reverse of the usual reading direction; it is what
  `connector-fanout` does with this anchor and it is not wrong, only unexpected.
- **Input buffer** - `SIG_IN` in from the left, R3 `1k`, a node with C6 `1n` shunting to `GND`,
  into U2A `OPA1678` pin 3 (the + input, drawn above the −), the triangle, and pin 1 out to an
  `AMP_OUT` label. The feedback runs from the output down and back to pin 2 as a rectangle under
  the amplifier: a unity-gain buffer, drawn the way one is drawn.
- **Spare op-amp channel** - U2B's triangle alone, all three pins ending in a small ✗. Three
  no-connect markers, which is the sheet's no-connect count exactly.
- **Op-amp supply** - U2C, the package's power unit, as a vertical line with `3V3` above and
  `GND` below. **The frame is 21.6 mm wide and 43.2 mm tall and every text in it is rotated 90°**
  (`V+`, `V−`, `U2C`, `OPA1678` and both rail names read bottom-to-top). It is legible and it is
  the least attractive thing on either sheet: one two-pin unit in a frame taller than every
  other one that holds a single part. (**Round 1 called it "the tallest frame on the page"
  and it is not**: at 21.59 x 43.18 mm it is beaten by the SPI flash frame on the same
  sheet, 54.61 x 55.88 mm, which holds an eight-pin IC and earns its size. The observation
  stands; the superlative was not measured.)
- **Crystal** - Y1 `12MHz` in the middle, `XI` and `XO` labels standing up on either side, C7 and
  C8 `12p` beneath each clock net down to their own grounds, and Y1's shield pins down to a third.
  Symmetric and clean.
- **SPI flash** - U3 `W25X40CLSS`, pins fanning LEFT into `FL_CS`, `FL_CLK`, `FL_DI`, `FL_DO` and
  two `3V3` arrows for `~{WP}` and `~{HOLD}`, VCC up and GND down. **Under the frame title there
  is a second line reading `SPI: FL_CS, FL_DO, FL_DI, FL_CLK`** - the bus renderer's legend,
  printed in the title band. That is the only place in either sheet where a frame carries more
  than its title, and the band grew to fit it.
- **Output connector** - J2 `Conn_01x07`, seven pins fanning left into the four flash nets, `XI`,
  `XO` and `AMP_OUT`.

**The root sheet** is two empty hierarchical boxes titled Power and Signal with their file names
under them. Correct and dull, which is what it should be.

**THE TITLE BLOCK CARRIES THE PROVENANCE, and it is worth seeing in a picture**:
*"KiCad 10.0.5; stock libraries 895cc96749279fdc"* and *"Generated by schgen from
tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts; do not edit"*, on every sheet.

**THE FRAME-TITLE COLLISION IS GONE, WHICH SETTLES G136's ATTRIBUTION (a).** That entry records
the title colliding with the topmost power symbol's text on four of eight scratch-harness
drawings, and argues from the source that the collision belongs to the harness because
`frameSize` reserves a title band and `contentOffset` puts content below it. **Through
`layoutSheet` it does not occur on any of the eleven frames**: every title sits inside its own
frame's top-left with clear space under it, and the one frame with a legend line grew its band to
hold both. The argument from source is now an observation.

**BOTH WHOLE-SHEET GUARDS RAN, FOR THE FIRST TIME, OVER A FRAME-BEARING SCENE - AND THEY ARE
PROVEN LIVE RATHER THAN MERELY SILENT.** `layoutSheet` calls `assertSheetSafe(scene)` and
`assertTextClear(textScene(…, { blocks, powers, labels, texts, frames }))`; **G136**'s caveat (c)
says neither had ever run here. Both accepted both sheets. Driven:

- two blocks of the `power` sheet placed at one origin ->
  `sheet power: wire safety:` / `wire 0 of REG (net GND) ends at (0, 12.7) touching nothing; end
  it on a pin, a label, a power symbol or another wire end`
- a frame slid 20 mm left ->
  `sheet power: text clearance:` / `title of frame "3V3 decoupling" crosses the border of frame
  "3V3 regulator"`

**AND THE PERTURBATION FOUND A BLIND SPOT, which is the part of this entry that is not a
description.** A third probe **shrank a frame to 60% of its width and height and
`assertTextClear` ACCEPTED it.** The reason is in `textProblems`: its frame clause is
`if (boxesOverlap(t.box, f.box) && !strictlyWithin(t.box, f.box))`, so it refuses a text that
STRADDLES a border and says nothing about a text that is entirely OUTSIDE one. A frame too small
for its content does not straddle anything - its content simply sits beside it - and no refusal
fires. **So nothing in the pipeline checks that a frame contains what it was sized from**, which
is the same gap **G164** records from the other direction: the eleven `FRAME_DERIVED` cells rest
on a 2.54 mm margin that no check defends.

**ERC, `runErc(root, "all")`: 0 errors, 2 warnings.** With `"error"`: 0 and 0. Both warnings are
the same `[pin_to_pin]` class - *"Pins of type Bidirectional and Power output are connected"* -
for U3's pin 3 `~{WP}` and pin 7 `~{HOLD}`, strapped to 3V3, which U1 pin 2 drives as a power
output. Strapping a flash's write-protect and hold pins high is correct practice and KiCad warns
about it regardless; **it is a fact about the fixture circuit, not about the generator.**

**AND THE TWO PICTURES G136's GAP (b) NAMES AS MISSING NOW EXIST.** That gap says the eight
template descriptions are *(template × pedals fixture)* and that nobody has seen *(template × this
repository's circuit)*. **G160**'s second column measures that `connector-fanout` draws
`tp-leg-lower-a` and `tp-leg-lower-b` under a probed anchor. Both were put through `layoutSheet`
and exported. **The anchors were not chosen here**: they are read verbatim from
`docs/schematic/template-parity-anchors.md`'s *"the anchors that drew something, verbatim"* table
(`RV3`#1 and `RV4`#1, no roles), which Task 10's brute-force sweep found. Every other block of
`transistor-preamp` keeps Task 9's declaration; the two blocks were put on a sheet of their own
because the other six are `auto` and need the ELK backend, so **this is two blocks of that
circuit and NOT its schematic.** Nothing was written into the repository.

**What they look like.** Two narrow frames side by side, *Lower bias leg A* and *Lower bias leg
B*, each a vertical chain read top to bottom: a `BASE` global label at the top (with its `[2]`
page ref), a `Jumper_2_Open` JP1/JP2, a resistor (`4.7K` / `47K`), and the trimmer (`10K` /
`200K`) with its wiper taken out to the right into a `GND` arrow and its lower end taken down into
a second `GND` arrow. **Six symbols, eight wires, four power symbols, two labels, zero junctions
across the two.** It is a correct and readable bias leg, and two things about it are worth saying
plainly: **the two ground symbols per leg are the same net** (the trimmer is wired as a rheostat -
**G160**'s finding - so its wiper and its end are strapped), where a person would draw one; and
**the `BASE` label and its page ref are rotated 90°**, reading bottom-to-top, because the chain
leaves upward. Neither is wrong. Both are what a reviewer would mention first.

**THE ONE THING BOTH SHEETS DO BADLY, and it is the same on all three drawings: the page is
mostly empty.** `packFrames` shelf-packs left to right and starts a new shelf only when the
current one is full, so eleven small frames sit in a single row across the top and the lower
three-quarters of every page is blank. On the A3 signal sheet the content occupies roughly the top
20% of the height and the full width; on the tp-leg probe, two frames occupy about 3% of an A3.
Nothing is wrong with the drawing - it is just not laid out for the paper it is on.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 6b, Step 6.
- **Evidence** a run, not a reading. `kicadVersion()` -> `10.0.5`; `generate` produced the ten
  files; `exportPdf` drove `kicad-cli sch export pdf --theme schgen`, which refuses a malformed
  `.kicad_sch` rather than drawing it; `pdftoppm -r 170 -png` produced three pages and all three
  were read with the Read tool. The counts above are printed by `layoutSheet`'s own result. The
  ERC figures are `runErc(root, "all")` and `runErc(root, "error")`, and the report's own totals
  line reads ` ** ERC messages: 2  Errors 0  Warnings 2`. The three perturbations each produced
  the output quoted above and were discarded; `git status --porcelain` is clean in this worktree
  and in `digital-pedal-platform`.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer generated, exported, converted and read every page, ran
  the three perturbations, and read the ERC report.
- **Why it is open** the blind spot above is real and unfixed, and the packing observation is a
  result somebody may want to act on.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION, two clauses.** (a) A frame that does not contain the
  content it was sized from fails a check. (b) A sheet whose frames use a small fraction of the
  declared paper is either reported or packed better - **and WHICH of those is right is not an
  implementer's call**, because "better" here is an acceptance criterion for an artifact an agent
  produces. **MECHANISMS, untried.** For (a): give `textProblems`' frame clause the owning frame
  of each text (the `Frame.blockId` is already there) and refuse a text outside its own frame;
  note that this changes a ported module and would need a divergence. For (b): nothing - it needs
  a decision first.
- **ROUND 2 OF TASK 15: clause (a) IS NOT ITS OWN FINDING AND IS SUPERSEDED BY G212**, which
  measures the same missing invariant at two more scales and carries the consolidated criterion.
  Read (a) there; it is left here because this entry's narrative is what found it.

### G166 - perturbed and restored: making `staleFiles` compare mtimes turns two tests red, and the one the brief names reports a hand-edited file with a FRESH mtime as current

`CLAUDE.md`: *"Derived artifacts are regenerated every run and compared by content, never by
timestamp - git does not preserve mtimes, and every mtime accident makes stale look current."*
`staleFiles` in `tools/schgen/generated-files.ts` implements that by reading each generated file
and comparing the text. The Task 6b brief asks for the claim to be driven rather than asserted.

**THE PERTURBATION.** The content comparison

```ts
const onDisk = fs.existsSync(file) ? fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8") : null;
if (onDisk !== g.files.get(name)) out.push(`${name} is stale; ...`);
```

was replaced by a timestamp comparison - stale if the file is missing or older than the design
module:

```ts
const stale = !fs.existsSync(file) || fs.statSync(file).mtimeMs < fs.statSync(d.file).mtimeMs;
if (stale) out.push(`${name} is stale; ...`);
```

**TWO TESTS WENT RED, AND THE FIRST IS EXACTLY THE BRIEF'S CASE - a file with a fresh mtime and
stale content, reported as current:**

```
tests/cli/schgen.test.ts:
180 |     const r = await run(["check", file])
181 |     expect(r.code).toBe(1)
                         ^
error: expect(received).toBe(expected)

Expected: 1
Received: 0

(fail) check against the ported mini design > reports a hand-edited generated file stale by CONTENT, with its mtime newer than the rest
```

That test writes `(kicad_sch (version 20250114))` over a generated `power.kicad_sch` and then sets
its mtime **sixty seconds into the future**, so it is the newest file in the directory. Under the
content comparison `check` exits 1 and names it; under the timestamp comparison `check` exits 0
and the schematic on disk - which is no longer the schematic the model produces - passes.

The second:

```
tests/schgen/emit-byte-stable.test.ts:
105 |     const stale = staleFiles(d, g)
106 |     expect(stale.length, "exactly the one file whose content changed").toBe(1)
                                                                             ^
error: exactly the one file whose content changed

Expected: 1
Received: 0

(fail) writeGeneration is the only writer > reports a file stale when its CONTENT differs, not when its mtime does
```

**AND A THIRD CHECK FIRED THAT WAS NOT THE TARGET**, which is worth recording because it is the
port mechanism catching exactly what it exists to catch: `generated-files.ts` is a PORTED file, so
`tests/schgen/port-fidelity.test.ts`'s byte-check went red naming it -
`error: tools/schgen/generated-files.ts` on *"every ported file is its source, rewritten only by
the manifest"*. **A hand edit to a ported file cannot be made quietly even for a moment.**

**RESTORED by re-running the porter** (`SCHGEN_SOURCE=... bun run tools/schgen/port.ts`), not by
editing the file back - which is the mechanism `lib/schgen/README.md` prescribes and which proves
the restoration is the source rather than this writer's memory of it.
`git status --porcelain tools/schgen/generated-files.ts` is **empty**, the five lines read back
character for character as quoted above, and the three affected files are **27 pass / 0 fail**.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 6b, Step 7.
- **Evidence** the red output quoted verbatim above, and the restoration verified three ways: the
  porter re-ran, `git status --porcelain` on the file is empty, and the suite is green.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer made the edit, ran the tests, read the failures, re-ran the
  porter and re-ran the tests.
- **Why it is open** it is not a defect; it is a property that now has a demonstration behind it,
  recorded so the next person to touch `staleFiles` knows the demonstration exists and what it
  costs to repeat.
- **What would settle it** nothing: this entry is a measurement with no open question. **It is
  deleted by whoever next finds it unhelpful**, and what the deletion takes with it is the
  evidence that the two tests above can actually fail - which is their whole value.

### G167 - the ported refusals tell the reader to run `pnpm`, and this repository uses `bun run`

`initHint` in `tools/schgen/generated-files.ts` returns
`run pnpm schgen generate --init <design> to create it`, and that sentence is what a person sees
the first time they run `bun run schgen check` on a design with no reference lock:

```
/…/out/refs.lock.json not found; run pnpm schgen generate --init tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts to create it
```

**There is no `pnpm` in this repository.** `package.json`'s scripts are run with `bun run`, and
Task 6b added `"schgen": "bun run tools/cli/schgen.ts"` beside the others. So the refusal names a
command that does not work here - and `CLAUDE.md`'s rule is that *"every `throw` names what is
missing, where to fix it, and why it is not defaulted"*, which this one does except for the
package manager.

**It is a ported defect carried on purpose, not an oversight.** `lib/schgen/README.md`: *"a defect
in a ported file is a defect in the source, carried here on purpose, fixed in a task that has a
stated reason to diverge."* Diverging `generated-files.ts` over one word would take the file out
of the byte-check for the rest of the plan, which is the cost **G139** sizes; that trade is not
obviously worth making for a hint string, and it is not an implementer's call to make silently.

**IT IS THREE SITES, NOT ONE, AND THE FIRST COUNT WAS WRONG.** This writer wrote *"the only such
string"* and then ran the grep, which is the order that catches it:
`grep -rn "pnpm" lib/schgen tools/schgen tools/cli` returns **five lines**, of which **three are
messages a user can see** - `generated-files.ts:37` (`initHint`, above),
`generated-files.ts:104` (*"`<file>` is stale; run pnpm schgen generate `<design>`"*, which is
what `check` prints on every stale file and therefore the one seen most often) and
`lib/schgen/lock/version-lock.ts:103` (*"accept it deliberately with pnpm schgen generate
--accept-toolchain"*). The other two are not: `design.ts:76` is a doc comment mentioning
`pnpm typecheck`, and the fifth is inside a `cuts` string in `port-manifest.json`, i.e. text that
is DELETED from the tree. **Two files, three messages**, and one of them is in `lib/schgen/`
rather than `tools/schgen/`, so a fix touches two ported files and not one.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 6b, Step 5, by running the CLI against the fixture design.
- **Evidence** the refusal above, printed by `bun run schgen check
  tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts`, and the grep.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the command and read the output.

- **What would settle it** **CRITERION:** no message a user of this repository can see names

### G168 - measured: nothing in this repository has ever drawn a pin mark or a DNP cross, **G130** rests on code no test executed, and one ported test is the only thing that changes that

**G130** is a measured entry whose entire subject is `dnpCross`'s asymmetric
margin arithmetic - *"the margins are mutating variables that start as the
overhangs, and the asymmetry between them is real"* - and `CROSS_BOUND`, the
obstacle matrix's reason for five cells, is the same arithmetic restated. Both
describe `lib/schgen/render/pin-marks.ts`. **Until Task 6b round 2 no test and
no fixture in this repository executed either `dnpCross` or `pinMarks`' mark
construction.**

**The measurement.** `bun test tests/ --coverage` before round 2:
`lib/schgen/render/pin-marks.ts` at **50.00% of functions and 55% of lines** -
the exported `pinMarkBox` ran, and `pinMarks`' body past its first guard and
the whole of `dnpCross` did not. **The reason is a fixture fact, not a gap in
the pipeline**: `polarIdentities` returns `null` for any part with
`dnp === false`, and the ported `mini` design declares
`dnp: false` on every part (`grep -c "dnp: true"` over it -> **0**). Both sheets
of the first generated schematic report **0 pin marks**, which is correct and is
why a reader of **G165**'s counts should not take them as coverage.

**AND ROUND 1 OF TASK 6b's REPORT SAID THE OPPOSITE BY IMPLICATION.** Its
concern 3 listed `pin-marks.ts` among the modules whose ported test was out and
read as though `layoutSheet` covered it. `layoutSheet` covers `bus.ts` (95.0%),
`sheet-check.ts`, `frames.ts` and `sheets.ts` (100%) - it does not cover this
one, because it draws no DNP part. **G124**'s Task 6b amendment listed coverage
for nine modules and omitted this one.

**WHAT CHANGED IT.** `render/pinMarks.test.ts`, which round 1 classified as
*"nobody's: the renderer is deleted"* on a `realiseLabelled` reference that was
pure scaffolding (**G163**). Diverged with two substitutions this task had
already used elsewhere, every assertion unchanged, it is **6 pass / 0 fail** and
takes `pin-marks.ts` to **100.00% of functions and 100.00% of lines**. One of
its tests asserts `dnpCross`'s exact box -
`{ minX: at.x - 2794, minY: at.y - 1727, maxX: at.x + 2794, maxY: at.y + 1727 }`
for `Fix:D` - which is **G130**'s arithmetic as a check that can fail, and the
only one there has ever been here.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 6b round 2, from the review's C2.
- **Evidence** two coverage runs over the whole suite at two commits, and a grep
  that could have come back non-zero: `grep -c "dnp: true"` over

### G169 - OWNER DECISION, 2026-10-20: KiCad is a dependency, and no path may be unique to one machine

The owner, asked nothing and volunteering it:

> *"treat kicad as a dependency. But make sure there are no hardcoded paths
> unique to this machine. Paths should be configurable with sensible defaults"*

**This closes G119's open question**, which asked whether a vendored symbol's
bytes should be what a drawing reads so that a machine without KiCad could still
draw a wholly-vendored circuit. The answer is no: KiCad is a dependency, so the
consequence G119 recorded and flagged - *"a machine with no KiCad cannot draw at
all"* - is accepted rather than a cost to be engineered away. It is also what
`CLAUDE.md` already said (*"Treat KiCad the way you would a compiler: required,
and not something to engineer around"*), now confirmed by the owner directly
against a specific trade rather than inferred from a general sentence. **The
second half is new and is a requirement, not a confirmation.**

**What the second half binds, measured before the task that fixes it.** This
table is CORRECTED below (see "What Task 10b found that this table missed") -
it undercounted, and its row 7 misattributes a function to the wrong file:

| site | state |
| --- | --- |
| `make/board.mk:44` | `KICAD_CLI ?= /Applications/...`, exported - overridable, macOS-only default |
| `tools/pultec/schematic-sync.ts:92` | `DEFAULT_KICAD_CLI` behind `deps.kicadCli ?? …` - overridable, macOS-only default |
| `tests/circuits/kicad-round-trip.ts:31` | `process.env["KICAD_CLI"] ?? /Applications/...` |
| `tests/kicad/footprint-library.ts:28` | `process.env["KICAD_FOOTPRINTS"] ?? /Applications/...` |
| `tests/kicad/symbol-library-disk.ts:33` | `process.env["KICAD_SYMBOLS"] ?? /Applications/...` |
| `tests/guide/print-pdf.test.ts:30` | `process.env["HTML_TO_PDF"] ?? /Applications/Google Chrome...` |
| `lib/schgen/render/stock-symbols.ts` | **already correct**: `KICAD_SYMBOL_DIR`, then `dirname(KICAD_CLI)/../SharedSupport/symbols`, then `/usr/share/kicad/symbols` |

**So the defect is NOT that paths are unoverridable - every site but one takes
an override already.** It is three narrower things. (1) **The same macOS literal
is duplicated across five sites**, each with its own environment variable, so a
KiCad installed anywhere else needs several variables set and nothing tells a
reader which. (2) **Every default is macOS-only** except `stockSymbolDir()`,
which is the single place that already walks a candidate chain including a Linux
path - it is the pattern to generalise rather than a special case. (3) **The
symbol and footprint roots are written out by hand** instead of being derived
from one resolved install root, so they can disagree with the `kicad-cli` a run
actually uses.

### G170 - the Makefile's sanctioned single literal is EXPORTED, so Task 10b's cross-platform resolver is unreachable through this repository's own primary workflow

Task 10b put every KiCad and browser path behind one resolver with a
per-platform candidate list (**G169**). `make/board.mk` keeps a single macOS
literal as a deliberate, tested carve-out, because Make cannot import
TypeScript - that part is sound and a test holds the two to each other.

**What the carve-out does that nothing recorded: it is `export`ed.**

```
make/board.mk:44   KICAD_CLI ?= /Applications/KiCad/KiCad.app/Contents/MacOS/kicad-cli
make/board.mk:45   export KICAD_CLI
make/board.mk:58   HTML_TO_PDF ?= /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome
make/board.mk:59   export HTML_TO_PDF
```

`make/board.mk` spawns **21** `bun` invocations, every one of which inherits
those variables; and `lib/kicad/netlist.ts` reads
`process.env["KICAD_CLI"] ?? defaultKicadCli()`, checking the environment
**first**. So for anyone who reaches this tooling through `make` rather than by
invoking `bun` directly, **the macOS literal wins unconditionally, on every
platform, and the candidate list never runs.** A Linux or Windows user running
`make check` still gets the macOS path and still has to discover and override
it by hand - **which is precisely the burden G169 exists to remove**, in the
workflow `CLAUDE.md` names as primary: *"`make check` invokes `kicad-cli` on
every board on every run."*

**It is new, and that is why nobody caught it.** Before Task 10b every
TypeScript default WAS the same macOS literal, so the export was a no-op and
the duplication was the only defect. Task 10b put a working cross-platform
resolver underneath an export that silently defeats it.

**The distinction the current contract misses.** `lib/kicad/netlist.ts`'s own
comment says *"an explicitly set `KICAD_CLI` always wins"*, which is the right
contract for a **user's** explicit override. The Makefile's `?=` default is not
that: it is a default **wearing an explicit override's clothes**, because Make
cannot tell the subprocess which of the two it is.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 10b reviewer, which reasoned it out from the
  export and the env-first read rather than observing it on another platform -
  nobody here has a Linux or Windows machine to run it on. Confirmed
  independently by the controller: `grep -n "^export \|?=" make/board.mk`
  returns the four lines above, and `grep -c "bun" make/board.mk` returns 21.
- **Evidence** a check that could have failed, and did not fail the way it
  should: `tests/kicad/install.test.ts`'s Makefile check asserts only that the
  Makefile's literal **agrees with** `defaultKicadCli("darwin")`. It passes, and
  it cannot detect this - it says nothing about whether the resolver is
  **reachable** on a non-darwin `make` invocation. A test that agrees with the
  thing it is meant to guard against is the shape this register exists to catch.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the mechanism, the line numbers and the counts,
  which the controller ran and read. **NOT verified on a non-darwin machine** -
  nobody here has one, which is also why G169's Linux and Windows candidates are
  recorded as unverified.
- **Why it is open** Task 11 was in flight when this was found and touches
  `lib/kicad/netlist.ts`, so dispatching a fix round concurrently would have put
  two implementers in the same files. It is queued for Task 10b's fix round, to
  run once Task 11 lands.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION:** on a machine that is not macOS,
  `make check` resolves `kicad-cli` and the HTML-to-PDF browser through the
  per-platform candidate list, and a user who has set neither variable is not
  handed a macOS path. **MECHANISMS**, both untried and the choice is open.
  (1) Stop exporting, and let each `bun` entry point resolve for itself - which
  costs the Makefile the ability to pass a user's explicit `make KICAD_CLI=...`
  down, unless that case is passed on the command line instead of through the
  environment. (2) Keep the export but make the Makefile's DEFAULT distinguish
  itself from a user's override - for example by exporting only when the
  variable came from the user (`origin` is `command line` or `environment`),
  which GNU Make can test, so an unset variable reaches the resolver untouched.
  **(2) preserves both contracts and is the one to try first**; (1) is simpler
  and loses something real.

**WHAT TASK 10b's FIX ROUND DID (2026-10-20), AND A THIRD CHANNEL NEITHER
MECHANISM ABOVE WOULD HAVE FIXED.** Re-reading `make/board.mk` before changing
it found that `netlist-agrees` and `guide` do not only rely on the export -
`netlist-agrees` (which `check` depends on, for every board declaring
`sch`/`netlist`) runs `bun "$(CLI)" netlist-sync ... --kicad-cli "$(KICAD_CLI)"`,
and `guide` passes `--kicad-cli "$(KICAD_CLI)" --html-to-pdf "$(HTML_TO_PDF)"`
the same way - an EXPLICIT command-line flag, built from the Make VARIABLE's
text, which neither mechanism above touches: mechanism (1) (stop exporting)
only affects what is in a child process's environment, and mechanism (2)
(conditional export) only affects whether the SAME value also reaches the
environment. Both leave `$(KICAD_CLI)` itself computed from the static `?=`
literal when unset, so BOTH would have left `make check`'s actual
`netlist-sync` invocation handing a non-macOS machine the macOS path via this
flag, regardless of either fix. `grep -c "^export \|?="` is the wrong check
for this - `grep -n '\-\-kicad-cli "\$(KICAD_CLI)"\|\-\-html-to-pdf
"\$(HTML_TO_PDF)"' make/board.mk` is, and it returns the two lines above.

**MECHANISM AS IMPLEMENTED, a third option neither (1) nor (2) is**: make the
Make VARIABLE's own value platform-aware, rather than choosing what to do
with a value that is always the macOS literal. `tools/cli/resolved-default.ts`
is a thin bridge - `bun tools/cli/resolved-default.ts kicad-cli` /
`... html-to-pdf` prints `defaultKicadCli()` / `defaultHtmlToPdf()` - the same
role `tools/cli/perfboard.ts board-info --field sch` already plays for
`$(SCH)` four lines above `KICAD_CLI` in this same file. `make/board.mk` now
reads:

```
ifeq ($(origin KICAD_CLI),undefined)
KICAD_CLI := $(shell bun "$(REPO_ROOT)/tools/cli/resolved-default.ts" kicad-cli)
endif
export KICAD_CLI
```

(and the same shape for `HTML_TO_PDF`). `$(origin)` distinguishes "nothing
set this" from "the user set this" - `?=` was dropped rather than kept,
because `?=` creates a recursively-expanded variable and `$(shell ...)` on its
right-hand side would re-run on every reference to `$(KICAD_CLI)` (export,
`netlist-agrees`, `guide`, the help text), not once; `:=` inside the `ifeq`
guard runs the shell-out at most once and only when needed. This fixes BOTH
channels at once - the export (now exporting a correctly-resolved value
rather than a literal) and the explicit `--kicad-cli`/`--html-to-pdf` flags
(now built from that same resolved value) - without touching
`tools/cli/perfboard-netlist-verb.ts` or `tools/cli/perfboard-binary-verbs.ts`,
whose own "no fallback of its own; make/board.mk resolves it" contract is
unchanged.

A `print-%: ; @echo '$($*)'` debug target (the standard GNU Make idiom) was
added so `tests/kicad/install.test.ts` could check the property this entry's
own Evidence line says the old test could not: that an UNSET variable
actually reaches the resolver, by running real `make` rather than parsing
this file's text. **Perturbation, confirming the new tests have teeth**: with
`make/board.mk` temporarily reverted to its pre-fix shape (`git stash`, this
worktree only, restored and dropped immediately after), the two new
reachability tests failed with `make: *** No rule to make target
'print-HTML_TO_PDF'` rather than passing - they cannot pass against the
defect this entry describes. With the fix applied again: `KICAD_CLI` unset ->
`make print-KICAD_CLI` prints `/Applications/KiCad/KiCad.app/Contents/MacOS/kicad-cli`
(this machine's real, existing path, found by `defaultKicadCli()`'s own
candidate search - not the literal, though the two happen to agree on
darwin); `KICAD_CLI=/tmp/...-sentinel` -> prints the sentinel back unchanged.
Also confirmed directly: with `KICAD_CLI` unset, `make -n netlist-agrees`'s
printed recipe now shows `--kicad-cli` carrying the resolver's value, not the
literal.

**STILL UNVERIFIED ON A NON-DARWIN MACHINE**, same as G169's own candidates -
nobody here has a Linux or Windows machine to run `make check` on, so this is
confirmed by reasoning about `$(origin)` and by the darwin-machine
perturbation above, not by observing the Linux or Windows arm run for real.

### G171 - gate 7 PORTS WHOLE and runs on NOTHING: no design in this repository has a checklist, so twenty ported tests pass over fixtures and the gate has never seen a circuit

`lib/schgen/gates/traceability.ts` is a pure port (`tools/schgen/port-manifest.json`'s `files`,
no cuts in the module itself). `tools/schgen/verify.ts`'s `runGates` registers gate 7 **only when
`d.spec.checklist !== null`**, and `DesignSpec.checklist` is `null` for every design this
repository has: the ported `mini` fixture, and the four parity circuits as
`tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` assembles them. **So gate 7 is registered zero times on a real
circuit**, and its row is absent from the census rather than carrying a problem.

**WHY THAT IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS GATE 8, AND SINCE TASK 18 IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AFTER ALL.**
Task 11 made gate 8 report `OSCAR_NOT_PORTED` for a design that declares `oscar`, because its
unavailability was then a fact about the PORT, and gate 7's missing piece was the INPUT - a real
difference. **Task 18 ported gate 8's M1 comparison, so that difference is gone**: gate 8 is now
available and complete too, and what it lacks is also an input - a GENERATED schematic, which
**G238** measures as unavailable for both references, and **G240** records (still unavailable for
both after Task 20, for two now-different reasons - **G245**). The two gates are now
one shape with two different missing inputs, and the paragraph is kept rather than deleted because
its reasoning about gate 7 stands unchanged. A design with no
checklist has nothing to trace to, and inventing a `SCHEMATIC-CHECKLIST.md` so the gate has
something to run on is precisely the invention `CLAUDE.md`'s acceptance-criteria invariant and
**G151**'s criterion forbid - the checklist is a statement of design intent, and an agent
authoring one for the artifact it is producing is the failure this whole workflow exists to
prevent.

**WHAT DOES RUN.** `tests/schgen/gates/traceability.test.ts` - the port, with four declared
`cuts` - is 20 tests over fixture circuits and fixture markdown, and they pass. They exercise
`checklistIds`' nine malformed-line refusals, its repeated-id refusal, and all nine of
`checkTraceability`'s problem kinds. **That is a unit-level regression check and not evidence that
gate 7 works on a design**, which is the distinction `tools/schgen/parity.ts`'s header draws
between port parity and the artifact.

**THE ONE CUT WORTH NAMING**, because it removes the only test that read a real checklist: the
pedals test's *"matches the item counts the real checklist states"* reads
`h7-platform/SCHEMATIC-CHECKLIST.md` and compares `checklistIds`' per-prefix counts against the
item-count line that file states about itself. That file does not exist here and cannot be
transcribed - it is another project's design intent - so the test is cut (a pure deletion, with
the three imports only it used). **Nothing in this repository now checks `checklistIds` against a
document that was not written for it.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 7, running `tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` over the four
  parity circuits.
- **Evidence** `bun run tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` prints, for each of the four circuits,
  `DID NOT RUN 7 checklist traceability     the design's \`checklist\` is null, so there is no
  checklist to trace to`. A check that could have failed: `grep -rn "checklist:" ` over
  `tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts` gives `checklist: null`, and
  `tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` sets the same; `grep -rln "SCHEMATIC-CHECKLIST" --include="*.md" .`
  outside `node_modules` returns **nothing**, so there is no checklist document here to point a
  design at. `bun test tests/schgen/gates/traceability.test.ts` is 20 pass / 0 fail.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the census, ran the ported test, and read `runGates`'
  registration condition.
- **Why it is open** it needs a `SCHEMATIC-CHECKLIST.md` for some circuit here, and that document
  is DESIGN INTENT: which items a schematic must demonstrate. The producing agent may not author
  it. Nothing in Task 11's brief assigns it, and nothing should until the owner or a spec says
  what this repository's checklist items are.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: gate 7 is registered and reports zero problems for at
  least one design in this repository whose checklist was authored by something other than the
  generator - and the census records it as having RUN rather than as absent.** A second,
  independent criterion the first does not protect: **until then, gate 7's absence is reported,
  not omitted** - which `tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`'s `DID NOT RUN` line and its `GATE_ORDER`
  table already satisfy, and which is the half of this that is done.
  **MECHANISM, untried:** give one circuit - `transistor-preamp`'s lab board is the smallest
  candidate - a `docs/<circuit>/SCHEMATIC-CHECKLIST.md` written by the owner or derived from an
  existing spec, and a `ChecklistConfig` naming it. The competing mechanism, **and it is not
  equivalent**, is to make a null `checklist` a gate-7 PROBLEM the way a declared `oscar` is now a
  gate-8 problem; that would make the gap loud on every run but would also make `make check` red
  for every design forever, so it is a decision rather than a fix.

### G172 - gate 3 now reads the s-expression netlist and no XML parser entered the tree - and the cost is that a `lib/schgen/` module transitively imports the module that spawns `kicad-cli`

**WHAT CHANGED AND WHY IT IS A SUBTRACTION.** Pedals' `tools/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` takes
a `Connectivity { nets: Map<string, string[]>; references: string[] }` built by
`connectivityFromXml`, which parses a `kicadxml` export with `fast-xml-parser`. This repository
already reads the s-expression `.net` export with `lib/kicad/netlist.ts`'s `importNetlist`, and
that result carries everything `compareConnectivity` reads: the references are
`components[].designator`, and each net's members are already the sorted `"designator.pin"`
strings. Task 11 therefore declared `lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` **diverged** and changed
exactly two reads. **ONE NETLIST READER, and one fewer dependency than the port would have
brought.**

**THE THREE KiCad NAME CONVENTIONS ARE UNCHANGED**, because they are KiCad's and not pedals':
`unconnected-(` is the IR's not-connected set, `Net-(` are the unlabelled block-internal nets
matched one-for-one by pin set, and everything else matches a labelled net by its leaf name.
Perturbed to prove it: changing `name.startsWith("Net-(")` to `"Net~("` turns **10 of the 14**
ported gate-3 tests red, and the internal-net comparison is among them by name -
`"internal net MID [R1.2, R2.1] has no matching unlabelled net in the schematic"` appears where
the test expects `[]`. Restored; `git status --porcelain` clean.

**THE COST, which is the reason this is recorded rather than only reported.**
`lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` imports `stderrProblems` from
`tools/schgen/kicad-run.ts`, exactly as the pedals source does - and in pedals both files live
under `tools/`. Here the gate landed under `lib/schgen/`, whose own README says in terms:
*"`kicad-cli` lives behind `tools/schgen/kicad-run.ts` once that file ports, never here — what
`render/library.ts` and `render/stock-symbols.ts` use is the *path* to it … never an
invocation."* **A module under `lib/schgen/` now transitively imports the module that calls
`spawnSync`.** Measured: nothing is spawned at import time (`kicad-run.ts`'s module scope is
imports, two `const`s and function declarations), so this is a dependency-direction breach and not
a behaviour change. `lib/schgen/gates/pin-identity.ts` has the milder version of the same thing -
it imports `lib/kicad/libtable.ts`, which imports `KICAD_CLI`, a path and not a spawner, which
the README explicitly permits.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 4, writing the divergence.
- **Evidence** the two reads are marked in `lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` and its manifest
  `diverged` entry states them. A check that could have failed:
  `grep -c "fast-xml-parser" package.json bun.lock` returns 0 in both, so no XML parser is in the
  dependency tree. For the breach: `grep -n "kicad-run" lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` gives
  the one import, and `grep -n "spawnSync" tools/schgen/kicad-run.ts` gives its two uses, both
  inside functions. For the convention: the perturbation above, which is a check that could have
  failed and did.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the divergence, ran the greps and ran the
  perturbation.
- **Why it is open** the import is what the pedals source does, and the gate's location under
  `lib/schgen/gates/` is the Task 11 brief's. Moving the gate to `tools/schgen/` or moving
  `stderrProblems` out of `kicad-run.ts` are both changes to a ported file's shape that no brief
  asks for, and `stderrProblems` is a pure text function that only lives beside the spawner
  because pedals put it there.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION, REPLACED 2026-10-20 BY THE TASK 11 REVIEW WITH A CHEAPER
  AND MORE CHECKABLE ONE, and the replacement is recorded rather than swapped in quietly.**

  **The criterion that now binds: NO FILE UNDER `lib/` IMPORTS FROM `tools/`, and a check that
  could fail says which.** `grep -rn 'from "../../../tools/' lib/` returns **exactly one hit** -
  `lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts:28`, this entry's subject - and nothing in the repository
  guards that direction. Measured, so the "one" is a count and not an impression:
  `grep -rln 'from "\(\.\./\)\{1,4\}tools/' lib/ | wc -l` is **1**.

  **THE WITHDRAWN CRITERION was *"no module under `lib/schgen/` reaches `spawnSync`, by any import
  path"*, and it was worse in two ways.** It is harder to check (it needs an import-graph walk
  rather than a grep), and **it is not actually the thing that is wrong**: the review priced the
  spawner reachability and it costs nothing - nothing spawns at import time, and
  `KICAD_CLI=/nonexistent/kicad-cli bun test tests/schgen/gates/connectivity.test.ts` gives
  **14 pass / 0 fail**, so the import is reachable on a machine with no KiCad at all and breaks
  nothing. What is wrong is the DEPENDENCY DIRECTION, which is a statement about layering that a
  one-line grep decides, and the layering is what `lib/schgen/README.md`'s rule is about.

  **MECHANISM, untried:** a test asserting that grep returns nothing, with
  `lib/schgen/gates/connectivity.ts` as a declared exemption until it is fixed - the same
  exemption-with-teeth shape the five guards of **G176** use. The fix it would then demand is
  unchanged: move `stderrProblems`/`BENIGN_STDERR` into a pure text module beside
  `lib/kicad/netlist.ts` and declare `kicad-run.ts` diverged to import them from there.
  **That mechanism would diverge a file four other tasks depend on**, so an implementer should
  price it before taking it; the grep itself costs nothing and can land first.

### G173 - the Task 11 brief decided to hand-transcribe `padNumbers`, and the premise was false: the whole pedals file is 26 lines with one resolvable import, so it is a byte-checked PORT instead

**THE BRIEF'S DECISION, verbatim:** *"Gate 6 ports `padNumbers`' body — 13 lines over `parse`,
reading `(pad "<n>" …)` atoms and skipping the empty number — into
`lib/schgen/gates/footprint-pads.ts`, resolving a footprint through the `fp-lib-table` that
`generatedFiles` already writes plus the KiCad install's own table."* Its premise was that
`@/kicad/footprint` cannot resolve here - `lib/schgen/README.md` said so: *"`@/kicad/footprint`
and `@/kicad/components`. Not resolved, and nothing here imports them yet."*

**MEASURED, AND THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD.** `digital-pedal-platform`'s `tools/kicad/footprint.ts`
is **26 lines**, its exports are `padNumbers` and nothing else, and its only imports are
`node:fs` and `@/kicad/sexpr` - which `port-manifest.json`'s `externals` already resolves to
`lib/kicad/sexpr.ts`, and which exports both names it needs (`parse`, and `SList` is not used).
So it ports through the same `pedals-tools` source root `lib/kicad/libtable.ts` uses (ruling R25),
lands at `lib/kicad/footprint.ts`, and is **byte-checked like every other `files[]` entry**.

**WHAT THAT CHANGED DOWNSTREAM, which is why it is worth more than one file.** With
`@/kicad/footprint` resolved, `gates/pinIdentity.ts` ports **whole** - `footprintPads`,
`designFootprintPads`, `GENERIC_SYMBOL_LIBRARIES` and all - so gate 6's footprint resolution is
not hand-written at all. **`lib/schgen/gates/footprint-pads.ts` was therefore not created.** The
brief named a FILE and a MECHANISM; its criterion was *"a footprint that does not resolve is a
gate-6 problem naming the footprint and where it was looked for"*, and the ported
`footprintProblem` satisfies it verbatim (`part X: footprint Y cannot be resolved: …`, with
`libtable.ts`'s own message naming every path tried).

**WHY THE DEVIATION IS STRICTLY BETTER AND NOT MERELY DIFFERENT.** A hand transcription of
`padNumbers` would have been a 10th hand-written file under `lib/schgen/`, byte-checked against
nothing - the exact residual **G123** records for
`tests/schgen/render/symbol-self-text.test.ts`. R25's criterion is that *"nothing enters this
repository from the pedals tree without a byte-check or a declared `sourceSha`"*, and a hand
transcription meets neither.

**AMENDED 2026-10-20 by the Task 11 review, which added the two facts that make this an entry
about a BRIEF rather than about a file.**

**1. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS NOT MERELY UNNECESSARY - IT WAS FALSE, AND CHECKABLE BEFORE ANY WORK
STARTED.** The brief said to hand-transcribe *because* `@/kicad/footprint` could not resolve here.
That is a claim with a one-command test: the file is 26 lines and imports `node:fs` and
`@/kicad/sexpr`, and `port-manifest.json`'s `externals` already resolved the second. **The reason
given for the mechanism was wrong, not just the mechanism**, and `tools/schgen/port-probe.ts`
exists precisely so that this question is asked without editing the manifest. The lesson a later
reader needs is the ORDER: probe a brief's stated premise before following the mechanism built on
it, because a brief is written by someone who had not yet tried it.

**2. A `files[]` ENTRY IS BYTE-COMPARED EVERY RUN, WHICH IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN A
`sourceSha`** - and that is the whole reason the deviation is an improvement rather than a
sideways move. A `sourceSha` notices only that the pedals source MOVED; the byte-check re-derives
the ported file from the source and the manifest's own rewrite rule and compares it. The review
drove all three claims rather than reading them: `lib/kicad/footprint.ts` is a `files[]` entry
with `root: "pedals-tools"`; perturbing one line of it turned `port-fidelity.test.ts` red naming
the file with the exact diff; and `lib/schgen/gates/pin-identity.ts` differs from its source by
**only** the 7-line provenance header and six import rewrites, with no `cuts` concealing a
substitution.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 1, probing whether the brief's premise held before following
  its mechanism. **Amended the same day by the Task 11 review**, which drove the three byte-check
  claims independently.
- **Evidence** `wc -l /Users/orion/work/pedals-work/digital-pedal-platform/tools/kicad/footprint.ts`
  is 26; `grep -n "^import\|^export" ` on it gives exactly `node:fs`, `@/kicad/sexpr` and
  `export function padNumbers`. A check that could have failed:
  `bun run tools/schgen/port.ts` ports it and 82 other files with no refusal, and
  `bun test tests/schgen/port-fidelity.test.ts` byte-checks all 83 - so the claim "it ports" is
  held by a test rather than asserted. `grep -rn "footprint-pads" lib tools tests` returns nothing,
  which is the deviation stated as an absence.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer read the pedals file, added the manifest entry, ran the
  porter and ran the byte-check.
- **Why it is open** it is not a defect; it is a DEVIATION from a brief's stated mechanism,
  recorded because `CLAUDE.md` requires the deviation to be written down rather than silently
  taken: *"the criterion is the settlement; the mechanism is advice from someone who had not yet
  tried it … record the deviation when the mechanism turns out to be wrong."* It also leaves one
  real residual, below.
- **What would settle it** nothing about `padNumbers`. **The residual that a later reader needs:**
  resolving `@/kicad/footprint` widens what a ported file may import, exactly as resolving
  `@/kicad/netlist` did in **G121**, and the same cost applies - a later ported file importing a
  name `lib/kicad/footprint.ts` does not have would once have refused at port time on the
  SPECIFIER. **Task 11 closed that hole for every external, including this one**
  (`assertExternalExports` in `tools/schgen/port.ts`; see G121's amended clause (a)), so the
  widening arrives with its guard rather than ahead of it. `@/kicad/components` remains
  unresolved, and `gates/oscar/graph.ts` still needs it - Task 18's.

### G174 - measured: `lib/kicad/libtable.ts` had been ported and executed by NOTHING; gate 6 is its first consumer and it worked unchanged - but only 3 of its 6 exported functions are reached

**THE MEASUREMENT.** Task 6b ported `digital-pedal-platform`'s `tools/kicad/libtable.ts` to
`lib/kicad/libtable.ts` - 279 lines, byte-checked, imported by `tools/schgen/kicad-config.ts` for
the `GlobalTable` TYPE only. Until Task 11 **no code path called any function in it**. Gate 6 is
the first: `footprintPads(d.outDir, stockFootprintTable(KICAD_CLI, kicadVersion()))` calls
`resolveFootprintIn`, which calls `resolveThrough` -> `resolveInTables` -> `searchTable` ->
`readLibTable`, with `expandHermetic` expanding the one `${KICAD10_FOOTPRINT_DIR}`-style variable
`stockFootprintTable` declares.

**IT WORKED ON FIRST USE, with no edit.** `tests/schgen/gates/gates.kicad.test.ts` resolves all
seventeen of the `mini` design's footprints - six distinct stock libraries, through the
`fp-lib-table` the generator wrote into the scratch `outDir` and then the install's own template
table - and gate 6 reports **zero problems**. That is the first time this repository has resolved
a footprint through a KiCad library table rather than through `tests/kicad/footprint-library.ts`'s
own directory walk.

**WHAT IS STILL UNEXECUTED, which is the half of this a later reader needs.** Of the file's six
exported functions, gate 6 reaches **three**: `readLibTable`, `resolveFootprintIn` and (as a
type) `GlobalTable`. Unreached by anything in this repository:

| export | what reaches it in pedals, and what does not here |
| --- | --- |
| `resolveFootprint` | the non-hermetic entry point, which consults `GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE` - the USER's `~/Library/Preferences/kicad/.../fp-lib-table`. Nothing here calls it, and nothing should: this repository's own rule is that results never depend on the user's KiCad profile. |
| `resolveFootprintInGlobal` | `designFootprintPads`, which gate 6 can use for a design checked BEFORE generation. `tools/schgen/verify.ts` uses `footprintPads` (post-generation) only, so this arm is dead here. The ported test that drives it, `gates/designPads.test.ts`, could not land - see **G175**. |
| `expandUri` | only `resolveFootprint`'s path, plus `BUILTIN_CANDIDATES`' three-candidate probe for `KICAD10_FOOTPRINT_DIR`. The hermetic path uses `expandHermetic` instead. |

**AND `GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE`'s DEFAULT IS A MACHINE-SPECIFIC PATH THAT G169's RESOLVER DOES NOT
COVER.** It is `process.env["KICAD_FP_LIB_TABLE"] ?? path.join(os.homedir(), "Library/Preferences/kicad/10.0/fp-lib-table")` -
a macOS-only literal, in a PORTED file, which `lib/kicad/install.ts` knows nothing about. Nothing
here evaluates it at run time today (only `resolveFootprint` and `kicadCommonVars` read it, and
nothing calls either), so it is latent rather than broken; the module-level `const` itself is
evaluated on every import of the file, but computing a path is not using one.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 5, which was the first code to call into the file.
- **Evidence** `bun test tests/schgen/gates/gates.kicad.test.ts` is 3 pass / 0 fail, and its gate-6
  case asserts `checkPinIdentity(...)` equals `[]` over the generated `mini` design with
  `footprintPads` resolving real `.kicad_mod` files - a check that could have failed, and did fail
  for a different reason before the pin-table fixture was copied (`part U_AMP names pin table
  OPA1688, which does not exist`). For the path:
  `grep -n "GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE" lib/kicad/libtable.ts` gives its definition and its two readers,
  both inside functions nothing calls. **"No call site" CORRECTED 2026-10-20, Task 10b round 2:**
  that original phrasing overstated what the grep actually shows. Re-running it verbatim -
  `grep -rn "resolveFootprint\b\|resolveFootprintInGlobal\|expandUri" lib tools tests` outside
  `lib/kicad/libtable.ts` itself - returns **two hits, not zero**:
  `lib/schgen/gates/pin-identity.ts:11` (the import) and `:60` (`resolveFootprintInGlobal(fp,
  global)` inside `designFootprintPads`). The table two paragraphs up already says as much -
  `resolveFootprintInGlobal`'s row names `designFootprintPads` as its caller - so the SUBSTANCE
  was recorded correctly; only the Evidence bullet's one-line summary was wrong to call it "no
  call site" rather than "one call site, on a function (`designFootprintPads`) nothing here calls
  in turn." **This does not change GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE's reachability**, which is the narrower and
  correct claim: `resolveFootprintInGlobal` takes `global: GlobalTable` as a caller-supplied
  PARAMETER and never reads `GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE` itself (confirmed:
  `grep -n "GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE" lib/kicad/libtable.ts` shows it read only inside `resolveFootprint`
  and `kicadCommonVars`, neither of which appears in the two-hit grep above or anywhere else
  outside `lib/kicad/libtable.ts`) - so the literal itself is still read by nothing reachable in
  this repository, on any platform, by any path.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the first consumer, ran it, and ran the greps; the
  correction above is CONFIRMED by this writer re-running the exact quoted command and reading its
  output, not relayed.
- **Why it is open** the unexecuted exports are not defects and three of them are deliberately
  unreachable here. What is open is the macOS literal, which **G169**'s directive covers in
  principle (*"no hardcoded paths unique to this machine"*) and which Task 10b's resolver did not
  reach because it is inside a ported file that may not be hand-edited.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: no path unique to one machine is computed anywhere in this
  repository without going through `lib/kicad/install.ts`, including inside a ported file - and a
  check that could fail says which.** `tests/kicad/install.test.ts` already pins the two surviving
  macOS literals it knows about; `GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE`'s is a third it does not count.
  **MECHANISM, untried:** extend that test's grep to `lib/kicad/libtable.ts` and declare the hit,
  then either set `KICAD_FP_LIB_TABLE` from `install.ts` at every entry point (which leaves the
  literal in place but unreachable) or declare `libtable.ts` diverged to compute its default from
  `defaultKicadCli()`. **The second costs the byte-check on a 279-line file for a one-line
  change**, which is a bad trade unless something starts calling `resolveFootprint`.

**TASK 10b ROUND 2 (2026-10-20): DEFERRED, NOT FIXED, WITH AN OWNER.** The
honest options, as this entry's directive-compliance review named them, were
(a) an upstream edit plus a re-port, declaring `lib/kicad/libtable.ts`
diverged with a `sourceSha` and paying the byte-check, or (b) routing its
*consumers* through `lib/kicad/install.ts` and leaving the constant
unreferenced. **(b) does not apply**: the evidence correction above confirms
there are zero consumers to route - `resolveFootprint` and `kicadCommonVars`,
the only two functions that read `GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE`, have no call site
anywhere in this repository, on any platform. **(a) is this entry's own
"bad trade" case**: declaring a 279-line ported file diverged, and paying its
byte-check on every future upstream diff, to fix a literal nothing can reach
is not a defensible trade for this fix round - the same conclusion this entry
already reached, now confirmed rather than merely argued. **This is therefore
a third instance of the owner's "no hardcoded paths unique to this machine"
directive left unaddressed, stated plainly rather than left with no owner.**
The owner of closing it: whichever task first calls `resolveFootprint` or
`kicadCommonVars`, OR makes gate 6's design-time path live by resolving
**G175**'s temp-scratch blind spot and landing `gates/designPads.test.ts` -
at that point `designFootprintPads`/`resolveFootprintInGlobal` becomes
reachable too, even though it still would not itself read
`GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE`, and the literal's dormancy argument for THIS literal
specifically ends the day `resolveFootprint` or `kicadCommonVars` gets a
first caller. **The mechanism to use then** is this entry's own: declare
`lib/kicad/libtable.ts` diverged with a `sourceSha`, and change
`GLOBAL_LIB_TABLE`'s default to read through `lib/kicad/install.ts` (a
sibling resolver function if the fp-lib-table path convention differs
enough from the symbol/footprint roots to need one - KiCad's own fp-lib-table
search path is a user-profile location, not an install-root one, so it may
not be `defaultSymbolDir`/`defaultFootprintDir`'s shape at all), paying the
byte-check once, at the point it is first worth paying.

### G175 - two of the four ported gate-6 test files CANNOT LAND, and what stops both is a measured BLIND SPOT in the temp-scratch guard: it refuses a correct removal written as an assignment rather than a declaration

**THE TWO FILES**, both out of the tree under ruling R4 (never land red), with their exact
manifest JSON so re-adding them is an edit and not a rediscovery:

```json
{ "from": "gates/designPads.test.ts", "to": "tests/schgen/gates/design-pads.test.ts" }
```
```json
{
  "from": "gates/pinIdentity.kicad.test.ts",
  "to": "tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.kicad.test.ts",
  "sourceSha": "7a554ed39cd07d2b13ee984f947895401d1db4dd51a0cf94e9854ff6388e2cea",
  "task": "<the task that lands it>",
  "why": "G112 (mcu/pinmap) and D3: its build() declares `{ kind: \"labels\", reason: \"fixture\" }`, which must become a rendering that still exists. It also needs the temp-scratch exemption this entry is about."
}
```

(`designPads.test.ts`'s SHA, for a `diverged` entry if one is ever needed, is
`42a7d1faa9fa7e504f9b9c9a2020445cd820031b6277f84a83ff398de69a9d29`. It needs no divergence
otherwise: it is import-clean once `@/kicad/footprint` resolves, which Task 11 did, and declares
no `labels` rendering and no MCU.)

**WHAT STOPS THEM, AND IT IS THE SAME THING TWICE.** `tests/stripboard/temp-scratch.test.ts`'s
static sweep requires every `mkdtempSync` site under `tests/` to either name its directory and
remove it, or register it. Its "named" detector is
`/(?:const|let|var)\s+(\w+)\s*=\s*fs\.mkdtempSync\(/`, so it counts only a site whose DECLARATION
and ASSIGNMENT are one statement. Both files write

```ts
let dir = "";
…
dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "…"));
```

which is a bare assignment to a variable declared earlier - so `sites !== named.length` and the
file is reported as having an *"unnamed site"*. **Both files then remove that directory
correctly**: `designPads.test.ts` with `afterEach(() => fs.rmSync(dir, …))` and
`pinIdentity.kicad.test.ts` with `afterAll(() => { fs.rmSync(dir, …) })`.

**SO THE GUARD REFUSES A SHAPE THAT SATISFIES ITS OWN STATED RULE**, which is its own words:
*"every `mkdtemp` site under `tests/` must either name its directory and remove it, or register
it here."* These sites name their directory and remove it. The blind spot is in the detector, not
in the rule, and it errs toward refusing - which is the right direction and is why this is a
finding rather than an alarm.

**WHY TASK 11 DID NOT WIDEN THE DETECTOR.** Relaxing a standing guard in order to land the agent's
own files is the acceptance-criteria breach `CLAUDE.md` names: the producing agent would be
choosing what the check is. The two files stay out, R4-style, and the decision is recorded here
for someone who is not landing them.

**WHAT IS LOST, measured rather than estimated.** `designPads.test.ts` is 5 tests and **the only
thing in either tree that drives `designFootprintPads`** - the pre-generation arm of gate 6's
footprint resolution, and with it `resolveFootprintInGlobal` (**G173**'s table).
`pinIdentity.kicad.test.ts` is 5 tests: 2 driving `footprintPads` against real stock footprints,
and 3 driving `GENERIC_SYMBOL_LIBRARIES` and the MPN-override rule against real installed
symbols. **Of those five, the MPN-override rule is covered elsewhere** - the ported
`gates/pin-identity.test.ts` has its own fixture cases - and `footprintPads` against real
footprints is covered by `tests/schgen/gates/gates.kicad.test.ts`. The uncovered residual is
therefore `designFootprintPads` and the three stock-library MPN cases.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 1, probing every gate-6 test file for portability.
- **Evidence** `grep -n "mkdtempSync\|rmSync" ` on both pedals files shows the assignment form and
  the removal. A check that could have failed: adding the `designPads.test.ts` entry and running
  `bun test tests/stripboard/temp-scratch.test.ts` fails the *"every mkdtemp site under tests/
  either removes its own directory or registers it"* test naming
  `schgen/gates/design-pads.test.ts: 1 unnamed site(s)` - and `bun test` is green with both entries
  out. For the coverage claim:
  `grep -rn "designFootprintPads" lib tools tests` returns only its definition in
  `lib/schgen/gates/pin-identity.ts`.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer read both pedals files, read the guard's regex, added and
  removed the manifest entries, and ran the guard both ways.
- **Why it is open** landing either needs a change to a guard this task's own implementer must not
  author. The `pinIdentity.kicad.test.ts` half needs a `labels` substitution as well, which is
  ordinary divergence work.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: `designFootprintPads` is executed by something, and the
  temp-scratch guard reports a file that writes `let dir` then `dir = fs.mkdtempSync(…)` then
  `fs.rmSync(dir, …)` as COMPLIANT rather than as an unnamed site - with a case that could have
  failed either way.** **MECHANISM, untried and NOT the criterion:** extend the guard's `named`
  detector to also match a bare `(\w+)\s*=\s*fs\.mkdtempSync\(` and keep the existing
  `rmSync(<name>)` requirement on it, so the relaxation is only about where the variable is
  declared and the removal is still proven. That is a change to a guard, so it wants a reviewer
  who is not the one landing the two files, and the detector change should be driven red first by
  deleting one of the two `rmSync` calls.

### G176 - the schematic port now holds declared exemptions in FIVE exemption tables across FOUR guard files, and the footprint sweep is the newest - **G133**'s recurrence, counted

**G133** recorded that a ported test FIXTURE collides with this repository's standing guards as
reliably as a ported test does, and that the symbol sweep was *"the second repo-wide static guard
the port has had to be exempted from, after the temp-scratch check of G122/G123"*, adding that
*"the recurrence matters more than either entry"*. Task 11 is the fourth task to hit it.

**THE COUNT, read off the exemption tables rather than remembered - AND IT IS FIVE TABLES ACROSS
FOUR FILES, NOT FIVE GUARDS.** An earlier version of this entry's heading said "five guards",
which its own table contradicts: two of the five rows are the same file
(`tests/stripboard/temp-scratch.test.ts`, whose static sweep and whose registering-module table
are separate exemption mechanisms in one guard file). **G133**'s criterion is about GUARDS a
porter will trip, so the distinction matters for answering it: a porter needs to know about four
files and five places to declare something.

| guard | exemption mechanism | entries the port holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/stripboard/temp-scratch.test.ts`, static sweep | `REMOVES_VIA_OWN_LIST` | 2 of 3 (`schgen/render/library.test.ts`, and Task 11's `schgen/verify.test.ts`) |
| the same file, registering-module table | `REGISTERING` | 1 of 12 (`run.ts`) |
| `tests/kicad/symbol-names.test.ts` | `NOT_A_KICAD_SYMBOL` | **all 7**, 3 of them Task 11's (`Fix:OPAMP2`, `Fix:OPAMP2X`, `H7:TPS7A4901`) |
| `tests/schgen/port-fidelity.test.ts`, no-shadowing | `SHADOWS_A_PEDALS_FILE_BY_DECISION` | both 2 |
| `tests/kicad/footprint-names.test.ts` | **`FIXTURE_FOOTPRINT_LIBRARY`, new in Task 11** | all 4 (`Pkg:SOIC8`, `Pkg:MISSING`, `Pkg:TWO`, `Pkg:SOIC8EP`), plus 1 entry in the pre-existing `NOT_A_KICAD_FOOTPRINT` (`" "`) |

**WHY A NEW TABLE RATHER THAN AN EXISTING ONE**, which is the part a later reader cannot
re-derive. `tests/kicad/footprint-sweep.ts` already had three exemption categories and **none of
them can hold a `Pkg:*` name**: `NOT_A_KICAD_FOOTPRINT` is for values that are not lib ids at all
(it is pinned against exactly the non-lib-id swept set, in both directions);
`CONSTRUCTED_FOR_A_REFUSAL`'s teeth assert `resolveFootprintOnDisk(name) === "no-such-footprint"`,
which a name whose LIBRARY half is invented can never be; and `SYNTHETIC_PREFIX` would require
renaming the literals, which is a hand edit to a PORTED file that `port-fidelity.test.ts` refuses
and that a `cuts` entry cannot make (cuts are deletion-only).

**THE NEW TABLE CARRIES THE SAME TWO TEETH THE SYMBOL SIDE HAS**, deliberately copied rather than
invented: every entry must still fail at the **library** (not at the footprint, and not resolve),
and every swept site must be under `tests/schgen/`. Plus the bidirectional pin, a reason over 60
characters, and a check that none of the nicknames is an installed footprint library - so if KiCad
ever ships a `Pkg.pretty` the exemption stops being safe loudly.

**AND ONE THING THE SWEEP FOUND THAT IS NOT AN EXEMPTION.** `tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts`
declares `footprint: " "` - a single space - because gate 6's refusal tests
`part.footprint.trim() === ""`, so only a blank-but-not-empty value reaches that arm. It is
recorded in `NOT_A_KICAD_FOOTPRINT` as what it is: the INPUT to a refusal, and a claim about no
library at all.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, running the full suite after the gate ports landed.
- **Evidence** `bun test` went from 3168 pass / 0 fail to 3290 pass / **3 fail** the moment the
  ported gate tests entered the tree, and the three failures were
  `every symbol name swept out of the source resolves in an installed KiCad library`,
  `every footprint name swept out of the repository resolves in an installed KiCad library` and
  `every swept value that is not a KiCad lib id is one this repository has accounted for` -
  quoted from the run. Each named its offenders. After the exemptions: 3294 pass / 0 fail. The
  counts in the table above were read off the five tables in the tree, not recalled - and the
  table is what caught this entry's own heading saying "five guards" where two rows name one file.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the suite before and after, read each guard's exemption
  mechanism, and established that none of the three existing footprint categories could hold a
  `Pkg:*` name by reading their teeth.
- **Why it is open** it is not a defect in any one guard or any one entry; it is a cost of the port
  that recurs per task and that **G133** asked to have counted. What is open is whether the
  pattern should be generalised before it happens a sixth time.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a task that lands a ported test fixture can find out, in
  one place, which repo-wide static guards it will trip and what each one's exemption mechanism
  is - without running the suite and reading four guard files.** **MECHANISM, untried:** a short
  section in `lib/schgen/README.md` listing the four guard files, their five exemption tables and their
  teeth, held to being complete by a test that asserts the named tables exist and are non-empty.
  The competing mechanism - teach the guards to skip `tests/schgen/` wholesale - is **rejected
  here and the reason belongs with the criterion**: every one of these guards exists because this
