  there the answer so far is no, in a second measure.
- **What would settle it** nothing - it is a measurement. **A caution for Task 17:** the sheet
  figures' `occupiedArea` includes the frames, so it moves with `packSheet` - **G207** measured the
  two packers giving one sheet extents of 185.42 x 38.10 mm and 109.22 x 71.12 mm for the same
  content. The first three sheet measures are properties of the drawing; the fourth is partly a
  property of the packing, and must not be compared across a packer change.

### G217 - the readability-baseline registry ships EMPTY and no agent may fill it, and the twelve-field shape departs TWICE - one departure the spec predicted and one it did not

`schematic/readability-baselines.json` holds `"baselines": []` and seven design notes.
`grantedBy` is a whitelist of one - `owner` - and `lib/schgen/readability/baseline-read.ts` refuses
anything else by name, citing `CLAUDE.md`'s invariant: **an agent that could enter its own drawing's
numbers as the reference would be authoring the criterion outright**, which is the failure that file
describes as an agent building the intent from the artifact it had already produced and then
checking the artifact against it.

**THE EMPTY LIST IS THE CORRECT STATE AND NOT AN UNFINISHED ONE.** §3.3's acceptance table: a
circuit generated for the first time *"reports the measures with no pass or fail"*, and every
drawing this repository has produced is a first generation. **One refusal of
`tools/stripboard/approvals.ts` is therefore deliberately NOT carried across**: that loader refuses
an empty `approvals` list - *"a registry that approves nothing is a file that looks like governance
and governs nothing"* - which is right THERE, because an empty approvals file means the gate it
feeds can never open. The protection here is instead that **every consumer prints the count it
read**: `tools/schgen/verify.ts` puts `schematic/readability-baselines.json 0 baseline(s)` on every
`GateResult`, so a reader is told zero rather than left to assume there were some.

**DEPARTURE ONE, WHICH SPEC §3.3 PREDICTED:** *"an approval admits one termination, whereas a
baseline carries four measured numbers"*, so `admits` becomes `measures`. It carries **five**
numbers and not four, because §3.3's table reads *"bends: count, and per edge"* - one measure in two
units - and the loader refuses a sixth by name, since §3.3 refuses a composite score and an extra
figure recorded beside the four is how a composite arrives without anybody deciding to adopt one.

**DEPARTURE TWO, WHICH IT DID NOT PREDICT, AND IT COSTS SOMETHING.** An approval's `board` becomes
`circuit` AND `block`, because a baseline is per block and a block id is unique only within a
circuit. The twelfth field that makes room for the second of those is **`renderedFrom`, which is
deleted.** That field is load-bearing in the approvals registry: it is where *"WHAT HE LOOKED AT WAS
THE PICTURE AND NOT THESE BYTES"* is said in prose a reader can judge, with the picture-to-bytes
link recorded as an agent's claim rather than collapsed into a path that would imply he inspected
the bytes (**G27**(2)). **A baseline has nowhere to say it.** What he was shown has to go in `why`
or `note`, and no field obliges anyone to say it at all.

**THREE RESIDUALS, each stated here rather than discovered later.**

1. **`compareMeasures` has no production exercise, and that follows from the registry being empty.**
   Every lookup is `absent`, so nothing in the pipeline ever builds a comparison; the
   `comparable-hash-moved` arm and the four rows are driven by
   `tests/schgen/readability/baseline.test.ts` and by nothing else. That is a consequence of *no
   agent may populate it*, not a wiring defect, and it will stop being true the first time he grants
   one.
2. **`consultedBy` is unexercised for the same reason.** The approvals loader proves each cited
   consumer exists and `tests/stripboard/approvals.test.ts` proves it reaches the loader; here there
   is no entry to check, so the clause is code no record has driven.
3. **A change in the EDGE COUNT alone is invisible to `compareMeasures`.** Its four rows are §3.3's
   four measures, and `bendsPerEdge` is not a fifth row - the same bends spread over more or fewer
   polylines moves `renderMeasures`'s second number and no row of the comparison.

**AND THE LIMIT THE APPROVALS CHANNEL ALREADY RECORDS IS CARRIED, NOT PAPERED OVER: no file can
prove the owner said anything** (**G27**). The three readings refuse a record that quotes nothing, a
quote in the narrator's voice, and a quote in which nobody is speaking - **the same code**, now in
`lib/owner-words.ts` and called by both loaders - and **a fabricated plausible sentence passes all
three.** What the design buys instead is scope and visibility.

**ONE NARROWING RELATIVE TO THE APPROVALS LOADER, deliberate:** the SELECTION shape
(*"low-cut: part-walk-s1"*) is **not admitted here.** It was added to the approvals registry on
2026-10-17 by a controller ruling **after the voice reading refused a real reply of his**; no
equivalent case has arisen for a baseline, so admitting it would be widening an admission on no
evidence. The refusal nonetheless CALLS `isSelectionFor` and reports whether the quote would have
passed it, so the cost of the narrowing is measured rather than assumed.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, Steps 3 and 5.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/readability/baseline.test.ts`, which drives a well-formed entry through
  the loader FIRST - a loader that threw on everything would satisfy every refusal - and then each
  refusal in turn. Three perturbations, applied and restored: dropping the `grantedBy` whitelist,
  the voice reading and the narration sweep each turn a named test red (P5, P6, P7). The two
  departures are read off `BASELINE_ENTRY_KEYS` against `APPROVAL_ENTRY_KEYS`, both in the tree.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote both, ran the tests and drove the perturbations.
- **Why it is open** residual 2 in particular: a clause no record has driven is a clause whose first
  real use is its first test. And the `renderedFrom` loss is a real reduction in what a baseline can
  be held to.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION for the `renderedFrom` loss: a reader of a granted baseline
  can tell what the owner actually looked at, and whether the link from that to the hashed bytes is
  a measurement or an agent's inference.** **MECHANISM, untried:** a thirteenth field, which would
  take this registry's shape off `render-approvals.json`'s twelve - so the alternative mechanism,
  also untried, is to require it in `why` and have the loader refuse a `why` that does not say what
  was shown. **The criterion is the settlement; neither mechanism has been tried.** For residuals 1
  and 2, **an owner decision is what settles them**, because both end the moment he grants a
  baseline - and nobody is to ask him for one unprompted.

### G218 - MEASURED: the size of G106's canonicalisation defect on this driver, over all twelve blocks - and it CORRECTS that entry's own expectation in three of five numbers

**G106** says *"every one of the four measures the spec requires - bends, bends per edge, crossings,
wire length - is then inflated by an unknown amount"*, and that *"that difference is the size of this
defect and nobody has measured it yet."* It is measured now. `[RAN]` Pre-snap on both sides, so the
only difference between the columns is the canonicalisation - same ELK geometry, once as the router
emitted it and once through `canonicalTopology`:

| block | wires raw -> canonical | bends raw / canonical | crossings raw / canonical | wire length inflation | area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ob-buffer` | 65 -> 57 | **26 / 28** | 7 / 7 | **+10.30 %** | identical |
| `oc-power` | 42 -> 31 | **4 / 5** | 1 / 1 | **+18.16 %** | identical |
| `oc-audio` | 82 -> 70 | **28 / 30** | 5 / 5 | **+14.54 %** | identical |
| `oc-sidechain` | 91 -> 76 | **26 / 27** | 7 / 7 | **+13.99 %** | identical |
| `pt-core` | 179 -> 155 | **81 / 83** | 78 / 78 | **+11.14 %** | identical |
| `tp-leg-upper` / `-feedback` / `-lower-a` / `-lower-b` | 14 -> 14 | 8 / 8 | 0 / 0 | **+2.05 %** | identical |
| `tp-leg-collector` | 11 -> 11 | 6 / 6 | 0 / 0 | **+3.09 %** | identical |
| `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` | 12 -> 12 | 6 / 6 | 0 / 0 | **+2.07 %** | identical |
| `tp-stage` | 75 -> 63 | **21 / 24** | 7 / 7 | **+13.05 %** | identical |

**WIRE LENGTH IS THE ONE MEASURE G106 GOT RIGHT: inflated on 12 of 12, by 2.05 % to 18.16 %.** That
range is the size of the defect on this driver.

**CROSSINGS DO NOT MOVE ON ANY OF THE TWELVE, which contradicts the spike sentence the whole
entry rests on.** `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` §7: *"any measure that does not collapse them
double-counts crossings."* On this driver it does not, for a structural reason rather than a lucky
one: `crossings` in `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts` collects CONTACT POINTS into a `Map` keyed by
`pointKey`, so two duplicate segments touching another net at one point contribute one entry however
many copies there are. **The spike's claim was about a measure that counts contacts per segment
pair; this one counts points.**

**BENDS AND BENDS PER EDGE MOVE THE OTHER WAY - the raw list reports FEWER, on 6 of 12 blocks.**
26 against 28, 4 against 5, 28 against 30, 26 against 27, 81 against 83, 21 against 24. The cause is
in the definition: a bend is a vertex of degree two whose two segments are perpendicular, and a
duplicate segment raises that vertex's degree, so the corner stops being counted as a bend and
starts being counted as a node. **So an uncanonicalised bend count is an UNDER-count, not an
inflation**, and a reader who took G106's sentence at face value would correct it in the wrong
direction.

**AND THAT UNDER-COUNT IS A PROPERTY OF THIS REPOSITORY'S BEND DEFINITION PLUS ITS
CONTACT-DIVISION NORMALISATION - NOT OF CANONICALISATION AS SUCH, AND THE CLAUSE ABOVE MUST NOT BE
READ AS A GENERAL ONE.** `[RELAYED]` The Task 16 review wrote its own naive bend count - a
degree-two vertex of one net whose two segments are perpendicular, **without `measuresOf`'s
`dividedAtContacts` normalisation** - and got the **OPPOSITE direction on 11 of the 12 blocks**: its
raw figures OVER-report. Its naive-raw against this table's canonical column: **31/28, 33/30, 29/27,
85/83, 9/8 four times, 7/6 twice, 27/24**, and **equal on `oc-power`**. (The counts are the
reviewer's and are NOT confirmed by this writer; pairing each with a block is read off this entry's
own canonical column, where 28 is `ob-buffer`, 30 `oc-audio`, 27 `oc-sidechain`, 83 `pt-core`, 8 the
four congruent `tp-leg` legs, 6 `tp-leg-collector` and `tp-leg-emitter-bypass`, and 24 `tp-stage`.)
So the direction of the error depends on which bend definition is in use, and anybody carrying *"an
uncanonicalised bend count under-reports"* to another repository, another frontend or another
normalisation is carrying a claim this measurement does not support.

**AREA IS IDENTICAL ON 12 OF 12, as it must be**: the bounding box of a point set is unchanged by
repeating a point. It is recorded because a measure that cannot be wrong in a given way should say
so rather than borrow the credibility of the ones that can.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, Step 8.
- **Evidence** the table, asserted row by row in `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts`
  (*"inflates wire length on all twelve, leaves crossings and area alone, and UNDER-reports
  bends"*), so it is recomputed on every run. **A check that could have failed, and the first form
  of it DID NOT:** perturbation P4 made `measuresOf` deduplicate its own input by exact endpoint
  order and the test stayed green - because of **G219** - so the perturbation was replaced with one
  that canonicalises the input properly (P4b), and that turns the comparison red naming
  `ob-buffer`. The first form is recorded rather than quietly replaced, because a perturbation that
  changes nothing is indistinguishable from a check with no teeth until you find out which it was.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every figure and both perturbations. **The one exception
  is the naive-bend clause added in Task 16's fix round 1: those figures are RELAYED from the Task
  16 review, which drove its own count, and this writer did not re-run them.**
- **Why it is open** G106 is still open on its own terms, and this entry does not close it: what it
  establishes is that **the defect's size is now known and its SHAPE is not what that entry says.**
  The sentences in G106 and in spec §1.4 revision 4 that say all four measures are inflated are
  wrong for this driver and are left in place rather than edited, so the disagreement is visible.
- **What would settle it** nothing - it is a measurement. **A caution for anyone comparing against
  the spikes:** these are deltas between two readings of ONE geometry, and the spikes' absolute
  crossing figures were taken over uncanonicalised geometry through a different frontend. The two
  are not the same quantity.

### G219 - MEASURED: EVERY ONE of the 82 duplicate wire segments ELK emits is DIRECTION-REVERSED, so a deduplication keyed on `(a, b)` in order would collapse NONE of them

`[RAN]` Over all twelve declared ELK blocks of the four parity circuits, counting duplicates in the
raw pre-snap wire list two ways:

| keyed on | duplicates found |
| --- | --- |
| net plus `a` then `b` **in the order the segment carries them** | **0** |
| net plus the two endpoints **sorted** | **82** |

Per block, by sorted ends: `ob-buffer` 8, `oc-power` 11, `oc-audio` 12, `oc-sidechain` 15,
`pt-core` 24, `tp-stage` 12, and zero on the six `tp-leg-*` blocks. **By exact order, zero
everywhere.**

**SO `geometryKey`'s SORT IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT DEFENSIVE.** `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts`
describes it as *"a segment's geometry, independent of which end was called `a`"* - which reads like
a tidiness measure. It is the entire deduplication: without the sort, clause (a) of spec §1.4's
canonical-topology criterion would collapse nothing at all, and **G218**'s measured wire-length
inflation of up to 18 % would survive into every drawing.

**WHY THE DUPLICATES ARE REVERSED, as far as this writer can tell, and it is stated as a reading
rather than a measurement.** The segments come in consecutive pairs of one net's spanning chain
(**G189**: edges `X:k` and `X:k+1` retracing one another), and a chain's successive edges run in
opposite directions along the shared stretch because each is routed from its own source to its own
target. This writer did not confirm it against `elkjs`'s router.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, Step 8, when perturbation P4 - a deduplication keyed on exact
  endpoint order - changed **nothing** and the test it was meant to drive red stayed green.
- **Evidence** the two-way count above, run over the same twelve blocks **G218** measures, with both
  columns printed. A check that could have failed in either direction: the sorted column is
  non-zero on 6 of 12 blocks and zero on the other 6, so the measurement discriminates rather than
  reporting one number everywhere.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote and ran the count. **The explanation of WHY they are
  reversed is RELAYED from G189's reading of the edge model and is not confirmed against the
  router.**
**THE RESIDUAL THIS ENTRY OPENED IS NOW CLOSED, and it is recorded here rather than left as a
mechanism nobody tried.** Round 1 of this entry said *"nothing in the tree asserts that the sort is
load-bearing"* and offered an assertion in `tests/schgen/elk/junctions.test.ts` as an untried
mechanism, declining it on the ground that `junctions.ts` is Task 13's module. **That reason was
weak** - adding a test modifies nobody's module - so the check was written instead, in
`tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts` (*"collapses two REVERSED copies of one segment, which a
direction-sensitive key would not"*), where it belongs because it is what **G218**'s inflation table
rests on. It asserts `collapsed: 1` over two reversed copies of one segment, and carries the control
that the same two segments on DIFFERENT nets are REFUSED rather than deduplicated - so the collapse
is keyed on the net as well as on the geometry, which the first half alone would not establish.

- **Why it is open** it is a measurement, and it is also a near miss worth keeping: the reason it
  was found is that a perturbation did nothing, and a perturbation that does nothing looks exactly
  like a check with no teeth.
- **What would settle it** nothing for the measurement. **The criterion it carried - *a change that
  makes `geometryKey` direction-sensitive fails a named check* - IS MET**, by the test named above.
  **What remains open is the explanation**, which is RELAYED: nothing has confirmed against
  `elkjs`'s router that the reversal comes from consecutive chain edges running in opposite
  directions. **MECHANISM, untried:** read the `ElkEdgeSection` provenance of one duplicate pair,
  which `tools/schgen/elk/diagnose.ts` already prints for a raise.

### G220 - `bendsPerEdge`'s DENOMINATOR is this repository's and NOT the spikes', so G96's 1.72 and 2.19-3.27 must not be compared against it

`lib/schgen/readability/measures.ts` defines an EDGE as **a maximal polyline of one net between two
nodes**, where a node is a point of that net whose degree is anything but two. That is the
graph-drawing sense of the phrase and it is the only one computable from a canonical topology, which
deliberately keeps no edge identity of its own - and it is also defined for a template-drawn block,
where there is no ELK graph at all.

**THE SPIKES DIVIDED BY SOMETHING ELSE.** **G96**'s figures - 1.72 for the representative probe,
2.19 to 3.27 over fourteen whole-circuit runs, *"0 of 14 beat the probe"* - divide ELK's own
`bendPoints` by ELK's own EDGE count, which for this backend is *"a net of degree n becomes n - 1
edges"* (`lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts`): a count of the two-terminal connections in the spanning chain,
not of the polylines the route came out as. **The two agree for a two-terminal net and diverge for
every other.**

**WHY THIS IS REGISTERED RATHER THAN LEFT TO A MODULE COMMENT.** §3.3's whole objection to a
composite score is that it *"would produce a number that looks cited"*. A `bends/edge` of 1.33
printed in this repository's render report, set beside a published 1.72, looks like a comparison and
is not one. The module comment says so; this entry is so that a reader who finds the two figures in
two different places finds the warning as well.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, while defining the measure.
- **Evidence** the two definitions read directly - `shapeOfNet` in
  `lib/schgen/readability/measures.ts` and `edgesForNet` in `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts`, whose own
  comment states *"a net of degree n becomes n - 1 edges"*. A check that could have failed:
  `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts` asserts a five-segment, four-corner single-net
  polyline measures **4 bends over 1 edge**, where the ELK denominator for the same route would be
  the number of chain edges that produced it - so the two are demonstrably different counts on a
  fixture.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for this repository's definition; the spike denominator is **RELAYED** from
  G96 and from `docs/schematic/generation-prior-art-third-pass.md` as that entry quotes them.
- **Why it is open** two figures with one name are in the tree and in the register, and nothing
  mechanical stops a later task putting them in one table.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: any report that prints a bends-per-edge figure states which
  denominator it used.** **MECHANISMS, untried, and they are alternatives rather than a plan:**
  rename the field to `bendsPerPolyline`, which would break the spec's own wording; or compute BOTH
  denominators and report them side by side, which is more honest and costs an ELK graph that a
  template-drawn block does not have. Neither has been tried.

### G221 - the generation manifest's DRAWING-identity claim covers 0 of 10 blocks on the only design that emits, and `canonicalNetlistSha256` is `null` on every design in the repository

Spec §2.1's manifest exists so *"four link checks that each pass prove nothing jointly unless they
ran over the same derivation"*. It now exists (`MANIFEST.json`, generated, committed, compared by
content). **Two of its six fields are empty or null for everything in this repository, and that is a
property of the inputs rather than a defect in the manifest - which is exactly why it is recorded.**

**`layoutInputSha256` IS EMPTY FOR `mini`.** `[RAN]` All ten of that design's blocks are drawn by
reviewed templates, so **none was handed to a layout backend** and the record has no entries. The
absence is meaningful - it means *no layout backend input*, never *no drawing* - and
`staleManifestInputs` reports a block appearing on one side and not the other in both directions, so
a block that starts or stops selecting ELK invalidates the manifest. **But the consequence stands:
on the only design in the repository that generates a schematic, the field that exists to stop two
different drawings being certified under one input hash covers nothing at all.** What identifies
`mini`'s drawing today is `sectionNetworkSha256` plus the template-library digest, and
`sectionNetworkSha256` is deliberately order-insensitive - so a reordering that moved a template's
output would be invisible to the manifest. Nothing is known about whether a template's output DOES
move under reordering; **G95**'s measurement is of ELK.

**AND THE OTHER HALF, ADDED IN TASK 16's FIX ROUND 1 AND RAISED BY THE REVIEW AS OUT OF SCOPE: NO
DESIGN's GENERATED OUTPUT IS COMMITTED ANYWHERE, so no manifest is ever present in a diff.**
`[RAN]` `git ls-files | grep -i MANIFEST.json` finds **one** file and it is
`tools/schgen/port-manifest.json`, which is not a generation manifest; `git ls-files | grep -i
RENDER-REPORT` finds **nothing**. The only design that emits is the ported `mini` fixture, whose
`outDir` is a temp scratch directory (`miniInScratch` in
`tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/run.ts`, registered with the temp-scratch sweep), so **the manifest and the four measures exist only inside temp directories
during a test run.** `CLAUDE.md` says a committed derived artifact earns its keep by being *"the
form in which a human's schematic edit becomes legible to an agent in a diff"*, and this one is
never in a diff. **The sentence in `lib/schgen/manifest.ts`'s `serializeManifest` comment - *"it is
a COMMITTED derived artifact, so it is written to be read in a diff"* - is therefore a statement
about how the bytes are FORMATTED and not about where they live today.**

**`canonicalNetlistSha256` IS `null` EVERYWHERE.** `DesignSpec` carries no canonical-netlist field.
`CLAUDE.md` says authority runs in both directions, and a canonical netlist export exists only for a
**schematic-first** circuit - the Pultec - which has no design module yet. So the null is a fact
about the designs; `staleManifestInputs` reports a design that gains or loses one, and the
`tests/schgen/manifest.test.ts` case for that is driven. **A reader seeing `null` in every manifest
needs to know which of the two it is**, which is why this is here rather than only in a comment.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, Step 5.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts` asserts
  `Object.keys(g.manifestSources.layoutInputs)` is `[]` for a real `generate` of `mini`, and
  `tests/schgen/manifest.test.ts` asserts `canonicalNetlistSha256` is null and that a netlist
  appearing is reported. A check that could have failed: that same file's *"reports a block whose
  layout input appeared or vanished"* case THROWS *"no block of the subject circuit reached the
  layout backend"* if `layoutInputs` is empty for the `transistor-preamp` parity circuit - so the
  empty result for `mini` is specific to `mini` rather than a function that always returns nothing.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran both.
- **Why it is open** the manifest's strongest field is inert on the only emitting design, and
  nothing says whether that matters: it would matter if a template's output moved under declaration
  reordering, and that has not been measured.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: for a design whose blocks are all template-drawn, something
  in the manifest moves when the drawing moves.** **MECHANISM, untried:** run G95's shuffle against
  a template-drawn design and see whether the emitted sheet changes at all; if it does not, the
  criterion is already met by `sectionNetworkSha256` and this entry resolves. **The criterion is the
  settlement; the mechanism is a measurement nobody has taken.**

  **FOR THE UNCOMMITTED-OUTPUT HALF: it BELONGS TO THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW and is nobody's fix
  inside Task 16, which has no design of its own to commit output for.** The review that raised it
  said so explicitly. **CRITERION, for whoever takes it: at least one design in this repository
  commits its generated set, so a manifest and a render report appear in a diff.** **MECHANISM,
  untried:** the first design this repository OWNS - which is the same trigger **G215**'s ruling
  R34 names, so the two land together or neither does. Committing `mini`'s output instead would
  commit a ported fixture's bytes, which is the objection R34 already sustained in another costume.
  - **Found** 2026-10-20 for this half, by the Task 16 review, and confirmed by the fix-round-1
    writer: the two `git ls-files` sweeps above were re-run here. **A check that could have failed:**
    the first sweep DOES match a file - `tools/schgen/port-manifest.json` - so it is not a grep that
    could only ever return nothing; what establishes the finding is that the one match is not a
    generation manifest.

### G222 - Task 16's deviations from its own brief, each with what it cost - including the one that was FORCED by a line ceiling and the one that cost a byte-check

Recorded for the reason **G213** was: a deviation nobody wrote down is a deviation the next reader
re-derives from scratch, or re-argues.

1. **`lib/schgen/readability/baseline.ts` is THREE files, not one.** Written as one it is just over
   **800 lines** against `CLAUDE.md`'s stated 300-500 ceiling. The seam is
   `tools/stripboard/approvals-*.ts`'s own and is not invented here - model, entry reader, registry
   front door. **Cost:** a reader following the brief's file list finds three files; the front door
   re-exports everything so nobody imports the parts.
2. **`compareMeasures` takes a FOURTH parameter and `MeasureComparison` carries a FOURTH field.**
   The brief declares three fields and three parameters, and separately requires that
   *"`compareMeasures` reports which of the two it is"* for G95's block-scale refinement. That
   classification is a function of the block's CELL COUNT, which neither a `ReadabilityBaseline` nor
   a `SchematicMeasures` carries, so the two requirements cannot both be met by the declared
   signature. **Cost:** every caller passes a cell count; the alternative - exporting `baselineScale`
   alone - would let a caller print four rows with no statement of which kind of baseline they came
   from, which is the precise thing the refinement exists to prevent.
3. **`tools/schgen/generated-files.ts` is DIVERGED, which costs its byte-check** against
   `digital-pedal-platform`'s `generateFiles.ts` permanently (**G139**'s loss, one file larger). The
   cheaper alternative was weighed and refused: `generate` could have added `MANIFEST.json` to the
   map `generatedFiles` returns, and it would have worked end to end, but `generatedFiles`'s
   contract is *the generated file set* and a second caller of it would then produce a set with no
   manifest in it. **Two places to keep correct in exchange for one byte-check.** The `sourceSha`
   watch on the other end of the line survives.
4. **The three `ownerWords` readings MOVED to `lib/owner-words.ts`.** The brief says to reuse
   `tools/stripboard/approvals-read.ts`'s three refusals rather than writing a fourth reader, and
   `lib/schgen/` **may not import from `tools/`** (the M1 plan's global constraint, stated in
   `lib/schgen/render/blocks.ts`). Reuse was therefore impossible where the readings lived. **Cost:**
   two stripboard modules now re-export rather than declare; nothing was widened, and
   `tests/stripboard/approvals-refusals.test.ts` passes unchanged, which is what makes the move
   checked rather than asserted.
5. **The modules were written BEFORE the tests, against the brief's Steps 1-4.** The measure
   definitions needed real geometry to pin - `bends`, `bendsPerEdge` and `occupiedArea` have no
   published values and the corpus had to be measured before an assertion could be written. **Cost:
   the tests were not seen to fail first**, and what replaces that guarantee is Step 8: twelve
   perturbations, eleven of which turned a named test red, and the twelfth replaced after it turned
   out to change nothing (**G219**). That is a weaker guarantee for the fixture-level tests and a
   stronger one for the corpus-level ones.
6. **`verify.ts` attaches the manifest's problems only to rows that would otherwise have NONE.**
   Spec §2.1's criterion is about a gate that *reports a pass*; a row already carrying a problem is
   already not one, and repeating the complaint on five rows would bury what actually failed.
   **Cost:** on a design whose gate 6 fails for its own reasons, the manifest complaint does not
   appear on that row - so `tests/schgen/verify.test.ts` identifies the passing gates from a CONTROL
   RUN rather than naming them, and asserts that the perturbed run leaves none.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, Steps 5 to 9.
- **Evidence** each deviation is stated in the module or manifest entry it affects - the three-file
  split in `baseline-model.ts`'s header, the fourth parameter in `compareMeasures`'s doc comment,
  the divergence in `tools/schgen/port-manifest.json`'s `diverged[]` entry with its `sourceSha`, the
  move in `tools/stripboard/approvals-words.ts`'s re-export comment. A check that could have failed
  for (3): `tests/schgen/port-fidelity.test.ts` refuses a file in two of the manifest's three lists
  and refuses a diverged entry with no reason, and both ran green only after the entry was written.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer made each deviation and ran each check.
- **Why it is open** (5) in particular: the fixture-level tests in
  `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts` were written against behaviour that already existed,
  so each one is a statement about what the code does rather than about what it should do. The
  perturbations are what distinguish those two, and they were run per test file rather than per
  assertion.
- **What would settle it** nothing for (1) to (4) and (6) - they are recorded decisions. For (5),
  **CRITERION: every assertion in that file fails when the behaviour it names is removed.**
  **MECHANISM, untried:** a per-assertion mutation sweep rather than a per-file one.

### G223 - the Task 16 brief's premise about G209's uncommitted direction-reversal figure is FALSE: it is in a committed file and it re-runs

The brief for this task states: *"G209's minor 6: the direction-reversal figure behind G200's '47% of
nets reverse direction on an axis' exists in no committed file - it was inherited from Task 13 and
nobody can re-run it. The other four G200 numbers reproduce exactly."*

**`[RAN]` It is committed and it re-runs.** `ShapeMeasures.reversing` is a field of `shapeMeasures`
in `lib/schgen/render/compose.ts`, and `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`'s *"G209's figures are
re-runnable"* asserts
`{ placements: 14, distinctX: 14, wiredNets: 19, reversing: 9, segments: 67, wire: 284_480 }` -
**six figures including the reversal, not five.** Task 15 round 2 landed it, and G209's own Evidence
section says so: *"ROUND 2 PUT THE MEASURE IN A COMMITTED FILE ... asserted against G200's six
figures by `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`, so a later reader can re-run it. Round 1's figures
were computed in a scratch script and were the only number in these entries nobody else could
reproduce."*

**So the brief was written against round 1's state of that entry.** The task was instructed to
decide whether the reversal measure *"falls out of"* the four measures and, if so, to commit it.
**The decision, and the reason:** it does NOT belong in the four, and it did not need committing.

- **It is not one of §3.3's four measures.** That table names bends, crossings between different
  nets, wire length and occupied area. Adding a fifth measure to `SchematicMeasures` would be this
  task widening the spec's measure set, which the brief forbids in as many words.
- **Taken over a canonical topology it would be UNSTABLE, and this is the part to read carefully
  because the obvious version of the argument is wrong.** A reversal is a property of a net's
  ROUTE DIRECTION: `shapeMeasures` reads the sign of each segment's displacement per net and asks
  whether both signs appear on one axis. A canonical topology's segments DO still carry a direction
  - `geometryKey` sorts the two ends only to build the deduplication KEY, and the surviving `Wire`
  keeps its own `a` and `b`. **What canonicalisation destroys is not direction but WHICH direction
  survives:** of two reversed duplicates it keeps whichever `canonicalTopology` met first, and
  **G219** measures that 82 of 82 duplicates are reversed pairs - so on the six blocks that have
  duplicates, the direction of every surviving segment is an artefact of encounter order. A
  reversal measure taken there would move when the iteration order did.
- **It already has the right home.** `shapeMeasures` is per block (**G209**: *"the number is a
  property of a block's interior and only of that"*), which is where G200 takes it.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16, checking the brief's premise before acting on it.
- **Evidence** `grep` is not the evidence - the field and the assertion were read directly, and
  `bun test tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts` runs them. A check that could have failed: the
  assertion is a `toEqual` over all six figures, so a reversal count that moved would turn it red
  naming the number.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer read both files and ran the test.
- **Why it is open** it is not a defect; it is a correction to a dispatch, recorded because **the
  same false premise could reach another dispatch.** The register entry it came from (G209) already
  carried the correction in its Evidence section, and the brief quoted the part of it that predates
  round 2.
- **What would settle it** nothing - it is settled. **A caution for whoever writes Task 17's
  brief:** G209 and G200 were both amended in place by later rounds, and a brief quoting them must
  quote the current text.

### G224 - THE GATE CENSUS, MANIFEST CITATION AND ALL, IS REACHED BY ONE TOOL AND BY THE TESTS - AND NOT BY `schgen check`, SO A USER AT THE CLI NEVER SEES A GATE NAME ITS DERIVATION

Spec §2.1's criterion is that *"a gate that reports a pass names the manifest it passed against"*.
Task 16 put `manifest` on every `GateResult`; its fix round 1 made `renderGateCensus` print it, so
the criterion is now met in an artifact a person reads. **This entry is the honest scope of that,
because the artifact is not one a user of the generator ever produces.**

`[CODE]` `tools/cli/schgen.ts`'s `runSchgen` has two verbs and **neither calls `runGates`**. `check`
calls `generate` and then `staleFiles`, and prints the stale list; `generate` calls `generate` and
then `writeGeneration`. `runGates` has exactly one non-test caller in the tree -
`tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`, which is run by hand (`bun run tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`) and by
`tests/schgen/gate-census.test.ts`.

**SO, PLAINLY: NO. A user running `bun run schgen check` or `bun run schgen generate` never sees a
gate's derivation citation.** What they do see is the `MANIFEST.json` FILE: `generate` writes it
into `outDir` as one of the generated files, and `check` compares it by content like every other
generated file and names it when it is stale. Those are gate 1's half - *this file differs* - and
not the half §2.1 added, which is *which input moved, attached to every gate that would otherwise
report a pass*.

**WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE.** Controller ruling **R37**, 2026-10-20: *"`schgen check` never calling
`runGates` at all is NOT yours to fix. It is Task 11's surface, the CLI plumbing question is larger
than a fix round, and re-plumbing it here would be scope you were not given."* Recorded rather than
argued, because the gap is not visible from either file on its own: `verify.ts` looks fully wired
and `schgen.ts` looks complete.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16 review, ruled R37; written up in fix round 1.
- **Evidence** `runSchgen` read directly - the `check` arm is six lines and `staleFiles` is the only
  gate-shaped thing in it - plus the census of `runGates` callers in the tree. **A check that could
  have failed:** the caller census is non-empty and finds a REAL production caller
  (`gate-census.ts`), so it is not a search that could only have returned tests; the finding is
  which caller is missing, not that there are none.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - the fix-round-1 writer read both files and re-ran the caller census. The
  ruling is RELAYED from the controller, verbatim above.
- **Why it is open** spec §2.1's criterion is met by a tool and by tests and by nothing a user
  invokes, and that is exactly the shape `CLAUDE.md` warns about in reverse: not a skipped check
  looking like a passing one, but a passing check nobody on the normal path runs.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a user who runs the repository's own front door against a
  design is told which derivation each gate ran against, or is told plainly that no gate ran.**
  **MECHANISMS, both untried and both larger than they look:** a third verb (`schgen verify`) that
  calls `runGates` and renders the census, which is the smallest edit and leaves `check` still
  looking like a gate runner it is not; or `check` calling `runGates` instead of `staleFiles`, which
  changes what `check` means and what it exits on, and `tests/cli/schgen.test.ts` pins the current
  meaning. **Neither has been tried and the choice is Task 11's surface, not this round's.**

### G225 - THE GENERATION PATH's REFUSAL SURFACE WIDENED INSIDE REPORT RENDERING: `generate` can now fail for a MEASUREMENT reason, attributed to the report rather than to a gate

`buildReport` calls `sheetMeasuresOf(d)` for every drawing (`lib/schgen/report.ts`), and
`sheetMeasuresOf` **throws** when `canonicalTopology` refuses the sheet's wires
(`lib/schgen/readability/measures.ts`): *"sheet `<id>`: the canonical topology of its wires was
refused (`<n>` ambiguous overlap(s)), so its four measures would be taken over a geometry with more
than one reading. It is refused rather than measured on one of them."* `buildReport` is called from
`generatedFiles`, which is called from `generate`. **So the path `generate` -> `generatedFiles` ->
`buildReport` -> `sheetMeasuresOf` can now refuse a generation for a reason that is a MEASUREMENT,
inside report rendering, and the message a user sees is attributed to the report rather than to any
gate.**

**THE REFUSAL ITSELF IS RIGHT AND IS NOT THE QUESTION.** Spec §1.4 revision 4 clause d is *refuse
rather than repair*: an ambiguous overlap has more than one reading and measuring one of them would
publish a number nobody can reproduce. **The question is whether its ATTRIBUTION is right** - a
geometry a generator will not certify arguably belongs to a geometric guard that says so as a gate,
not to the renderer of a diagnostics section - and that is an owner-visible design question rather
than a fix. **Nothing here moves or softens the throw.**

**REACHABILITY ON A REAL TEMPLATE-DRAWN SHEET IS NOT ESTABLISHED, which is why this is a recorded
observation rather than a defect.** `[RELAYED]` The Task 16 review DROVE the throw, with a
constructed cross-net collinear partial overlap, and got exactly the message above. It constructed
the case; nobody has produced one from a template. The two halves of why that is unresolved:

- An **ELK** block's wires are already canonicalised before they leave `adaptElkLayoutReported`
  (`lib/schgen/elk/adapt.ts`'s `pre` pass), and a block whose route is ambiguous is refused THERE,
  as an `invalidGeometry` mismatch naming the block - so an ELK sheet cannot carry an ambiguity into
  `sheetMeasuresOf`.
- A **template-drawn** block's wires are not canonicalised anywhere, and **G212** records that
  sheet-level geometry is not fully guarded: not one whole-sheet guard checks containment in a
  reference box, and the guards that do exist check pairwise straddling and clearance rather than
  collinear overlap across nets. **So nothing in the tree establishes that a template cannot draw
  the shape the review constructed.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, by the Task 16 review; written up in fix round 1 under the review's
  instruction to record rather than change.
- **Evidence** the call chain read directly (`generatedFiles` line `add("RENDER-REPORT.md",
  renderReport(buildReport(...)))`, `buildReport`'s `drawings.map`, `sheetMeasuresOf`'s `if (!t.ok)
  throw`), and the review's own probe quoted above. **A check that could have failed:** the ELK half
  is a claim that could be false and was checked - `adapt.ts` returns `invalidGeometry` on
  `!pre.ok`, so the ambiguity is caught before a drawing exists, which is why the live corpus does
  not hit this throw.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the call chain and for the ELK pre-pass refusal - this writer read
  all four modules. **RELAYED for the probe**: the review constructed and ran it; this writer did
  not reproduce it.
- **Why it is open** because the attribution is a decision nobody has taken, and because a
  generation that fails inside RENDER-REPORT rendering reads, to whoever runs it, as a reporting
  bug rather than as a refusal about their drawing.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a sheet whose wire topology has more than one reading is
  refused by something whose name says it is checking the geometry, and the message says which
  sheet and which overlap.** The second clause is already met; the first is not. **MECHANISMS, both
  untried:** canonicalise a template-drawn block's wires where an ELK block's are canonicalised, so
  the refusal lands on the block that drew it; or add the check to the whole-sheet guard
  neighbourhood (`assertSheetSafe`) and let `sheetMeasuresOf` assume a topology already proven
  unambiguous. **An owner decision about attribution is the other way this settles**, and it is not
  to be asked for unprompted.

### G226 - THE PATTERN, NAMED: a mechanism exercised only by its own tests, and the thing that distinguishes an acceptable instance from the G201 failure is whether the PRICE is recorded

**THREE TASKS HAVE NOW PRODUCED ONE EACH AND THE REGISTER HAD RECORDED TWO OF THREE.** The pattern,
in the Task 16 review's words, which controller ruling **R35** adopts as this entry's claim: **a
mechanism exercised only by its own tests is a mechanism whose first real use is its first test;
that is acceptable when the precondition for wiring it is NAMED and the price is RECORDED, and it is
the G201 failure when it is not.**

**THE DISTINGUISHING FEATURE IS NOT WHETHER THE THING IS WIRED. IT IS WHETHER THE GAP IS RECORDED
WITH ITS PRICE.** R35: *"the right name is not 'unwired'."*

| instance | state | recorded? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **G215** - `composeBlocks` and `interiorDrift`, Task 15 | deferred by ruling R34, with a named trigger (the first design this repository owns that has a composable sheet) | **YES, and it is the model**: *"§1.9's criterion is checked over two subjects by tests and over NOTHING by the pipeline"* is the deferral's price, and that entry says it is not to be softened |
| **G201** - `elkBackendFrom`'s stale refusal, Task 13 | unwired AND undeclared: the real pipeline could not emit a single ELK block for five rounds | **NO - this is the failure.** A test asserted `toThrow(/adaptElkLayout/)`, so the one check that would have caught it was pinning it. Nobody could see the gap, because nothing said it was there |
| **G217** residuals 1 and 2 - `compareMeasures` and `consultedBy`, Task 16 | **CORRECT BY DESIGN** and recorded: the registry ships empty by design, so every lookup is `absent` and a consumer would be code that cannot execute | **YES**, with the precondition named - the owner grants a baseline - and *"nobody is to ask him for one unprompted"* |
| **G245** - `validateSourcing`, Task 20 | **CORRECT BY DESIGN** and recorded: `bomFields` left `validateCircuit` under the owner's ruling that the BOM requirement belongs to the CONSUMER of an artifact, and this repository has no such consumer yet, so the composition runs in tests and in no pipeline | **YES**, with the precondition named in one sentence - *something here must emit an artifact a third party sources and places* - and the price stated: the rule is checked by two test files and by no artifact a person running `schgen` reaches. Controller ruling **R67** also rules the named composition is **not to be collapsed** into its test callers, because the name is what tells a future fabrication path what to call |

**R35 RULES THAT NO CONSUMER IS TO BE BUILT FOR `compareMeasures` OR `consultedBy`, and that a
reviewer would refuse one.** That is the ruling to read before "fixing" either.

**TASK 16 PRODUCED TWO MEMBERS THAT WERE IN NO ENTRY AT ALL, AND THEY ARE THE REASON THIS ENTRY
EXISTS.**

1. **SPEC §3.5's WHOLE FINDING CONTRACT IS DRIVEN BY ONE TEST FILE AND BY NOTHING ELSE.** `[RAN]`
   `parseFindings`, `ReadabilityFinding`, `FINDING_KEYS` and `FORBIDDEN_FINDING_KEYS` are declared
   in `lib/schgen/readability/finding.ts` and named in exactly one other file in the tree:
   `tests/schgen/readability/finding.test.ts`. **This is correct by design** - the M1 plan's
   obligation table maps both §3.5 rows to Task 16 alone, and **no M1 task builds the reviewer** the
   contract is for - but **G217** records the equivalent state for `compareMeasures` and
   `consultedBy` and nothing recorded it for the finding contract. The next agent to touch §3.5 had
   no way to learn that the whole contract rests on one test file. **The price: if that file is
   deleted, weakened or narrowed, §3.5's contract has no check at all and nothing else in the tree
   will notice.**
2. **`GateResult.manifest` WAS POPULATED, ASSERTED, AND RENDERED BY NOTHING, FOR A ROUND.**
   `runGates` set it on every row and `tests/schgen/verify.test.ts` asserted it; its only non-test
   consumer, `renderGateCensus`, dropped the field, so spec §2.1's criterion - *a gate that reports
   a pass NAMES the manifest it passed against* - was met in the data structure and in no artifact a
   person reads. **Fix round 1's item 3 fixed the rendering** (a derivation line per `ran` row,
   driven by `tests/schgen/gate-census.test.ts` on the content). The instance is recorded anyway,
   because the instance is that it shipped unrendered - a field nothing renders is a field whose
   first real use is its first test, and the whole task's point was that a gate must say what it
   graded against.

**WHAT THIS ENTRY ASKS OF A LATER TASK, since the pattern is now named rather than re-derived:**
when you build a mechanism nothing calls, say in the register which precondition would wire it and
what its absence costs. That is a sentence, and **G201** is what it costs to leave it out.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16 review (the lead question and its Important 5); written up in fix
  round 1 under ruling R35.
- **Evidence** the consumer census for member 1, run over `lib`, `tools` and `tests` for all four
  names, which returns the declaring module and one test file; the `renderGateCensus` body before

  failed:** the same census run for `compareMeasures` and `consultedBy` returns **thirteen** files
  against member 1's **two**, because those names are shared with the stripboard approvals and
  exemptions loaders - so the search discriminates rather than returning one file for everything,
  and member 1's result is a fact about §3.5's contract and not an artefact of how the census was
  run.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran both censuses and made the item 3 fix. **The pattern's
  statement is RELAYED from the review and adopted verbatim by R35**; the classification of G201,
  G215 and G217 into the table is this writer's reading of those three entries.
- **Why it is open** it is a recorded pattern rather than a defect, and it stays open because the
  thing that makes an instance acceptable - a recorded price - is a discipline no check enforces.
  Member 1 in particular remains in the state it describes: nothing but one test file drives §3.5's
  contract, and that is correct until the reviewer exists.
- **What would settle it** nothing for the pattern. **For member 1, CRITERION: §3.5's contract has
  a consumer that is not a test, or the register says why it does not.** The second half is now
  met; the first waits on the reviewer, which no M1 task builds. **MECHANISM, untried, and offered
  only to be refused clearly:** writing a reviewer-shaped consumer now would be a consumer with no
  reviewer behind it, which is the shape **R35** refuses for `compareMeasures` - so the honest
  settlement is a later milestone's, not a mechanism available here.

### G227 - `CanonicalTopology` IS AN UNBRANDED INTERFACE, so *"measures are taken over the canonical topology, never a raw segment list"* is a convention the type makes awkward rather than impossible - DEFERRED to the whole-branch review

`[CODE]` `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts` declares `CanonicalTopology` as a plain discriminated union:
an `ok: true` arm carrying `wires`, `branches`, `collapsed`, `zeroLength` and `contained`, and a
refusal arm. **There is no brand, no private symbol and no opaque witness**, so nothing at the type
level prevents a caller assembling an object of that shape from a raw `Wire[]` and handing it to
`measuresOf` - which is the one thing the whole measure design rests on NOT happening
(`lib/schgen/readability/measures.ts`: *"`measuresOf` takes a `CanonicalTopology` and not a
`Wire[]`"*, **G106**).

**IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE `verdict` FINDING - a type that makes the defect hard to write by
accident and trivial to write on purpose.** Writing it by accident is genuinely hard: the arm
requires five fields including two counts whose values a fabricator would have to invent, and
`assertPinsAgree` refuses a topology whose pin ends do not match the pins it is handed. Writing it
on purpose takes one object literal.

**DEFERRED, NOT DECLINED - controller ruling R36, 2026-10-20.** Branding the type touches every
caller **including the test helpers that deliberately construct one**, so it is a whole-branch edit
rather than a fix-round one, and it is deferred to the whole-branch review together with the
`verdict` finding it resembles. **The price of the deferral, stated so it is not read as a closed
question: until then, the rule that measures are taken over a canonical topology is held by the
signature's TYPE NAME and by review, and by nothing a compiler enforces.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16 review (its Minor 9); recorded in fix round 1 under R36.
- **Evidence** the type declaration read directly at `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts`, and
  `measuresOf`'s signature. **A check that could have failed:** the type DOES carry a real guard
  that could have made the finding false - `assertPinsAgree` - and it was read; it constrains a
  topology's pin ends against a pin list and says nothing about where the wires came from, so the
  finding survives contact with the one defence the module has.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer read the declaration and the guard. The ruling to defer is
  RELAYED from the controller (R36).
- **Why it is open** it is deferred with no trigger beyond the whole-branch review, and a deferral
  with no recorded price is the **G226** failure.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a caller cannot hand `measuresOf` a topology it assembled
  itself without the compiler objecting.** **MECHANISM, untried:** a brand - a private symbol field
  on the `ok: true` arm, with `canonicalTopology` the only producer and the test helpers routed
  through it rather than around it. **Its cost, which is why R36 deferred rather than ruled:** every
  deliberately-constructed fixture in the tests must then go through the real producer, which makes
  some fixtures harder to write and may make one or two impossible - and that is the trade the
  whole-branch review is to make, not this round.

### G228 - MEASURED AND FIXED: `templateLibrarySha256` did not move when a template's DRAWN GEOMETRY moved, and the fix OVER-COVERS on purpose

**THE DEFECT.** `libraryDigest` in `tools/schgen/generate.ts` hashed
`fs.readdirSync("lib/schgen/render/templates").filter(n => n.endsWith(".ts"))` - nine files,
one directory level. `[RAN]` **Eight of those nine import their geometry producers from the PARENT
directory**: `chain-kit.ts`, `layout-kit.ts`, `fanout-kit.ts`, `geometry.ts`, `drawn-extent.ts`,
`power-text.ts`, `text-boxes.ts`, `lib-pins.ts`. So an edit to `chain-kit.ts` changed a template's
drawn geometry and left `templateLibrarySha256` exactly where it was - **the failure the function's
own doc comment said it existed to prevent** (*"a digest over the ids would not move when a
template's GEOMETRY changed - a hash that cannot detect the thing it exists to detect"*).

**IT WAS A MIS-ATTRIBUTION RATHER THAN A BLIND SPOT IN THE GATE, AND THAT MATTERS FOR HOW ALARMED TO
BE.** The resulting output change was still caught by `generatedSha256` through gate 1's
`staleFiles`. What was wrong is what spec §2.1 asks the manifest to RECORD: the template library
version that graded the output, which was incomplete.

**AND A SECOND DEFECT, WORSE IN KIND: `readdirSync` IS NON-RECURSIVE AND THE FUNCTION REFUSED ONLY
AN EMPTY DIRECTORY.** Adding a subdirectory under `templates/` or `rules/` silently NARROWED the
digest with nothing failing - *"a skipped check must never look like a passing one"* in miniature,
inside the record whose whole job is to say what graded the output.

**THE FIX, AND THE MECHANISM CHOICE, because the mechanism matters to a later reader.** The function
is now `moduleTreeDigest(root, dir)` and hashes every `.ts` module in the directory **tree**, each
beside its path relative to the tree's root, and **the template library is the whole of
`lib/schgen/render` rather than `lib/schgen/render/templates`.** Two mechanisms were available and
the review had tried neither: the transitive import closure of the template modules, which is exact
and needs an import walker this repository does not have; and a wholesale directory hash, which is
cheaper and **OVER-COVERS**.

**THE OVER-COVERAGE IS THE CHOICE AND IS SAID OUT LOUD IN THE CODE, because a reader who later sees
the digest move for an unrelated reason needs to know that is by design rather than a bug.** An edit
anywhere in `render/` that changes no template's geometry moves `templateLibrarySha256`. That is a
false-positive staleness, which costs a regeneration; the alternative error is a false pass, which
certifies a drawing against a library version that did not draw it. **The two are not symmetric.**

**WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER.** `lib/schgen/rules/*.ts` import
`../render/geometry.ts` and `../render/library.ts`, so a geometry edit moves the TEMPLATE digest and
not the RULE digest even though it changed what the rules computed. Both fields are in one manifest
and `staleManifestInputs` reports either, so the manifest as a whole still goes stale - **the
mis-attribution is now between two fields of one record rather than a gap.**

**AND THE GENERATION PATH's REFUSAL SURFACE WIDENED AGAIN, which is the same class of thing G225
records.** Clause (b) of the fix round's criterion was that *adding a file the digest does not cover
cannot pass silently*, so `moduleTreeDigest` **refuses by name** any entry in the tree it cannot
hash, rather than filtering it out. **THE COST THE FIRST ROUND OF THIS FIX MEASURED, and it is a
real one: a stray non-`.ts` file under `lib/schgen/render/` or `lib/schgen/rules/` - a `.DS_Store`
from a Finder visit, an editor backup - refused every generation** until it was deleted. That round
took the position that there should be NO whitelist of ignorable names at all, on
`CLAUDE.md`'s *"an empty whitelist that refuses loudly beats a general rule that quietly accepts a
guess"*, and put the cost here rather than paying it silently.

**CONTROLLER RULING R43, 2026-10-20, PAYS IT THE OTHER WAY, AND THE FACT THAT DECIDED IT WAS
ALREADY COMMITTED.** The refusal stays as the general rule, with a **named exemption list holding
exactly one entry, `.DS_Store`** (`DIGEST_EXEMPT` in `tools/schgen/generate.ts`). The ruling:
**`.gitignore:20` already declares `.DS_Store` a non-artifact of this repository**, under its `OS
files` heading and by the same reasoning `.gitignore:54` applies to `*.kicad_prl` - per-user state,
never design data. Refusing a generation over it was *"two parts of the repository disagreeing"*,
and the owner is on macOS where a single Finder visit to a library directory arms it; a refusal that
says *delete the file your file manager made* teaches nothing about the circuit, which is not
`CLAUDE.md`'s standard for a refusal. **So the entry is a reading of an existing decision, not a
fresh judgement**, and that is why the code cites the `.gitignore` line.

**AND THE RULING CORRECTS A MISREADING THIS WRITER HAD OF `CLAUDE.md`, which is worth keeping
because it is a confusion anybody could repeat.** The first round treated a named list as a
FALLBACK. It is the opposite: **a fallback substitutes behaviour when something is missing, so the
UNKNOWN case passes; a named exemption list refuses everything not named, so the unknown case
REFUSES.** The sentence quoted above is not a grudging allowance for a whitelist - it is the
prescribed shape, and it specifies the default state (empty) and the extension discipline (a
deliberate edit with a test beside it, never a silent widening).

**THE OBJECTION THE FIRST ROUND RAISED - *"it would hide exactly the file somebody hid
deliberately"* - LOSES ON A FACT RATHER THAN ON TASTE.** Drawn geometry reaches a template through a
`.ts` import, and the digest now hashes every `.ts` in the tree recursively, so a geometry-bearing
`.json`, a `.ts.bak` or a vendored data file **still refuses by name under a one-entry list exactly
as it did under none**. The one-entry list loses nothing clause (b) was protecting.

**THE RESIDUAL COST OF R43, NAMED PLAINLY AND NOT TO BE SOFTENED: a file named exactly `.DS_Store`
that CARRIED GEOMETRY would be neither hashed nor refused.** That is the price of the direction
chosen. It is one name, it is exact (`.DS_Store.bak`, `foo.DS_Store` and a DIRECTORY called
`.DS_Store` all still refuse), and the judgement behind accepting it is R43's: if geometry hidden in
a file with that name is the threat model, **the digest is the wrong place to fight it.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 16 review (its Important 2); fixed in fix round 1.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/generate-digest.test.ts`, which copies the library tree to scratch,
  proves the copy digests identically to what `generate` hashes, then **mutates each of the eight
  geometry producers' bytes in the copy and asserts the digest moved** - a real perturbation, not a
  membership assertion - and asserts separately that each of the eight is NOT under `templates/`,
  which is the finding. **Three perturbations of the implementation, applied and restored:** making
  the walk non-recursive turns three named tests red; filtering the unhashable file instead of
  refusing turns one red; **reverting the directory to `templates/` turns ELEVEN red, including all
  eight geometry producers** - which is this entry's defect, reproduced as a failing check.
  **FOR R43's EXEMPTION, three more checks and three more perturbations:** an unexempted non-`.ts`
  file refuses by name; `.DS_Store` present does NOT refuse and does NOT move the digest; and the
  exemption is exact - `.DS_Store.bak`, `foo.DS_Store` and `.DS_Store` as a DIRECTORY each still
  refuse. The list's LENGTH is asserted, so growing it cannot be quiet, and a separate check reads
  `.gitignore` and fails if it stops declaring the name - which is what keeps the exemption a
  reading of a committed decision rather than this repository's own opinion. Driven, each restored:
  making the match a suffix test, and dropping the directory guard, each turn the exactness test
  red; removing the exemption skip turns the no-refusal test red naming both `.DS_Store` paths.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer made the fix, wrote the tests and drove all six
  perturbations. The eight-module import claim is the review's and was re-run here. **R43 is
  RELAYED from the controller; the `.gitignore` lines it rests on were read directly here** (line 20
  `.DS_Store`, line 54 `*.kicad_prl`).
- **Why it is open** the over-coverage is a recorded decision and the rule-digest attribution is a
  recorded limit; what keeps the entry open is R43's residual - a file named exactly `.DS_Store`
  carrying geometry is neither hashed nor refused - which nobody has hit and which no check can
  catch, by construction.
- **What would settle it** nothing for the fix - it is driven. **For the over-coverage, CRITERION:
  `templateLibrarySha256` moves when and only when something a template draws with has changed.**
  **MECHANISM, untried:** the transitive import closure, which needs an import walker; it is the
  exact answer and nobody has costed building one. **For R43's residual: nothing settles it inside
  this digest, and that is the ruling rather than a gap** - the criterion *a file that cannot carry
  geometry does not stop a generation, and a file that can is not skipped* cannot be met for a name
  the repository has declared empty of content, so one of the two clauses is chosen deliberately.
  R43 chose the first. **MECHANISM, untried and recorded only to be refused clearly:** reading the
  exempt file's bytes to check it really is Finder metadata would put a parser for a foreign binary
  format in the generation path, which is more surface than the residual is worth.

### G229 - MEASURED: the five blocks that draw, drawn as ONE flat graph, are REFUSED by the junction obligation - so the integrated experiment's flat side has no accepted drawing at all

`[RAN]` `tools/schgen/remeasure-composed.ts`'s flat probe puts the members of
`transistor-preamp`'s five drawing blocks into one `BlockSubgraph` and hands it to
the same `elkInputOf` -> `layoutBlocks` -> `adaptElkLayoutReported` chain every
declared block goes through. The 14-placement graph lays out, and then:

> *"block `tp-drawing-legs~flat`: the junctions the sheet emitter would place
> disagree with the branch points of the canonical topology in 1 place(s). For
> template geometry `junctionPoints` is cosmetic; for ELK geometry it is not,
> because a branch point with no junction is a connection KiCad does not make
> (spec 1.4 obligation 2). net BASE branches at (45.72, 48.26) (t-junction) and
> no junction is emitted"*

**THE CONSEQUENCE FOR TASK 17 STEP 4 IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS AN ENTRY.** The
integrated experiment's accepted-stage comparison therefore has **one side**: a
composed drawing, and a refusal. The experiment reports the flat side at the
`backend-output` stage instead - 1 crossing, 360.20 grid steps of wire, 38 bends -
and takes **no ratio** between stages. **G105** carries the figures.

**WHAT IT IS AND IS NOT EVIDENCE OF.** It is NOT evidence that a 14-placement
block cannot be drawn: `tp-stage` has 16 placements and is refused by a different
gate, and this probe's refusal is a SINGLE branch point of a single net. It IS
evidence that **the junction obligation is reached by a graph that the
clearance checks never see**, which is a gate ordering nothing had exercised: of
the twelve declared blocks, none is refused at obligation 2 (five fail
`checkLayout`, one fails the snap collapse, one fails the port-coordinate
comparison), so **this probe is the only subject in the repository that has ever
reached that arm with a real circuit in it.**

**AND IT IS A PROBE, WHICH IS LOAD-BEARING FOR HOW IT MAY BE READ.** Nothing in
this repository declares a five-leg block, `flatSubgraphOf` writes no declaration
and emits nothing, and the probe exists because controller ruling **R38** directs
the subject to be *"the five as one flat graph through the same backend"*. It is
the posture **G160** states for the anchor sweep: a brute-forced subject *"chooses
no arrangement, writes no declaration and emits nothing, so it is a measurement
rather than an authored criterion."*

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 Step 4, the first time a flat multi-block graph
  was put through the realization contract.
- **Evidence** the refusal above, verbatim, asserted in
  `tests/schgen/remeasure.test.ts` including the coordinate and the net name, so
  a change that moved the branch point or fixed the junction turns it red naming
  the figure. A check that could have failed: the same test asserts the
  `backend-output` stage of the same probe DOES produce figures, so the refusal is
  located at obligation 2 and not at the layout.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer built the probe, ran it and read the
  refusal.
- **Why it is open** nothing is fixed. A flat graph of five real blocks cannot be
  drawn by this pipeline, and whether that is a defect in `junctionProblems`, in
  `junctionPoints`, or in the route itself is undiagnosed: **this writer did not
  determine which of the two rules is wrong about (45.72, 48.26)**, only that they
  disagree there.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a branch point of a canonical topology
  and the junction set the sheet emitter would emit agree on every net of a graph
  this size, or the disagreement is attributed to one of the two rules by name.**
  **MECHANISMS, untried and they are alternatives:** read the two point sets at
  that coordinate and say which rule omits it - `junctionPoints` in
  `lib/schgen/render/connectivity.ts` is the ported cosmetic rule and
  `junctionProblems` in `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts` is the topology one, and
  **G197** records that those two already *"count a coincident PIN differently"*
  on the crystal template, which is the first place to look; or establish that the
  route itself brings three segments to a point no pin is at, which would make it
  a routing finding rather than a junction one. **Nothing here chooses between

### G230 - `docs/known-gaps.md` G216 PUBLISHES TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES UNDER THE NAME "cells" AND A THIRD UNDER "parts", and the spikes' ceiling is stated in the one it does not use

**Found while re-taking the ceiling, which is why it matters rather than being a
tidiness note.** The spikes' ceiling is stated in PARTS, `baselineScale` keys on
PLACEMENTS, and **G216**'s two tables use the word `cells` for both of two
different counts:

| where | the word | what it counts | `tp-leg-upper` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G216's block-scale table | `cells` | units PLACED | **3** |
| G216's D1 report line | `cells` | ELK graph CHILDREN: placed units plus zero-size boundary nodes | **5** |
| G216's D1 report line | `parts` | units, NOT distinct parts | 3, and `ob-buffer` **11** |
| `docs/schematic/template-parity.md` | `parts` | DISTINCT parts | `ob-buffer` **9** |

`[RAN]` **The `parts` discrepancy is real on 3 of the 12 declared blocks** -
`ob-buffer` 9 parts against 11 units, `oc-audio` 12 against 14, `oc-sidechain` 17
against 19 - because those three hold multi-unit packages. The other nine agree,
which is why it went unnoticed.

**WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC.** The spikes' ceiling is *"zero crossings on every
block of 8 PARTS or fewer"*, and `oc-sidechain` is 17 parts and 19 units. A
comparison that read G216's `parts` column would place three blocks at the wrong
size on the spike's own axis. `tools/schgen/remeasure.ts` therefore carries
`parts`, `units`, `geometry.placements` and `graphCells` as four separate fields
with a doc comment on each, and the re-measurement document prints all four.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 Step 3, while deciding which count to compare
  against the spike's `parts` column.
- **Evidence** the four counts measured per block and printed side by side by
  `tools/schgen/remeasure.ts`, asserted in `tests/schgen/remeasure.test.ts`; and
  `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts`'s two rows for `tp-leg-upper` -
  `cells=3` in one assertion and `cells=5` in the other - read directly. A check
  that could have failed: the four counts agree on nine of the twelve blocks, so
  the measurement discriminates rather than reporting a difference everywhere.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the four counts and for the two readings of `cells`
  in the test. **RELAYED for G216's published tables**, which were read rather
  than re-derived.
- **Why it is open** G216's tables are not edited by this entry. They are
  correct in their own terms and ambiguous across them, and a reader who takes
  either `cells` column for the other gets a wrong answer for three blocks.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: any figure printed against a block's SIZE
  names which count it is - distinct parts, units, placements, or graph cells.**
  **MECHANISM, untried:** renaming the fields in
  `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts`'s two report lines, which is a
  one-line change in a Task 16 file and was not made here because the figures are
  pinned by that test and a rename would move the pinned strings for no
  measurement gain.

**Why this entry exists:** the same shape as **G213** (Task 15) and **G222**
(Task 16). A deviation recorded only in a `.superpowers/` report is invisible to

A binary verdict would have published a comparison between different quantities. **Cost: none - the brief itself says to record a figure that cannot be compared** |

> | `Device:C` (`pt-core` `C7#1`) | 4064 x 2032 | x 0, y 7620 | 6350 x 5080 | **0 of 5** |
> | `Device:C_Polarized` (`tp-stage` `C3#1`) | 4572 x 3810 | x 0, y 7620 | 6350 x 5080 | **0 of 5** |

> 5080 um the grown pair needs, so none of its five inside slots can hold it** -
> which is **G239**'s finding for a 2032 um capacitor, unchanged by the different
> symbol. The jumper is drawn HORIZONTALLY (pin spread in x, not y) where the
> capacitors are vertical, so its pin-free sides are up and down rather than left
> and right; that rotates which slots are which and changes nothing about the
> count.

> KiCad's value field holds the part name"*, and `from-network.ts` hands it the
> RESOLVED lib id. **So this unit asks for nearly three times the horizontal room
> of G239's case, from a stated decision rather than from a defect.**

> **AND THE REASON PUBLISHED FOR NOT REPRODUCING THE OTHER HALF OF THE POSITIVE
> CONTROL WAS FALSE.** This entry said the reviewer's `STM32H743IITx` case was

> an STM32** (`declared.has(...)` is `false`), so it is not in the population the

> only the controller's question: **it is the same case, and on the width axis a
> worse one.** `docs/known-gaps.md` **G245** holds the measurement's context. **A scope decision taken on "9 of 12" as though
