> not mean that**, and the figure was published here before anybody had put the
> gate-1 refusal beside it. **G239** adds the other half: five of the eleven
> candidate field slots can never serve a small two-pin passive, so the first
> mechanism below has six positions to work with rather than eleven.

**THE SOLE-BLOCKER / PARTIAL-BLOCKER SPLIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS WHY THE
LEVERAGE IS 4 AND NOT 5.** `leverageOf` reports, per problem class, the blocks
whose ONLY blocker it is and the blocks it blocks alongside something else. **A
total would overstate it**: `body-label-overlap` appears on one block and is the
sole blocker of **zero**, so fixing it by itself moves nothing. Quoting a count
of blocks a class *appears on* as the number a fix unblocks is the error this
split exists to prevent.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say the field-placement routine is wrong -
`lib/schgen/render/field-placement.ts` is ported, reviewed and drawing the pedals
corpus - nor that the fix is small, nor where it belongs. It is plausible that
what is wrong is the ROUTE that leaves no room rather than the placement that
cannot find any, and **this writer did not determine which.** The two candidates
point at different modules and the entry names neither as the culprit.

**AND IT DOES NOT SAY THE OTHER TWO BLOCKS ARE CLOSE.** `oc-audio` and
`oc-sidechain` refuse at obligations 1 and 3, before any clearance check runs, so
**nothing has looked at their clearances** and their empty problem lists must not
be read as clean. Those two are **G185**'s and **G190**'s territory, not this
entry's.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17, while classifying the seven refusals for the
  re-measurement document; **recorded as its own entry under ruling R46** rather
  than left as a clause.
- **Evidence** the table, computed by `coverageCensus` and asserted row by row in
  `tests/schgen/remeasure.test.ts`, so it recomputes on every run and a block that
  started or stopped drawing moves it. **Checks that could have failed:** the
  sole-blocker and partial-blocker lists are asserted SEPARATELY, so a class that
  blocks nothing by itself cannot pass as leverage - and `body-label-overlap`'s
  sole-blocker list is asserted EMPTY, which is that check firing in the negative;
  `5 + 4 = 9` is asserted against the measured draw count rather than written as a
  sentence; and `classOf` **throws** for a problem text matching no known class,
  which is driven by a test, so a new `checkLayout` problem shape fails rather
  than being binned as *other* and quietly changing the leverage.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the census, ran it and read every
  problem string in full rather than the truncated forms that appear in a
  refusal message. **The first version of this finding, in the Task 17 report,
  said "four of the five checkLayout refusals are the same defect"; the measured
  statement is narrower and is the one above**: the defect is in 5 of 5 and is the
  SOLE blocker of 4.
- **Why it is open** nothing is fixed, by instruction. **The leverage is the
  reason it is open rather than closed as a measurement:** a one-defect fix that
  nearly doubles draw coverage is a scope question somebody has to answer, and
  until it is answered every figure in this register that rests on *"5 of 12
  blocks draw"* - **G200**, **G208**, **G209**, **G211**, **G216** and Task 17's
  own - is scoped to a corpus one fix would change.
- **What would settle it** **AN OWNER-VISIBLE SCOPE DECISION, which R46 is
  carrying to the final review: does M1 spend a task on draw coverage?** This
  entry is the evidence for it and does not answer it. **CRITERION if the answer
  is yes: a declared block whose parts are placed and whose route is legal has
  somewhere to print every designator and value, or the refusal names which of
  the two - the route or the placement - it attributes the failure to.**
  **MECHANISMS, untried and they are alternatives rather than a plan:** give
  `field-placement.ts` more candidate positions, which risks text where a reader
  does not expect it; or treat *"no room for the fields"* as a routing cost the
  backend should avoid, which means `lib/schgen/elk/` knowing about text and is a
  much larger change. **Nothing here chooses between them, and the criterion is
  what binds.** **AND THE LEVERAGE FIGURE DISCRIMINATES BETWEEN THEM, which is
  worth knowing before the scope decision:** *"9 of 12"* is exact for the first
  mechanism and is a ceiling rather than a count for the second, because the
  second moves geometry and re-opens four other obligations. **A scope decision
  taken on 9 of 12 is taking it on the field-local mechanism.**

### G233 - A PERTURBATION HARNESS THAT NAMES A TEST FILE SILENTLY NO-OPS WHEN THE ASSERTION MOVES, AND REPORTS THE RESULTING GREEN AS A PASSING DRIVE

**MEASURED HERE, TWICE, ONE LAYER APART.** A perturbation is how this repository
proves a check has teeth - *"a skipped check must never look like a passing
one"*. **A perturbation harness that names the test file to run is itself a
pointer, and it rots exactly as a prose pointer does.**

**WHAT HAPPENED.** Task 17's fix round 1 split the two scale-constant pins out of
`tests/schgen/remeasure.test.ts` into `tests/schgen/remeasure-ceiling.test.ts`.
The drive harness still named the old file. `[RAN]` Driving all four
perturbations against it:

| drive | against the stale file | against the file that holds the pin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCALE_INVARIANT_UPTO` 3 -> 2 | 22 pass / **1 fail**, pinning test NOT named | 6 pass / 2 fail, pinning test red |
| `SCALE_INVARIANT_UPTO` 3 -> 4 | 23 pass / **0 fail** | 6 pass / 2 fail, pinning test red |
| `SCALE_UNSTABLE_FROM` 8 -> 7 | 23 pass / **0 fail** | 7 pass / 1 fail, pinning test red |
| `SCALE_UNSTABLE_FROM` 8 -> 9 | 22 pass / **1 fail**, pinning test NOT named | 7 pass / 1 fail, pinning test red |

**TWO OF THE FOUR WERE GREEN AND THE OTHER TWO WERE RED FOR UNRELATED REASONS.**
That is the dangerous half: a harness that only checks *did something go red*
accepts a drive that reddened some other test, and **red for the wrong reason
reads exactly like a check with teeth.**

**AND THE SAME STALENESS REACHED THE REGISTER, which is how it was found a second
time.** Seven pointers in `docs/known-gaps.md` and in the modules named the old
file as the home of checks that had moved - including **G101**'s Evidence and
`BLOCK_SIZE.evidence`, both of which tell a reader which file verifies the two
bounds. `[RAN]` Perturb `SCALE_UNSTABLE_FROM` to 7 and run the file they named:
**23 pass / 0 fail.** The register was instructing a reader to verify a pinned
constant against a file that does not pin it.

**THREE HARDENINGS, EACH FROM A DISTINCT FAILURE, because the first two were not
enough.**

1. **the needle must be present.** An edit that matches nothing changes nothing
   and the suite is green. This fired for a different reason first: an unquoted
   shell variable in a `zsh` loop - which does not word-split - wrote
   `SCALE_UNSTABLE_FROM = 8 9 FROM-up8 7 FROM-down...` into the module, so four
   "drives" ran against one corrupted line. Caught by reading the diff;
2. **the named test file must contain the assertion being driven.** This is the
   defect above. The harness now refuses to start when it does not, naming the
   assertion it looked for;
3. **the named assertion must be the thing that went red.** `[RAN]` With this
   added, all four drives are valid: red, and red because the pinning test
   failed. Without it, the two drives that went red for unrelated reasons passed
   as valid.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 fix round 1, when two of four drives came back
  green; **re-found in the register** at fix round 2, item A, by the review.
- **Evidence** the table above, driven both ways on the same four perturbations,
  plus the register's own false green at 23 pass / 0 fail. **A check that could
  have failed and does:** `tests/schgen/pointers.test.ts` asserts, for each
  pointer that cites a measurement, that the cited file exists AND contains a
  fragment of the cited assertion's own title - and it is driven in both
  directions: reverting `BLOCK_SIZE.evidence`'s pointer to the old file turns it
  red (2 failures), and moving the pin's title out of the cited file turns it red
  (3 failures) saying the assertion has moved.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every row of the table, both drive
  arms and both perturbations of the pointer guard. **The register half was found
  by the Task 17 review and the figure 23 pass / 0 fail was re-measured here.**
- **Why it is open** **the pointer guard covers well under a tenth of the
  population, and stating that as a bare count was itself misleading - twice.**
  Round 2 published a count that read like a population; round 3 replaced it with
  a literal **269 citations across 262 lines** that was **already stale at the
  commit which published it**, because that commit's own insertion changed it.
  Measured per revision: `4ba4260` 268/261, `38ff473` 269/262, `0039872`
  **270/263**, HEAD higher again. **So no literal is published here any more.**
  `[RAN]` The count is now computed by `citationCount` in
  `tests/schgen/pointers.test.ts` on every run, which asserts the coverage
  FRACTION is under a tenth rather than any exact numerator; the register holds a
  few hundred citations and the guard holds **17 rows - 13 register rows, 2 module
  comments and 2 document lines** (Task 18 added the tenth to thirteenth register
  rows - **G239**, **G240**, **G241**, and R61's guard after ruling R62 moved it to
  another file - and the second document line).
  `[RELAYED]` The review puts roughly **120** of
  those citations in evidentiary positions. Round 2's
  *"covers the ten pointers that cite a measurement"* reads as if ten were the
  population - it is the sample. **What the guard does guarantee is narrower and
  worth having: every pointer fix round 2 repaired is under it** - all seven since
  fix round 3, which `tests/schgen/pointers.test.ts` asserts by citation, so a
  later repair that forgets a row fails. **Every other prose reference to a test
  file in this repository can still rot silently.** **And the harness itself is a
  scratchpad throwaway** - `.superpowers/` is gitignored and the script is not
  committed - so the three hardenings survive only as this entry. The next agent
  writing one has to read this rather than inherit it.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a perturbation is reported as a valid
  drive only when the named assertion is the thing that failed, and a citation of
  a test file fails a check when the assertion it names is no longer there.** The
  second half is met for the pointers the guard covers - twelve rows, listed in
  `POINTERS` - and unmet everywhere else.
  **MECHANISMS, untried:** extend `POINTERS` as entries are written, which is
  cheap and manual; or derive the pointers mechanically by scanning for
  `tests/.*\.test\.ts` in the register and requiring each to carry a marker in a
  declared format, which needs a convention nobody has written and would flag
  every passing mention. **The first is what is happening; the second is the one
  that would actually close this.**

### G234 - A BATCH EDIT SCRIPT THAT ASSERTS A LATER NEEDLE CAN RAISE BEFORE ITS WRITE AND DISCARD EARLIER REPLACEMENTS IN THE SAME RUN - and the reason nobody noticed is that three people checked the figures and not the prose

**MEASURED HERE, AND THE COST WAS TWO REGISTER EDITS REPORTED AS LANDED AND
ABSENT FROM DISK.** This is **G233**'s class one layer over: that entry records a
PERTURBATION harness that silently no-ops, and this one records an EDIT script
that silently discards.

**THE SHAPE.** A script applies several replacements to one file, asserting each
needle is present, and writes the file at the end:

```
s = s.replace(old1, new1)      applied in memory
assert old2 in s               <- raises here
s = s.replace(old2, new2)
open(p, "w").write(s)          never reached
```

**The first replacement is lost without a trace.** The script reports an
`AssertionError` about the SECOND edit, which reads as *"one edit did not apply"*
and is acted on as such - a follow-up script fixes the second edit and nobody
re-checks the first. **Nothing in the output says the earlier replacement was
discarded**, because from the script's point of view it never happened.

**WHAT IT COST, at Task 17 fix round 1.** Two edits to **G100** were reported to
the controller as landed and were not on disk: its **Evidence** paragraph still
described the superseded assertion (*"asserts the edge counts of both circuits as
EQUALITIES"*, naming a test file and a check that the corrected re-take had
replaced), and its **Verified** line was missing the statement that this writer
re-measured 69 and 48 independently and agreed to the edge. Both were applied at
fix round 2 in `bb532aa`, in the same change that fixed the stale pointers -
which is how they were found at all.

**HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND THIS IS THE CLAUSE A LATER AGENT MOST NEEDS.** It was
found by **READING THE PROSE** while editing a pointer in the same paragraph -
not by any check and not by re-reading the figures.

> **VERIFYING A REGISTER FIX BY ITS FIGURES IS NOT VERIFYING IT.** Three readers
> checked round 1 - the implementer, the re-reviewer and the controller - and
> **all three checked the numbers.** The numbers were right the whole time, which
> is exactly why nobody read the sentences around them. A register entry's claim
> lives in its prose: which file holds the check, what the check could have
> failed on, whether a figure is CONFIRMED or RELAYED. **None of that is a
> number, and none of it is covered by verifying the numbers.**

**THE SHAPE NOW USED, and it is two rules rather than one.** Every edit script in
this task since fix round 2: **reports a miss per edit** - printing `ok` or `MISS`
for each, continuing rather than aborting - **and writes each file exactly once**,
after all replacements for it have been attempted. It exits non-zero at the end
when anything missed, so a partial application is loud and complete. The scripts
are scratchpad throwaways, so the shape survives only as this entry.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 fix round 2, while repairing an unrelated pointer
  in the same paragraph. **Not found by a check** - there is none that would.
- **Evidence** the two restored edits are in `bb532aa`'s diff against
  `docs/known-gaps.md`, and their absence beforehand is visible as the same diff's
  removal of the superseded Evidence text. **A check that could have failed and
  did not, which is the point of recording this:** the Task 17 re-review searched
  five ways for other reported-as-landed edits missing from disk, including a
  mechanical sweep of all **4,664 added prose lines** across the task that
  resolved every backticked path and identifier against disk, **and found none**.
  So the damage was bounded at two edits - but it was bounded by a sweep nobody
  runs routinely, not by anything in the workflow.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer caused the defect, found it, applied both
  recovered edits and changed the script shape. **The five-way sweep that bounded
  it is RELAYED from the re-review and was not re-executed here.**
- **Why it is open** nothing mechanical prevents it. The script shape is a habit
  carried in prose, the scripts themselves are not committed, and **the
  figures-not-prose reading failure has no guard at all** - it is the kind of
  thing only a reader catches.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a change that reports an edit as applied
  has the applied text checked against disk before it is reported.** **MECHANISMS,
  one tried and one untried.** Tried and in use: the report-a-miss-per-edit,
  write-once shape above, which makes a partial application loud - it does not
  make a WRONG report impossible, only unlikely. Untried: have the edit script
  re-read each file after writing and assert every `new` string is present, which
  is cheap and would turn *"reported as landed"* into a checked claim; it was not
  done here because the scripts are throwaways and the habit was the cheaper fix.
  **Neither addresses the prose-versus-figures half, and nothing proposed does.**

### G235 - THE PATTERN, NAMED: a change whose PRIMARY effect is correct and whose COLLATERAL effect is wrong, so a reviewer checking the changed behaviour passes it - three instances in one task, all three found by reading the whole diff

**RULING R48, AND IT IS THE IMPLEMENTER's OBSERVATION RATHER THAN THE REVIEW's.**
Each of the three instances below is already recorded individually. **What was
not recorded is that they are one shape**, and an entry that only re-listed them
would add nothing - so this one names the shape, states the property that made
all three invisible to the obvious check, and says what might catch the next one.

**AND THE CIRCUMSTANCE OF ITS OWN WRITING IS EVIDENCE FOR G234, which is why it
is recorded here rather than left as a remark.** The implementer put this pattern
in a hand-back message to the controller and **did not write it down** - **one
message after writing G234**, the entry about exactly that failure. The
controller's words: *"you told me something interesting and did not write it down
- which is exactly what G234 is about, one message after you wrote G234. That is
not a criticism; it is the strongest possible evidence that G234 generalises."*
**So G234 is not about register fixes specifically. It is about anything
interesting that reaches a human before it reaches a file.**

**THE SHAPE.** A change has a primary effect and a collateral one. **The primary
effect is correct; the collateral effect is wrong; and every check anyone would
naturally run is a check of the primary effect.** A reviewer reading the changed
behaviour - *did the fix fix the thing?* - passes it. The defect is visible only
to someone reading the WHOLE change for what else it moved.

**THE THREE INSTANCES, with what each one's primary effect was and what its
collateral effect broke.**

| instance | the primary effect, correct | the collateral effect, wrong | what it broke | found by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flatSubgraphOf` spreading `{...c, blocks}` (Task 17, `2d0a003`) | a `BlockSubgraph` over the union of several blocks' members - it built one, and it laid out | `Circuit.unitBlock` was not rebuilt, so `labelledNets` still saw the original split | **the headline figure and its direction**: the flat control inherited the decomposition it was controlling for, and 1.000x was one artefact cancelling another. Corrected to 0.958x / 0.906x, **ADDS** rather than removes (**G100**) | the review, round 1 item 1(c) |
| splitting the pinning assertions into `remeasure-ceiling.test.ts` (fix round 1, `83c4042`) | the split itself - `remeasure.test.ts` was at 526 lines against `CLAUDE.md`'s cap, and the split was the right remedy | seven pointers in the register and the modules kept naming the old file | **the register instructed a reader to verify a pinned constant against a file that does not pin it, and the verification came back 23 pass / 0 fail** (**G233**) | the review, round 2 item A |
| extracting `crossingNets` so `governingNetsOf` could reuse it (fix round 2, `7977ea4`) | the extraction - two functions needed one traversal, and sharing it was right | `crossingNonRailNets`'s `Array.sort()` became a `localeCompare` comparator nothing had asked for | **nothing published, yet**: membership and every list were unchanged, but both lists are compared with `toEqual` and the two orders differ on `["AB", "A_B"]` - a latent shift in a published figure (**G100**) | the review, round 3 item 3 |
| taking `bomFields` out of the drawing path (Task 20, **G245**) | the split itself - the owner's ruling is implemented, and `transistor-preamp` went from 101 gate-1 problems to **0** | the gate census's `transistor-preamp` row stopped reporting the CIRCUIT and started reporting a HARNESS artifact (a missing `refs.lock.json`, because `runGates` forces `initLock: false`), on a non-deterministic temp path | **the committed census became LESS informative for the one circuit the change unblocked**, and a reader comparing censuses across the commit sees the refusal MOVE from 101 to 1 rather than disappear - whose obvious reading is that the fix did not work | the implementer, driving the census after the change; **parked under ruling R68** |

> **THE FOURTH ROW IS FROM A DIFFERENT TASK AND WAS FOUND A DIFFERENT WAY, so the
> title's "three instances in one task" is the original naming rather than the
> current count** (added under ruling **R68**, Task 20). It matters because it
> varies the one claim below that is about detection: all three original
> instances were found **by the reviewing agent reading the whole diff**, and the
> fourth was found **by the implementer RUNNING THE TOOL the change affected** and
> reading its output - `CLAUDE.md`'s *"look at the output, not only the tests"*,
> which no diff read would have produced because the census output is not in the
> diff. **So the pattern now has two detection routes rather than one**, and the
> second is cheaper than it looks: re-run the committed measurement tools after a
> change and read them, not only the suite.

**WHAT THE THREE HAVE IN COMMON, which is the useful part.** In every case **the
thing the change was for worked**. The flat probe produced a subgraph that laid
out; the split brought the file under the cap; the extraction removed a duplicated
traversal. **So the natural check passed in all three** - and in the third case
the whole suite passed, because nothing asserted the quantity that moved. **All
three were found by someone reading the whole change rather than the changed
behaviour, and all three were found by the reviewing agent rather than by the
implementer.**

> **A CORRECTION TO THE RULING THAT COMMISSIONED THIS ENTRY.** R48 says *"two of
> the three were found by a reviewer rather than by you."* **It is three of
> three.** Round 1's item 1(c), round 2's item A and round 3's item 3 were each
> brought by the review; the implementer found the pattern, and the separate
> lost-edit defect of **G234**, but none of these three. The correction makes the
> finding slightly worse rather than better, which is why it is here.

**ONE HONEST DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE INSTANCES, because forcing three into one
mould would be the kind of tidiness this register distrusts.** Instances two and
three are collateral damage from a STRUCTURAL EDIT made in service of something
else. Instance one is **stale DERIVED STATE on a copied record** - a different
mechanism of error. **What all three share is the DETECTION property, not the
cause**, and the detection property is what the entry is about.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 fix round 3, by the implementer, after the third
  instance was reported by the review. **Named as a pattern under ruling R48**,
  on the precedent that *"built, tested and unwired"* earned one entry after
  three instances rather than being discovered a fourth time.
- **Evidence** the three rows above, each traceable to a commit and to the entry
  that records it individually - `2d0a003` and **G100**'s correction block,
  `83c4042` and **G233**, `7977ea4` and **G100**'s *"what was and was not
  touched"* block. **A check that could have failed and did not:** the Task 17
  re-review swept all **4,664** added prose lines of the task resolving every
  backticked path and identifier against disk, looking for a fourth instance of
  this class in the documentation, and found none - so three is the measured
  count for this task and not a floor anybody has reason to raise. `[RELAYED]`
  that sweep is the re-review's and was not re-executed here.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - the implementer caused all three, and read each
  instance's own entry while writing this one. **The attribution of each
  discovery is read off the three fix-round briefs**, which name the reviewer as
  the source in each case.
- **Why it is open** **OPEN, and the reason is specific: the pattern is recorded
  and no mechanism for catching the next one has any evidence behind it.** Three
  are proposed below and **none has been tested**. The entry would be resolvable
  if one of them were measured against a fourth instance, and manufacturing a
  fourth instance to test it is not something to do deliberately. **What is
  settled is the shape; what is open is the remedy.**
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a mechanism that catches a collateral
  change whose primary change is correct, with evidence that it does - not an
  instruction to be careful.** Three candidates, **all UNTRIED**:

  **(a) the controller's, R48:** *read the full diff of a fix for collateral
  change rather than reading the fix.* **Evidence: suggestive and not a
  measurement** - all three were in fact caught that way, by reviewers. **Its
  weakness, stated because R48 asks not to be taken as settled: it is
  attention-based**, it tells a reader to look without telling them what for, and
  the implementer read each of these diffs too.

  **(b) the implementer's alternative, which is the one with the best odds on two
  of the three instances:** *for every structural change made in service of a
  fix, NAME the observable quantity it could move, and assert that quantity in
  the same change.* It produces an artefact instead of relying on attention, and
  it is what both later fixes actually did once the defect was known - the order
  pin for instance three, `tests/schgen/pointers.test.ts` for instance two.
  **What it would and would not have caught, stated rather than claimed:** it
  catches instance three cleanly (*extracting a function that returns a sorted
  list* names the order) and instance two cleanly (*splitting a test file* names
  what cites it); on instance one it **degrades to "know your data model"**,
  because naming the quantity requires already knowing that `unitBlock` derives
  from `blocks`, which is precisely the knowledge that was missing. **So: 2 of 3,
  and honest about the third.**

  **(c) narrow, for instance one's class only:** make a `Circuit` copied with a
  field overridden rebuild every field derived from it, so `{...c, blocks}` is
  not reachable. **It is a code change and R48 forbids one for this entry**, so
  it is recorded and not built; it would also need someone to decide where
  derived-field knowledge lives, which is a generator design question and not
  this task's.

  **None of the three addresses the half that worries the implementer most: that
  the natural check passing is what makes this class safe to ship.** A mechanism
  that only improves reading does not change that.

### G236 - MEASURED: the order pin written to catch a reintroduced comparator CANNOT catch it, because both published lists are FIXED POINTS of both orders - the third check-that-cannot-fail on this task

**THE BEST CATCH ON TASK 17, AND IT IS THE REVIEW's.** Fix round 3 reverted an
unintended `localeCompare` comparator (**G100**, **G235**) and added an assertion
described - in the test, in the commit body and in the register - as making *"a
comparator reintroduced into either function fail here"*. **That statement was
false.**

`[RAN]` The review put `localeCompare` back into **BOTH** name-returning
functions - where it has to go to do harm, since the shared `crossingNets`
helper's two `.sort()` calls erase a comparator placed there - and measured:

| the tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| clean | 3593 pass / 0 fail / 41,913 `expect()` |
| **both comparators reintroduced** | **3593 pass / 0 fail / 41,913 `expect()` - identical** |
| that one test file, comparators reintroduced | **14 pass / 0 fail** |

**THE CAUSE: both published lists are fixed points of both comparators.**
`expect(x).toEqual([...x].sort())` can only fail when the function's own order
differs from default-sorted order. Divergence between the two comparators needs a
`_` adjacent to an alphanumeric in a particular position - `_` is 0x5F, which
sorts AFTER letters and digits by code unit and BEFORE them under ICU collation.
**Neither published list has such a pair**: `OUT_PRE, VBIAS, VBIAS_RAW` and
`BASE, BYPASS_CAP, BYPASS_JUMPED, COLLECTOR, EMITTER` come out identically under
both orders, so the assertion compares a list against itself.

**IT IS NOT VACUOUS IN GENERAL, AND THE THREE PERTURBATIONS ARE NOT
INTERCHANGEABLE - which this entry's first version got wrong.** `[RAN]` Each
comparator put into BOTH name-returning functions, this round:

| comparator | that test file | does the fixture test fail? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a.localeCompare(b)` - locale ascending, the one the pin was written for | 14 pass / 1 fail | **yes** |
| `(a, b) => b.localeCompare(a)` - locale REVERSAL | 13 pass / 2 fail | **NO - it passes** |
| code-unit descending | 12 pass / 3 fail | **yes** |

**So the order assertion catches locale-reversal and code-unit descending and
misses the locale ascending it was built for** - which is the only comparator ever
actually introduced here. **And the 12/3 figure this entry first published belongs
to code-unit descending, not to the review's locale-reversal**: under reversal the
fixture pair comes out `BYPASSED, BYPASS_CAP`, identical to default order, so the
fixture test passes. **G237** records that mis-attribution.

**WHAT WAS DONE, and both halves of the criterion were taken rather than one.**

1. **THE CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN WHEREVER IT APPEARED.** The test's doc comment now
   states what the assertion catches (a reversing comparator, with the figure) and
   what it cannot (a collation comparator on these nets). **G100**'s statement
   points here instead of implying the pin is sufficient. `38ff473`'s commit body
   carries the superseded claim and cannot be edited, which is why this entry
   exists;
2. **A CHECK THAT CAN FAIL WAS ADDED, and it does.** `[RAN]` It drives both
   name-returning functions over a `blockCircuit` fixture whose two crossing
   non-rail nets are a pair the two comparators order differently, and under the
   reintroduced comparator it reddens: **14 pass / 1 fail, the failing test being
   the one built for it.**

**THE DIVERGING SHAPE IS COMPUTED, NOT GUESSED, and that is deliberate.** `[RAN]`
A sweep over the **216** names `A` + three characters from `{A, B, Z, 0, 9, _}` -
all `NET_NAME`-legal - found **7,740** of the **23,220** pairs diverging. **The
candidate set is defined here because the sweep script is NOT committed**, so a
later reader must rebuild it from that definition rather than re-run it; the
figures were re-driven in fix round 6 and rest on that run.

**AND THE ONE-THIRD IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A CURIOSITY.** 7,740 is
exactly `23,220 / 3`, which the review noticed and left undiagnosed. `[RAN]` It is
**`2/n` for an n-character alphabet containing one `_`**, because two names
diverge **exactly when the first position at which they differ holds `_` in one
and an alphanumeric in the other** - and given that two such names differ, that
first differing position carries a uniformly distributed unordered pair of
distinct characters, of which `n - 1` of the `C(n, 2)` include the `_`. Driven on
four alphabet and length combinations, where the diverging count and the
first-differing-position count agree exactly every time: **6 chars / len 3 =
7,740 of 23,220; 6 / len 2 = 210 of 630; 4 / len 3 = 1,008 of 2,016 (a half);
5 / len 3 = 3,100 of 7,750 (two fifths).** **So the one third is an artefact of a
six-character alphabet with one underscore in it, and says nothing about net
names.** **The pair is ONE REAL NET AND ONE CONSTRUCTED NAME, and it had to
be:** `BYPASS_CAP` is a real `transistor-preamp` net and **`BYPASSED` is not a net
of any circuit here.** `[RAN]` Over all **153** pairs of that circuit's **18**
declared nets, **0 diverge** - `BYPASS_CAP` against `BYPASS_JUMPED` included - so
**no two real nets would have served** and the term is one the real corpus cannot
drive. The test asserts the divergence before relying on it. **An earlier figure
on this task was guessed and a test caught it** (the five-leg union's edge count,
14 guessed against 24 measured), and **the sentence this paragraph replaces was
itself a claim that did not reproduce** - it called `BYPASSED` a real net - which
is **G237**.

**THE FIXTURE IS TEST DATA IN TEST CODE AND NOT A HAND-BUILT OBJECT.**
`blockCircuit` goes through `buildCircuit`, and each `external` net gets a peer
resistor in a second block, so both nets genuinely cross a block boundary and
neither is a rail - which is what puts them in the governing set. **The real
corpus cannot drive this term**: no declared circuit here has a diverging pair,
which is the same *"the term under test was zero"* shape that justified the
fixtures in `tests/schgen/readability/measures.test.ts`.

**THIS IS THE THIRD CHECK-THAT-CANNOT-FAIL ON THIS TASK**, after the `x !== x`
tautology in `adaptElkLayoutReported`'s counts assertion (**G218**-era, recorded
in `lib/schgen/elk/adapt.ts`) and the window loop that would pass over nothing
with adjacent bounds (fix round 1, item 2). **`CLAUDE.md`: evidence must be a
check that could have failed, and a skipped check must never look like a passing
one.** Three instances in one task - **four, counting the one inside the test
written to fix this third** (**G237**) - says the rule is easy to satisfy in
appearance.

**AND THE DISCLOSURE THAT BELONGS IN THE ACTIVE VOICE, BECAUSE IT IS THE CLAUSE A
LATER AGENT NEEDS AND IT ALMOST DID NOT GET RECORDED.** The implementer's own
account, in the implementer's own words rather than as *"someone believed it had
teeth"*:

> **I claimed a drive I never performed.** My fix-round-3 report stated that the
> order pin made *"a comparator reintroduced into either function fail here"*.
> **I drove the revert and I never drove the pin.** Had I driven it once, in the
> same action as the claim, I would have seen 14 pass / 0 fail and the sentence
> would never have been written. **And all four checks-that-cannot-fail on this
> task are mine** - the `x !== x` counts assertion, the window loop with adjacent
> bounds, this order pin, and the entailed `not.toEqual` inside the test I wrote
> to fix it.

**This disclosure reached the controller in a hand-back message and sat in a
gitignored report for a full round before being recorded**, which is **G234**'s
failure for the third time on this task and is why the passive construction above
is called out rather than quietly rewritten.

**FIVE SMALLER FINDINGS FROM THE SAME REVIEW, recorded here rather than in five
entries because each is one sentence and they share a cause - a correction landing
in one place while a second place keeps the superseded text.**

| finding | what it was | fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| three statements attributed a **THREE**-clause sentence to round 1, which published **TWO** | one was two lines below the title the fixing commit rewrote; one was the round-2 review's nit, **which survived because the brief labelled it a nit** | all three; no file contradicts itself on the point now |
| **G233**'s *"met for the ten pointers"* survived nine lines below the paragraph that replaced the count | inside the very commit that was fixing that count | names the twelve rows and points at `POINTERS` |
| the coverage breakdown was wrong **by composition** in both homes | *"10 register lines and 2 module comments"* folded the document line into the register; it is **9 / 2 / 1** | corrected, and the guard now ASSERTS the composition so prose cannot drift from it |
| the review's **~120** evidentiary estimate was adopted inside a `[RAN]`-marked sentence | a relayed estimate presented as measured here - the attribution failure this register exists to prevent | marked `[RELAYED]`, outside the measured clause |
| the **269/262** citation literal was **stale at the commit that published it** | counted before that commit's own insertion, which took the register to 270/263; per revision: `4ba4260` 268/261, `38ff473` 269/262, `0039872` **270/263**, later higher | **no literal is published any more** - see the ruling below |

**RULING, FROM THE CONTROLLER, AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS FIGURE: a literal
citation count published in the register rots on every register edit, including
the edit that publishes it.** The remedy taken is the stronger of the two offered:

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 fix round 5, by the review, which drove the
  comparator reintroduction rather than reading the assertion.
- **Evidence** the three-row table above, re-driven here before anything was

  and this bullet did not, which is **this entry's own defect class inside this
  entry** - a right number under a wrong label, in a sentence whose point was
  that the claim is measured. **The check that
  could have failed and now does:** the fixture assertion reddens at 14 pass / 1

- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer re-drove the comparator reintroduction, the
  reversing contrast, the fixture check's red, and the per-revision citation

  which is **RELAYED**.
- **Why it is open** **RESOLVED for the pin and OPEN for the class.** The specific

- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a new assertion is accompanied by a drive

### G237 - THE PATTERN THAT SURVIVED FIVE ROUNDS OF FIXING: three times on this task a prose claim about the author's OWN drive did not reproduce, and a wrong sentence about a drive passes every test in the suite

**THIS IS THE SIBLING OF G235 AND G236 AND IT IS THE ONE THAT KEPT GOING.**
**G235** names collateral change - a correct primary effect with a wrong secondary
one. **G236** names the check that cannot fail. This names the third and most
durable: **a claim IN PROSE about a measurement the author performed, where the
measurement was sound and the sentence describing it was not.**

**WHY IT OUTLIVED FIVE FIX ROUNDS: nothing can catch it.** A can't-fail check can
be caught by driving it. Collateral change can be caught by reading the whole
diff. **A wrong sentence about a drive passes `bun test`, passes `tsc`, passes the
suite, and passes a reviewer who checks the numbers** - because the numbers are
usually right. It is caught only by someone re-performing the drive the sentence
describes.

**THE THREE INSTANCES, each driven and each corrected in a later round.**

| round | the claim | what was actually true | found by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | the order pin means *"a comparator reintroduced into either function fails here"* | `[RAN]` **14 pass / 0 fail**: both published lists are fixed points of both comparators, so the assertion compared a list against itself (**G236**) | the round-5 review |
| 5 | `BYPASS_CAP` and `BYPASSED` are *"two real `transistor-preamp` net names"* | `[RAN]` `BYPASSED` is **not a net of any circuit here**. Of all **153** pairs of that circuit's **18** nets, **0 diverge**, so the name HAD to be constructed - which is a better fact than the false one | the round-6 review |
| 5 | a reversing comparator gives *"12 pass / 3 fail ... which also fails under reversal"* | `[RAN]` **the review's locale-reversal gives 13 pass / 2 fail and the fixture test PASSES.** 12/3 is CODE-UNIT DESCENDING, a different perturbation | the round-6 review |

**ALL THREE SENTENCES SAT INSIDE PARAGRAPHS ABOUT RIGOUR**, which is the part
worth noticing. The first was the sentence claiming a check had teeth. The second
was three lines above *"an earlier figure on this task was guessed and a test
caught it; this one is derived"* - inside a paragraph headed *"THE DIVERGING PAIR
IS COMPUTED, NOT GUESSED"*. The third was marked `[RAN]`. **A rigour claim is
exactly where this defect is least likely to be re-checked**, because the
paragraph tells the reader it already was.

**THIS ROUND's OTHER FINDINGS, recorded here because each is one sentence and all
five share the shape above or G236's.**

| finding | what it was | fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a **fourth** home of the clause-count attribution defect, eight lines from where the previous round edited | said the *"THREE-clause SENTENCE predicts 5"*; `[RAN]` with `BASE` off-sheet the **TWO**-clause set is **5** and the THREE-clause set is **4**, so the sentence predicting 5 is the two-clause one | corrected, and the drive is now `[RAN]` in that module rather than `[RELAYED]` - it is the repository's only record of the clause-(3) falsifier |
| the composition guard's third clause was **arithmetic on literals** | `POINTERS.length - 9 - 1 === 2` asserted only that `POINTERS` has twelve rows; swapping a module row for a document row left it **1 pass / 0 fail** while its message *"2 module comments"* became false | counts the module-comment citers instead. `[RAN]` the same swap now gives **14 pass / 2 fail** |
| the **fourth** check that cannot fail, inside the test written to fix the third | `expect(byDefault).not.toEqual(byCollation)` is entailed by the two literal assertions above it and could never be the cause of a failure | now a comment, which is what it always was |
| **G233**'s *"whitelist of ten pointers"* in **G231** | true at fix round 2; the guard has held twelve since fix round 3 | corrected |
| the sweep's **216 / 7,740** figures were unreproducible - candidate set undefined, script uncommitted | a `[RAN]` figure a later reader cannot re-drive | the candidate set is now DEFINED in **G236** (`A` plus three characters from `{A, B, Z, 0, 9, _}`) and the figures were re-driven this round; **the script is still not committed and the entry says so** |

**ONE THING THE REVIEW LEFT UNDIAGNOSED IS NOW ESTABLISHED, and it is recorded as
established rather than as a curiosity.** 7,740 is exactly `C(216, 2) / 3`.
`[RAN]` The cause: two names diverge **exactly when the first position at which
they differ holds `_` in one and an alphanumeric in the other**, so the diverging
share is `(n - 1) / C(n, 2) = 2/n` for an n-character alphabet containing one
`_`. Driven on four alphabet-and-length combinations, with the diverging count
and the first-differing-position count agreeing exactly every time: **6 chars,
length 3 - 7,740 of 23,220 (a third); 6 chars, length 2 - 210 of 630; 4 chars -
1,008 of 2,016 (a half); 5 chars - 3,100 of 7,750 (two fifths).** **So the one
third is an artefact of a six-character alphabet with one underscore in it and

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 17 fix round 6, by the controller naming the pattern

- **Evidence** the three-row table, every figure in it driven in fix round 6

  one, so the measurement discriminates between perturbations rather than

- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer caused all three instances, drove all
  three corrections and pasted the outputs into the task report. **The discovery
  of instances two and three is the round-6 review's; instance one's is the

- **Why it is open** **OPEN, and more firmly than G235 or G236.** Those two have

- **What would settle it** **CRITERION, imposed by the controller for fix round 6
  and the candidate remedy: a `[RAN]` mark means the stated numbers reproduce
  under the stated perturbation, and a number that cannot be driven in the same
  action is not written.** **MARK IT UNTRIED.** It was followed for one round -
  this one - and that is not evidence it works: **the same author has now failed
  three discipline-based remedies on this task** (drive every new assertion;
  report a miss per edit; read the whole diff), so a fourth stated as prose
  deserves the same doubt. **MECHANISMS, both untried and neither cheap:** a
  convention that every `[RAN]` figure carries the command that produces it, so a
  reader can re-run rather than re-derive - which does not stop a wrong number,
  only shortens the path to catching one; or review that re-performs every drive a
  change claims, which is what actually caught all three and is the reviewer's
  cost rather than a mechanism. **Nothing here converts this into something a
  check can catch, and that is the finding.**

**THIS IS TASK 18's STEP 0, ORDERED BY THE CONTROLLER AS A DELIVERABLE IN ITS OWN
RIGHT**, on the grounds that *"what stands between the generator and this
repository's own circuits is something a later reader cannot re-derive"*. **It
corrects the controller's own reading, which was offered as a hypothesis to be
measured rather than trusted.**

schematic declares ONE block, `pt-core`, and `pt-core` is on that sole-blocker
list. **So pt2399-core may become generatable if and only if the field-placement
defect is fixed.**"* It is false in both directions. Fixing the field-placement
defect would NOT make `pt2399-core` generatable, and the field-placement defect
is not what stands in the way.

single block reaches a layout backend.** `[RAN]` `bun tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`:

| `opamp-buffer` | 40 | 1 header; 3 pinsDeclared (**G151**); 36 bomFields |

`generate` calls `validateCircuit` and throws on a non-empty problem list
(`tools/schgen/generate.ts`, the `circuit is invalid:` raise), and `realiseBlock`

`layoutSheet`. **So every block-level measurement in G232 describes a stage
neither reference's generation reaches.** Gates 3, 6 and 8 all cascade to

**AND THOSE REFUSALS ARE NOT TO BE RELAXED, which is why this is a wall rather

invented BOM fields - and no backend invents an input"*. **G149**, **G150**,
**G151** and **G159** each record one class, and each says the refusal IS the
measurement. Closing them is authoring work on the circuits - real BOM fields,
real net names - not a defect fix in the generator.

(`tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts`) and a literal inside

`DesignSpec` per parity circuit from the authoring declaration through
`circuitSpecFrom`, and `gateCensus` already drives the real `runGates` over it.
That is how the table above was measured. **So the generated side of gate 8 is
blocked by the four authoring classes and not by a missing design module**, and
writing a design module would add nothing a later reader could use.

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR GATE 8's M1 HALF, stated here because the consequence is
this entry's whole point.** Gate 8 compares a GENERATED schematic against a
hand-arranged one. The reference half is fully available for both references -
both drawings are committed, both have a committed s-expression netlist
(`tests/fixtures/pt2399-core.net`, `tests/fixtures/transistor-preamp-lab.net`),
and `kicad-cli` exports either on demand. **The generated half is available for
neither.** Controller ruling R51 governs that case, and **G240** records what
was built under it with the price of its not having run.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 18 Step 0, by running the two committed censuses

### G239 - MEASURED: FIVE of the eleven candidate field slots can NEVER serve a small two-pin passive, so G232's "give it more candidate positions" mechanism starts from six usable slots and not eleven

**THIS ANSWERS HALF OF WHAT G232 LEFT OPEN AND NOT THE WHOLE QUESTION.** That
entry says: *"It is plausible that what is wrong is the ROUTE that leaves no room
rather than the placement that cannot find any, and this writer did not determine
which."* This does not determine which either. **What it measures is the size of
the search space the placement mechanism has to work in**, which is the number
G232's first mechanism - *give `field-placement.ts` more candidate positions* -
would be starting from, and it is smaller than the code's candidate list makes it
look.

> **AMENDED 2026-10-21 BY TASK 21: THIS ENTRY'S ARITHMETIC IS INTACT AND ITS
> CONCLUSION - "THE FIX IS NOT NARROW" - WAS WRONG, because a narrow fix existed
> outside the two mechanisms this entry and G232 were choosing between.** The
> owner asked whether an extremely long label is pathological. It is: a Value
> that is nothing but the symbol's own part name repeats the glyph beside it, so
> it is now emitted hidden and needs no slot (**G257**). **That is neither *more
> candidate positions* nor *a routing cost* - it is REQUIRING LESS**, and
> neither this entry nor **G232** considered it in two rounds of measuring the
> search space.
>
> **WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO THE FIGURES HERE, driven rather than
> reasoned** (`[RAN]`, the same inside-slot arithmetic over the installed stock
> libraries, with the value drawn and with it hidden):
>
> | symbol | value | grown pair, drawn | grown pair, hidden | inside slots that fit |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `Jumper:Jumper_2_Open` (body 5080 x 2286) | `Jumper_2_Open` | 17780 x 5080 | **7620 x 2540** | **0 of 5 either way** |
> | `Device:C` (body 4064 x 2032) | `100nF` | 7620 x 5080 | 6350 x 2540 | **0 of 5 either way** |
> | `Device:C_Polarized` (body 4572 x 3810) | `4.7uF` | 7620 x 5080 | 6350 x 2540 | **0 of 5 either way** |
> | `Audio:PT2399` (body 20320 x 30480) | `PT2399` | 8890 x 5080 | 6350 x 2540 | **5 of 5 either way** - the positive control, and it could have moved |
>
> **THE FIVE INSIDE SLOTS ARE STILL UNUSABLE FOR THE JUMPER, HIDDEN VALUE AND
> ALL**: the Reference box alone is `2 x GRID = 2540 um` tall once grown, against
> a 2286 um body. **So this entry's five-of-eleven finding survives the fix
> completely** - what the fix moved is the SIX OUTSIDE candidates, where a slot
> whose Value row was crossed is now usable because there is no Value row to
> cross. The capacitor rows are the cases this fix cannot help at all: `100nF`
> and `4.7uF` are electrical parameters that must be drawn.
>
> **AND THE BLOCKER TABLE ABOVE IS NOW PARTLY HISTORICAL.** For
> `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` `JP5#1` it listed `wire 4 (EMITTER)`, `pin RV6.1
> text`, `label EMITTER`, `label BYPASS_CAP` - and after the fix that unit
> PLACES, so at least one of its six outside candidates now has a clear
> REFERENCE row. **Which of those four obstacles was blocking only the Value row
> was NOT re-measured**, and this writer is not inferring it: the instrumentation
> that produced that table was never committed. The two capacitor rows are
> unaffected and were not re-driven.

**THE ARITHMETIC.** `candidates()` offers eleven slots for a vertical two-pin
passive: two pin-free sides, five inside the body, four beside the outermost
pins. `slotFields` stacks the Reference one `GRID` above the slot's centre and
the Value one `GRID` below it, `textBox` gives each line a height of `GRID`, and
`tryPlaceFields` grows both by `MARGIN = GRID / 2`. **So the grown pair is
`4 x GRID = 5080 um` tall at every slot.** An inside slot is taken only when both
grown boxes lie STRICTLY within the unit's own body, and **`Fix:C`'s body is
`2032 um` tall** - the same height as `Device:C`'s body as placed in `pt-core`,
measured as `{minX: 90678, minY: 59944, maxX: 94742, maxY: 61976}`. **No inside
slot can hold the pair, at any route, for any symbol whose body is shorter than
`4 x GRID`.**

**SO A SMALL TWO-PIN PASSIVE HAS SIX USABLE CANDIDATES, ALL SIX OUTSIDE THE BODY
WHERE THE ROUTE CAN REACH THEM.** On the three units that refuse in this
repository, all six are blocked, and `[MEASURED, by temporary instrumentation of
`blockerOf`, NOT COMMITTED]` by what:

| unit | the six outside candidates' blockers |
| --- | --- |
| `pt-core` `C7#1` (`Device:C`) | right slot and both right-hand beside-pin slots: `wire 70`/`wire 69 (Net-(C7-Pad1))` - **C7's OWN net**; left slot and both left-hand beside-pin slots: `wire 77 (Net-(C8-Pad2))` |
| `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` `JP5#1` (`Jumper:Jumper_2_Open`) | `wire 4 (EMITTER)`, `pin RV6.1 text`, `label EMITTER`, `label BYPASS_CAP` |
| `tp-stage` `C3#1` (`Device:C_Polarized`) | `wire 3 (BASE)`, `wire 2 (BASE)`, `wire 19 (EMITTER)`, `body of R6#1` (twice) |

**That table is the part of this entry that is NOT backed by a committed check**,
and it is marked as such rather than dropped: `blockerOf` and `candidates` are
private to `lib/schgen/render/field-placement.ts`, and exporting them to measure
them would be a structural change to a ported-and-diverged module in service of a
diagnostic - the shape **G235** names. It is re-derivable by printing
`candidates(p)` with `blockerOf(c)` from the `cand === undefined` arm of
`tryPlaceFields` and running `tools/schgen/remeasure-coverage.ts`.

**WHAT IS BACKED BY A COMMITTED CHECK is the five-of-eleven finding**, in
`tests/schgen/render/field-slots.test.ts`.

> **THE JUMPER IN THAT TABLE IS THE SAME CASE AS THE CAPACITORS, MEASURED AFTER
> TASK 20 MADE IT THE ONE THAT MATTERS** (controller question, Task 20 review).
> `JP5#1 (Jumper:Jumper_2_Open)` is now the SOLE blocker of `transistor-preamp`'s
> generation - **G232**, **G245** - so whether its geometry escapes this entry's
> arithmetic was worth asking. It does not. `[RAN]` **body 5080 x 2286 um against
> the 5080 um the grown pair needs: 0 of 5 inside slots fit**, exactly as for
> `Device:C`'s 2032 um body, with `Device:C` and `Device:C_Polarized` driven as
> controls in the same run. The jumper is drawn horizontally rather than
> vertically, which rotates which sides are pin-free and changes no count. **On
> width it is the HARDER instance: its grown pair is 17780 um against the
> capacitors' 6350**, because a jumper has no electrical parameter and `valueFor`
> therefore puts the symbol's part name - `Jumper_2_Open`, thirteen characters -
> in the value field. **So this entry's "the fix is not narrow" conclusion covers
> the blocking unit too**, and nothing about the jumper makes it the cheap case.

> **CORRECTED 2026-10-21 UNDER RULING R59: THIS ENTRY CITED THE WRONG CASE AS ITS
> SHARPEST, AND THE FINDING IS SOUND ANYWAY.** It said the sharpest case was the
> THIRD - *"only the SIX OUTSIDE candidates are blocked and the unit still
> refuses"*. **That case is not sensitive to the 5080-into-2032 arithmetic at
> all.** `[RAN]`, with a control that passes (**3 pass / 0 fail**): removing the
> inside-containment check from `field-placement.ts` entirely - the
> `if (inside && !within(b, p.body))` arm - leaves **all three cases GREEN**,
> because the inside slots are independently blocked by the symbol's own interior
> graphics, so the containment arm is never the thing that rejects them.
>
> **THE ARITHMETIC IS PINNED BY CASE ONE**, which is this entry's actual evidence.
> `[RAN]` setting `MARGIN` to zero so the grown pair is `3 x GRID` instead of
> `4 x GRID`: case one goes **RED**, `Expected: 5080  Received: 3810`, and the two
> other cases stay green. **So the number this entry publishes has a check that
> fails when the number moves, and the over-claim was only about which case it
> is.**
>
> **WHAT CASE THREE DOES PIN, stated accurately rather than dropped:** that a
> refusal needs **all six** outside candidates blocked - `[RAN]` blocking only
> five leaves the unit placed and the case goes red - so it holds the size of the
> usable candidate SET. It does not hold the REASON the inside five are unusable.
> Two different claims, two different cases, and this entry had them crossed.

The wires in case three are derived from the candidate geometry rather than
written as coordinates, so a change to `slotFields` or `besidePinFields` moves
them with it.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 18 Step 0, while establishing whether controller

- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/render/field-slots.test.ts`, three cases, 19
  assertions. **Every one of them was driven RED once before being relied on**:

- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the test, drove all ten
  perturbations and read the instrumented blocker table in full. **The blocker

- **Why it is open** **it is a measurement, and it is open because the thing it
  was taken for was declined.** R49 put the field-placement fix in scope as a
  prerequisite *if* a reference were blocked only by it, with the condition that

  So a fix is either a new KIND of candidate position, which is a placement

- **What would settle it** nothing settles the measurement; it is true. **For the

  candidate placed further out along a pin-free side, at increasing offsets, is

  not expect it"* cost G232 already names.

### G240 - GATE 8's M1 COMPARISON IS BUILT, DRIVEN AND WIRED, AND HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST A GENERATED DRAWING - the fourth instance of G226's pattern in this plan

**RECORDED UNDER CONTROLLER RULING R51, which is explicit about what this entry
is for:** *"say plainly, in the document and in the register, that the gate is
built and has never run against a human-trusted drawing, and what stands in the
way. **That is a worse outcome than exercising it and it is an honest one.**"*

**WHAT IS BUILT.** `lib/schgen/gates/reference-graph.ts` reduces a netlist to
components keyed by canonical value and library id plus the unordered pin pairs
of every net; `lib/schgen/gates/graph-match.ts` compares two such graphs;
`lib/schgen/gates/declared-delta.ts` holds a permitted-delta declaration to its
rules; `oscarGate` in `tools/schgen/verify.ts` runs the comparison per declared
reference and refuses loudly on every arm that cannot proceed.

**WHAT IT HAS RUN ON.** Two real hand-arranged drawings, through the real
`kicad-cli`: `pt2399-core` (24 components, 117 pin-to-pin pairs) and
`transistor-preamp` lab-board (32, 150). **On NO generated schematic.**

**WHY, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A SEQUENCING ARGUMENT.** **G238**:
`generate` refuses both references at gate 1, on 115 and 101 `validateCircuit`
problems, before any block reaches a layout backend. The gate's subject - *a
generated drawing* - does not exist for either reference, and no design in this
repository declares `oscar`, so `oscarGate`'s comparison is reachable only from
`tests/schgen/gates/reference-graph.kicad.test.ts`.

> **AMENDED 2026-10-21 BY TASK 20: ONE OF THE TWO REFERENCES NO LONGER REFUSES AT
> GATE 1, AND THE GATE IS STILL UNREACHABLE.** Under the owner's ruling that the

**THE PRICE, which is what G226 asks for rather than the fact.** The gate exists
to catch a defect class the round trip structurally cannot: *a generator that
mangles a circuit the same way at both ends passes a round trip happily.*
**Until it runs on a generated drawing, that defect class is unguarded in this
repository**, and nothing else in the suite covers it - the round trip
(`tests/schgen/gates/round-trip.kicad.test.ts`) is self-consistency by
construction and its own module comment says it must never be reported as this
check. So what is unexercised is not a convenience; it is the only check of its
kind.

**AND WHAT WAS NOT DONE INSTEAD, because it is the tempting thing.** Running the
empty-delta check against the ported `mini` fixture would have produced a green
gate 8. R50 forbids it: *"`mini` is a ported fixture with no hand-arranged
schematic a human trusts, and the gate's entire premise is that it proves the
generated drawing matches a drawing a human made and trusts... Substituting the
fixture would produce a green gate that checks self-consistency, which is the
round trip wearing gate 8's name."*

**THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF G226's PATTERN IN THIS PLAN** - *a mechanism
exercised only by its own tests* - and that entry's distinguishing test is
whether the precondition is named and the price recorded, which is what the two
paragraphs above do. The three before it are **G215** (`composeBlocks`),
**G217**'s residuals (`compareMeasures`, `consultedBy`) and §3.5's finding
contract. Citing it rather than re-deriving it is R51's instruction.

- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the gate, ran the censuses behind

### G241 - MEASURED: TWO STAGES OF THE GATE-8 MATCHER COULD BE PERTURBED OUT OF EXISTENCE WITH THE WHOLE SUITE STAYING GREEN; one is RESTORED AND NOW GUARDED after the urgency figure behind it was withdrawn by its own author; and a probe without a passing control proved nothing FIVE times, across two authors

**THIS IS G236's CLASS, FOUND BY THE DISCIPLINE G236 ASKED FOR, and both findings
are this writer's own code.** The controller imposed *"drive every new assertion
red once before you rely on it"* on Task 18 directly. Doing it to the
implementation rather than to the assertions found two stages nothing in the
repository depended on, and **the measurements are what got them deleted rather
than documented.**

> **REVERSED 2026-10-21 UNDER RULING R57 AND SETTLED UNDER R61: THE REFINEMENT IS
> RESTORED AND IS NOW GUARDED. The justification below is left standing because it
> is where the gap was, and the gap was real.** Deleted in `f57c5dd`, restored in
> `586ab53`.
>
> **THE DIAGNOSIS THAT GOT IT RESTORED, AND IT IS CORRECT.** The deletion's three
> measurements are all true and all about **a MATCHING symmetric pair, which is
> the EASY case.** The worst case for a backtracking search is **a symmetric pair
> that does NOT match**, and the deletion never measured one - this entry's own
> words, *"Every case matched (ok=true) under both"*, are the admission. So
> *"it can only ever prune a search that would have reached the same verdict"* is
> **true of `ok` and false of what is REPORTED**, and that sentence is the one
> this entry got wrong.
>
> **WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, in three numbers.**
>
> 1. **On inputs `graphFromNetlist` can produce, the budget first exhausts at 120
>    nodes** - `[RAN]` `topology differs` (STATED) at 24, 32, 36, 48, 72 and 96
>    nodes, and *"did not complete"* first at 120 (176 ms). That is **3.75x the
>    larger reference**, not below it, and it is the figure of record for how
>    urgent this is.
> 2. **The only construction on which the refinement changes what is reported is a
>    hand-built graph the netlist path cannot produce**, and on it the difference
>    is stark: `[RAN]` with the refinement **a stated difference at 0.2 ms** at 12
>    through 18 nodes; without it, **402 ms stated at 12 nodes and COULD NOT
>    FINISH at 14, 16, 18 and 20** (391-469 ms), self-match controls MATCHED under
>    both.
> 3. **The reason the cheap arm always wins first, which is the generalisation and
>    is the review's:** **pin-labelled connection signatures are sensitive to
>    ORIENTATION**, and both a pad transposition and a fitting flip are orientation
>    changes - while **a net expands to a CLIQUE** over its members. So in any real
>    netlist an orientation change moves the connection multiset and is caught
>    before the search is reached.
>
> **THE 14-NODE URGENCY IS WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR**, and that is recorded as the

> `graphFromNetlist` cannot emit that shape, because a rail is a NET and a net

>
> | construction | pin-labelled connection census |

> | `hub(10)` flip=true | `(1-1) x10  (1-2) x10` - **identical, so the cheap arm is blind** |
> | `clique(10)` flip=false | `(1-1) x45  (2-2) x45` |

> `[RAN]` under the clique shape - what a netlist really produces for that circuit

> **AND IT NAMED ITS OWN ERROR: it hand-built a `ReferenceGraph` and treated it as

> `tests/schgen/gates/graph-match.test.ts` now holds the hub construction as a

> with the refinement removed: RED, 3672 pass / 3 fail** - the 14-, 16- and

>
> **THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE SURVIVES THIS INSTANCE AND IS UPHELD, AND THE INSTANCE
> TURNED OUT BENIGN - both halves, because an entry that records only the scare
> teaches the wrong lesson.** The principle: **"no check fails when I remove this"
> is not sufficient grounds to delete something whose absence changes WHAT IS
> REPORTED in a case nobody has measured.** It is **better evidenced** by this
> episode, not worse: the original deletion's justification was true on reachable
> inputs, the uncovered case existed, and it simply lay outside the netlist path -
> which nobody knew until somebody built it. **And the benign half matters just as
> much: the gap was not live, the 120-node threshold is the operational figure,

> **MARK THE PRINCIPLE's REMEDY UNTRIED.** There is no evidence a stated principle
> stops a future deletion: the three discipline-based remedies on this branch have
