> actually protects the refinement now is the test, not the principle.**

**ONE: THE COLOUR REFINEMENT.** `graph-match.ts` refined each node's signature
from its neighbourhood until the partition stopped growing, compressing the
signatures each round over the union of both sides. Three measurements:

1. `[RAN]` perturbing the whole loop to `for (let round = 0; round < 0; ...)`:
   **30 pass / 0 fail** over the unit and `kicad` gate tests, both real
   references included. Nothing depended on it.
2. It is a bijection INVARIANT, so a class mismatch always implies no bijection
   exists. **It can only prune a search that would have reached the same
   verdict** - it cannot pass something the search would refuse.
3. `[RAN]` timed with the loop enabled and disabled, over all five cases
   measured - both real references, a twelve-resistor chain, and parallel
   resistor ladders of ten and fourteen identical parts, which are the worst
   case for the search: enabled **1.4 / 0.8 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5 ms**, disabled
   **1.2 / 0.5 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 ms**. **Marginally slower with it, on every one
   of the five**, because `consistent` already prunes on the first bound
   neighbour. Every case matched (`ok=true`) under both.

**AND A PROSE CLAIM ABOUT IT DID NOT REPRODUCE, which is G237's shape.** The
module header said compressing the two sides independently *"would make `c3` on
one side unrelated to `c3` on the other and every comparison downstream
meaningless."* `[RAN]` perturbing exactly that: **22 pass / 0 fail**, then
**30 pass / 0 fail** with the `kicad` tests added. **The sentence is false**: a
signature carries no designator, so two isomorphic graphs produce identical
signature STRINGS and compress consistently even independently; the only effect
is a degraded class LABEL in a message about a difference that is reported
either way. The sentence is gone with the code it was about.

**TWO: THE PER-COMPONENT SIGNATURE COMPARISON.** A multiset comparison of
`<value>|<libId>|<connected pins>` stood between the connection multiset and the
search. `[RAN]` removing the arm: **30 pass / 0 fail**. `[RAN]` dropping the pin
list from the key as well: **30 pass / 0 fail**. It is redundant by argument too:
by the time it ran, the component multiset, the edge count and the connection
multiset had agreed, and **an injective node map preserving pin numbers over
equal edge counts covers every edge on both sides**, so a pin-set difference
cannot survive the search even with a coarser key. The comparison is deleted and
the signature survives as the search's grouping key, which the module now says.

**THREE, AND THIS ONE IS A LESSON ABOUT PERTURBING RATHER THAN ABOUT THE CODE: A
ONE-SIDED PERTURBATION OF A SYMMETRIC CHECK CANNOT GO RED.** The first attempt at
the connection-multiset perturbation disabled only `connOnlyA`. `[RAN]`
**27 pass / 0 fail** - because `connOnlyB` catches the same differences from the
other side. The same was true of the component multiset. **A green there says
nothing about the check and everything about the perturbation**, and reading it
as *"this check has no teeth"* would have deleted a check that does. Both are now
perturbed in both directions and both go red.

> **THIS IS A DIFFERENT CLASS FROM G236's FOUR, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE
> POINT OF RECORDING IT - ruling R55's closing instruction.** **G236** and
> **G237** are about an **ASSERTION THAT CANNOT FAIL**: the check was written,
> the check was wrong, and running it proved nothing because it compared
> something against itself. **This is a PERTURBATION THAT CANNOT DETECT.** The
> assertion was fine. The check had teeth the whole time. What could not fail was
> the *probe* - and **the probe was the remedy G236 prescribes.**
>
> **SO THE REMEDIES ARE DIFFERENT, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A FIFTH
> INSTANCE.** G236's remedy is *drive it red once*, and **that remedy is exactly
> what produced the false green here**: the drive WAS performed, it came back
> green, and the green was wrong about the code. A reader who meets only G236
> will take a green drive as evidence the check is inert and delete a check that
> works. **The remedy for THIS class is to ask what else could have caught the
> defect the perturbation introduced** - and for a symmetric check the answer is
> *its mirror image*, which is why both multisets are now perturbed on both
> sides. The same question also exposed the probe in **G243** row two's drive,
> where a `tsc` run whose CONTROL also failed proved nothing about the two cases
> it was meant to discriminate.
>
> **THE END STATE, which is the figure to quote rather than the journey:** `[RAN]`
> **20 perturbations, 20 red, 0 green**, each restoring the file it edited and
> asserting the restore byte for byte before continuing.
>
> **AND THE CLAUSE HAS FIVE INSTANCES ACROSS TWO AUTHORS, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT
> A CLASS RATHER THAN A LAPSE - rulings R60 and R61.** Two of them are on the SAME
> ruling, R53's type change, within a day:
>
> | author | the probe | why it proved nothing |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | **the implementer** `[CONFIRMED]` | a one-sided perturbation of the component multiset | `compOnlyB` catches the same differences from the other side |
> | **the implementer** `[CONFIRMED]` | a one-sided perturbation of the connection multiset | the same, through `connOnlyB` |
> | **the implementer** `[CONFIRMED]` | `bunx tsc --noEmit` on a single probe file | a single-file invocation ignores the project `tsconfig`, so unrelated `lib/kicad/install.ts` errors came back for **all three cases including the control** |
> | **the reviewer** `[RELAYED]` | a probe with `// @ts-expect-error` written at the head of a comment | the directive **suppressed the diagnostic it was there to catch**, so the case passed for the wrong reason; re-driven clean afterwards |
> | **the reviewer** `[RELAYED]` | a hand-built `ReferenceGraph` treated as representative of `graphFromNetlist`'s output | the shape was unreachable through the production path, so its 14-node urgency figure described no input the gate can see. **Withdrawn by its author**; see the R57/R61 block above |
> | **the implementer, Task 20** `[CONFIRMED]` | the jumper-geometry run's **three controls were all NEGATIVE** - `Jumper:Jumper_2_Open` and the two capacitors, each answering `0 of 5` inside slots | **a control that returns the same answer as the treatment tests nothing.** Three negatives cannot distinguish a correct measurement from a probe that only ever answers zero. **It is a NEW SHAPE**: not a probe that cannot fail, but a control that cannot differ. Every figure it reported reproduced, so no result changed - what changed is what the run established. See **G245**, where the missing positive control was supplied and passed |
>
> **WHAT THAT STRENGTHENS, and it is the reason to record more than one: the
> clause is not about carelessness in one author.** Two people reached false
> greens by **four different routes** - a one-sided perturbation, a wrong compiler
> invocation, a suppressed diagnostic, an unreachable input - and **none of them
> looks like a mistake while you are making it, because in every case the probe
> RAN AND REPORTED SOMETHING.**
>
> > **AMENDED, TASK 20: THE TABLE NOW CARRIES FIVE AND THE CLAUSE IS WIDER THAN
> > "A CONTROL THAT PASSES".** The fifth row is a control that passed and could
> > not have answered differently, which the clause as written does not exclude -
> > a negative control for a predicate that is answering negative everywhere is
> > indistinguishable from a broken predicate. **So the clause is now: every probe
> > needs a control that passes AND that could have answered differently.**
> > `[RELAYED]` the controller counts this as the **eighth** route to a false
> > green on this branch; that count is its own and was not re-derived here, and
> > what is confirmed here is the row.
>
> **THAT IS THIS BRANCH's FIRST ARGUMENT FROM MECHANISM RATHER THAN FROM
> EXHORTATION FOR WHY A CONTROL BEATS A DISCIPLINE.** A control that passes is
> what separates *"my probe discriminates"* from *"my probe emits output"*, and it
> **catches all four routes without the author having to anticipate which one they
> are taking.** Every other remedy on this branch - read the whole diff (**G235**),
> drive every assertion red (**G236**), check your own prose (**G237**) - asks the
> author to look for something, and so can only catch a failure the author has
> already imagined. **A control is a check the probe has to pass, not an
> instruction the author has to remember**, which is why it is the one remedy here
> with an argument behind it rather than a hope.

**FOUR: THE REFUSAL THAT SEPARATES "COULD NOT FINISH" FROM "AGREED" HAD NEVER
BEEN TAKEN.** `matchGraphs` bounds its backtracking and reports exhaustion as a
problem. `[RAN]` perturbing that arm to `if (false)`: **22 pass / 0 fail**. The
budget is now a parameter *solely* so a test can exhaust it, and the test
asserts the refusal says `This is NOT a pass` and does NOT say `topology
differs`, because reporting an unfinished search as a difference between the
drawings would be a false defect report.

- **Found** 2026-10-21, Task 18, by driving every new check red against the
  implementation rather than against the assertions. **The three deletions and
  the one addition were all made in the same change as the measurement.**
- **Evidence** the perturbation harness is a scratchpad throwaway and is NOT
  committed, which is this entry's own weakness and is stated rather than
  glossed: what IS committed is the resulting code and
  `tests/schgen/gates/reference-graph.test.ts`, whose budget-refusal case and
  two-three-rings case are the two the deletions left standing on. **A check that
  could have failed and did:** the final drive is `[RAN]` **20 perturbations, 20
  red, 0 green**, and each one restores the file it edited and asserts the
  restore byte for byte before continuing - an unrestored source would stop the
  run rather than silently poison the next perturbation.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the code, wrote the perturbations,
  ran every figure quoted above and read each output. **The timing figures are
  single runs, not repeated measurements**, which is why the conclusion drawn
  from them is only *"no measurable benefit"* and not a speedup claim.
- **Why it is open** **the code is fixed; the METHOD finding is what stays
  open.** Three of the four items here are closed by deletion or by a new test.
  What is open is item three: **nothing stops the next agent from perturbing one
  side of a symmetric check and reading the green as a finding**, and the only
  thing standing against it is this paragraph. It is the same shape as **G235**'s
  and **G237**'s remedies - a discipline with no mechanism - and the same doubt
  applies.
- **What would settle it** nothing for the signature-comparison deletion; it is
  done and the review confirmed it. **AND NOTHING FOR THE REFINEMENT EITHER - THAT
  QUESTION IS CLOSED, which this clause said otherwise for one round.** It read
  that there was *"an open question and it is not mine to close"*, that the
  review's construction *"did not reproduce here"*, that *"four constructions were
  tried and none did"*, and that the discriminator *"rests on a threshold this
  writer measures at 120 nodes and the review measures at 14"*. **Every clause of
  that is now false** and it is quoted rather than deleted because **this is the
  clause a later agent reads to find out what to do next, and it was telling them
  a settled dispute was live** - the exact failure the clause set exists to
  prevent. What closed it: the construction was written down, **reproduced here
  exactly**, and is committed as a test; its 14-node urgency is **withdrawn by its
  author**; and **120 nodes is the figure of record**. The R57/R61 block above has
  the figures. **The refinement is kept, is guarded, and nothing is waiting on
  anybody.**
  **CRITERION for item three: a perturbation reported as leaving a check green
  has been shown to be the only way that check could have caught the defect** -
  i.e. a symmetric check is perturbed on both sides, and a discriminating probe
  has a CONTROL that passes, before a green is believed. **The control clause has
  FIVE instances across two authors** (rulings R60 and R61, the table above):
  this task's one-sided perturbations of the component and connection multisets,
  the implementer's single-file `tsc` run, the reviewer's suppressed
  `@ts-expect-error`, and the reviewer's hand-built `ReferenceGraph` treated as
  representative of what `graphFromNetlist` emits. It is cheap:
  **a probe whose control also fails has measured nothing**, and the clause
  catches that without the author having to anticipate their own error.
  **MECHANISMS, both untried:** a harness that refuses a perturbation whose
  needle appears more than once in the file, which would have flagged both
  one-sided attempts mechanically; or a harness that requires every perturbation
  set to carry an unperturbed control run and refuses a set whose control is not
  green. Neither is built, because the harness is a throwaway and committing one
  is a larger decision than this task's - **but note that the second mechanism is
  the one that generalises, since "perturb its mirror image" only applies to a
  symmetric check while "your control must pass" applies to every probe.**

### G242 - FOUR THINGS GATE 8's COMPARISON DOES NOT DO: two deliberate narrowings that make it STRICTER, one of which could make two different symbols compare equal, one type declared twice on purpose, and a structural bypass that M1 refuses and M2 would act on

**RECORDED BECAUSE EACH IS A PLACE A LATER READER WOULD OTHERWISE READ THE GATE
AS CLAIMING MORE THAN IT DOES**, and because the first one will produce a
difference that looks like a false positive and must not be treated as one.

**ONE: THERE IS NO PIN-SYMMETRY MODEL.** Pedals' gate 8 treats an allow-listed
non-polarised two-pin symbol's pads as interchangeable - `SYMMETRIC_LIB_IDS`
plus a per-netlist declaration (`OscarConfig.symmetricSymbols`), each id checked
against its `<libpart>`'s polarity mark in `gates/oscar/symbols.ts`. **None of
that is ported.** Here every pin matches by number, so **a non-polarised
capacitor whose two pads are wired the other way round from the reference is
reported as an undeclared difference.**

**IT ERRS TOWARD FAILING AND NEVER TOWARD PASSING, which is why it was shipped
this way rather than guessed at.** `CLAUDE.md`: *an empty whitelist that refuses
loudly beats a general rule that quietly accepts a guess.*

> **THE DANGER HERE IS NOT THE FALSE POSITIVE. IT IS THE FIX SOMEBODY WILL REACH
> FOR, AND RULING R54 REQUIRES THIS ENTRY TO FORBID IT IN ADVANCE.** The
> controller, verbatim: *"The danger is the next agent who sees a non-polarised
> capacitor wired pad-for-pad the other way round, recognises it as harmless, and
> **ADDS A PERMITTED DELTA FOR IT.** That is the provenance violation this gate
> exists to prevent, arriving through the gate's own escape hatch, and it would
> look reasonable at the time."*
>
> **SO: A DIFFERENCE OF THIS SHAPE IS DIAGNOSED, NEVER DECLARED.** Pin symmetry
> is a **missing MODEL**, not a permitted electrical change. **No transformation
> produces a pad swap** - nothing in this repository transforms either drawing,
> which is exactly why M1's permitted delta is `{ kind: "empty" }` - so there is
> no `from` to name, and a delta entered for one would have to invent its
> `from`. That is the breach `lib/schgen/gates/declared-delta.ts`'s module
> comment forbids and **G104** records the withdrawal of: *"a generator defect
> could be retrospectively classified as an intended change."* A pad swap is
> electrically nothing and is still a difference between the two drawings, and
> whether it is a generator defect or a missing symmetry model is a question to
> ANSWER, not to route around.
>
> **AND THE DISCRIMINATOR HAS TO SURVIVE THE SEARCH TO BE READABLE AT ALL, which
> is why the colour refinement was restored under ruling R57** (**G241**): if a
> real difference comes back as *"the search did not complete"* instead of a
> stated topology difference, the operator gets nothing to discriminate on and is
> invited to raise a budget instead of reading this entry. **On reachable inputs
> that threshold is 120 nodes - 3.75x the larger reference - and the 14-node
> figure that made this look urgent was WITHDRAWN by its own author** once the
> construction behind it turned out to be a graph `graphFromNetlist` cannot emit.
> **G241** records both, and the reason: pin-labelled connection signatures are
> orientation-sensitive while a net expands to a clique, so on any real netlist an
> orientation change is caught before the search is reached. **This discriminator
> was never actually at risk on a real drawing**, which is worth knowing before
> anybody treats it as fragile.
>
> **IT IS ALSO THE FIRST THING TO CHECK WHEN THE GATE FIRST RUNS AGAINST A
> GENERATED SIDE** (**G240**'s criterion). A non-empty `undeclared` list whose
> entries are all two-pin passives with their pins transposed is this entry, not
> a generator defect; anything else in that list is a generator defect until a
> declared transformation accounts for it. **Read the list before reading it as
> either.**

**WHAT PORTING IT WOULD NEED, so the next agent does not re-derive it:** the
allow-list is keyed by exact library id and validated against each component's
`<libpart>` - the symbol's pin-polarity mark - and `lib/kicad/netlist.ts`'s
`importNetlist` exposes neither. It reads `(libsource (lib ...) (part ...))` and
keeps only `part`.

**TWO, AND IT FOLLOWS FROM THE SAME GAP: THE GRAPH KEYS ON THE LIBSOURCE PART
NAME, NOT A FULL `Library:Part` ID.** `ReferenceGraph.nodes[i].libId` is
`ImportedComponent.libPart`, which is `libsource`'s `part` attribute - `"C"`,
`"C_Polarized"`, `"TL072"`. The s-expression netlist carries `lib` beside it and
`importNetlist` drops it. **So two symbols with the same part name in different
libraries would compare equal**, and a swap between them would be invisible to
this gate.

**HOW MUCH THAT MATTERS HERE, measured rather than assumed - and the first
draft of this paragraph got it wrong, which is why it was driven.** `[RAN]` over
both committed netlists' `(libsource (lib ...) (part ...))` blocks:
`pt2399-core` holds **24** blocks naming **3** libraries - `Audio`,
`Connector_Generic`, `Device` - and **5** distinct part names; lab-board holds
**32** naming **5** - `Connector`, `Connector_Generic`, `Device`, `Jumper`,
`Transistor_BJT` - and **7** distinct part names. **Part names appearing in more
than one library: 0 in both.** So the narrowing costs nothing on today's corpus
and is a latent gap rather than a live one. (The draft said one of the libraries
was `Amplifier_Audio`; it is `Audio`. The figure that mattered - zero shared
names - was right, and the name beside it was not, which is **G237**'s shape
caught before it was committed.)

**THREE: `GraphEdit` AND `DeltaEdit` ARE ONE SHAPE DECLARED TWICE, AND THE
DUPLICATION IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.**
`lib/schgen/gates/declared-delta.ts` declares `GraphEdit` with five kinds -
`setValue`, `removePart`, `addPart`, `mergeNets`, `movePin` - and
`lib/schgen/gates/oscar/boundary.ts` declares `DeltaEdit` with the same five
plus a `delta` (a CORE-BRIEF id) and a `why` on every one. **They were not
unified**, because unifying them means choosing M2's provenance channel - a
CORE-BRIEF id against `DeclaredDelta.from` - and that choice belongs with the
CORE-BRIEF reader, which is not ported. `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that *supersede
means delete* and that one canonical model is the rule, so a duplication kept on
purpose is recorded with its price rather than left to be found: **an edit kind
added to one and not the other is a silent divergence nothing checks.**
`boundary.ts` also still says Task 18 *"replaces this file WHOLESALE"*; it does
not, and that file's header now says what Task 18 actually did.

**AND THE `declared` ARM OF `parseDeclaredDeltas` IS EXERCISED ONLY BY ITS OWN
TESTS**, which is **G226**'s state again: no design in this repository declares
`oscar`, and if one did, `checkReferenceGraph` would refuse a declared list as
M2's rather than applying it. **The precondition that would wire it** is M2's
Pultec transformation manifest; **the price** is that a declaration shape nobody
has used may not be the shape M2 wants, and the committed corpus in
`tests/schgen/__fixtures__/deltas/` is the only thing holding it to anything.

**FOUR, ADDED UNDER RULING R58: `parseDeclaredDeltas` IS THE ONLY CALL SITE THAT
BUILDS A `PermittedDelta`, NOT THE ONLY WAY TO BUILD ONE - and M2 is where that
starts to matter.** `declared-delta.ts`'s header claimed *"`parseDeclaredDeltas`
is the only way to obtain a `PermittedDelta` with deltas in it"*. **True of every
call site in this repository, false of the TYPE:** `PermittedDelta` is a
structural union, so a caller can write
`{ kind: "declared", deltas: [{ id, from: "", why: "", edit }] }` as a literal and
never pass through the parser or its blank-`from` refusal.

`[RAN]`, with a control: the literal **typechecks and reaches
`checkReferenceGraph`**, and comes back carrying `DECLARED_DELTAS_ARE_M2` -
**`undeclared` length 1, a FAILURE** - while the control, the same two netlists
under an EMPTY delta, returns `undeclared` length **0**, a pass. **So in M1 the
bypass cannot reach a pass**, because the gate refuses a declared list outright
rather than acting on it.

**WHERE IT BITES IS M2**, which is the milestone that makes a declared list
something the gate applies instead of refusing: at that point a literal with a
blank `from` becomes a permitted electrical change nobody declared a
transformation for, which is the breach item ONE's blockquote forbids arriving by
a different door. **The type is deliberately NOT branded** - R58 applies R54's
reasoning: that is M2's surface and the fix belongs with the task that needs it.
`tests/schgen/gates/declared-delta.test.ts` pins the current behaviour and **goes
RED the day a declared list stops being refused**, which is exactly when somebody
should read this.

- **Found** 2026-10-21, Task 18, while adapting `graphFromNetlist` from the
  pedals XML readers to `importNetlist` - the adaptation Task 11's one-netlist-
  reader criterion requires. **Item three was found while writing the module
  comment that claims the register records it**, which is the only reason it is
  here rather than in prose nobody checks. **Item four is the review's**, and the
  drive and its control are this writer's.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/gates/reference-graph.test.ts` asserts the symmetry
  narrowing as a POSITIVE check - *"reports a non-polarised capacitor's pads
  wired the other way round, having no symmetry model"* - so the behaviour is
  pinned rather than merely described, and the day a symmetry model lands that
  case goes red and has to be rewritten deliberately. **A check that could have
  failed:** `graphFromNetlist` **throws** for a component with no `libsource`
  part rather than keying it by value alone, and that refusal is driven, so a
  netlist missing the field cannot silently weaken the key further. The
  single-library claim is read off both committed netlists' `libsource` blocks.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the two narrowings and for the refusal - this writer
  wrote them and drove both. **The "no part name is shared across two libraries"
  claim is this writer's reading of the two committed netlists and is NOT
  asserted by any check**, so it is true of those two files today and would not
  fail if a third reference broke it.
- **Why it is open** **ALL THREE ARE OPEN BY RULING R54, WHICH IS A DECISION
  RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.** The controller: *"Do NOT add `libsource`'s `lib` to
  `importNetlist`."* Three reasons, his: **the collateral surface is wide and
  shared** - the round trip, `tests/circuits/*` and the stripboard importers all
  read `ImportedComponent`, which is the shape **G235** warns about; **the gate
  has never run against a generated side (G240), so the false positive cannot
  occur yet**; and **the fix is two changes bundled** - pin symmetry and the
  `libId` spelling - *"which deserve separating"*. The mechanism below is
  therefore recorded as the path and **not** as licence to take it now. The first
  item will also produce differences that look like noise to somebody who has not
  read the blockquote above.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION for ONE: a non-polarised two-pin symbol
  declared symmetric has its pads compared either way round, and a symbol NOT so
  declared does not** - the declaration being external to the comparison, as the
  acceptance-criteria invariant requires. **CRITERION for TWO: two symbols with
  the same part name in different libraries compare as different components.**
  **CRITERION for THREE: one edit vocabulary, or a check that the two agree.**
  **CRITERION for FOUR: a `PermittedDelta` carrying deltas cannot be constructed
  without passing the blank-`from` refusal** - which is a statement about the
  TYPE and not about the call sites. **MECHANISM, untried and explicitly deferred
  by R58:** brand the type, so only `parseDeclaredDeltas` can mint one. **Do not
  take it in M1** - it is M2's surface, and in M1 the bypass cannot reach a pass
  because a declared list is refused outright.
  **MECHANISMS, all untried, AND R54 DEFERS THEM - taking one is a decision
  somebody makes, not a gap to close on sight.** `importNetlist` carrying
  `libsource`'s `lib` beside its `part` is a few lines in one reader and makes
  `libId` a full `Library:Part`; the pedals allow-list can then be ported keyed on
  that, which is why TWO's mechanism is ONE's prerequisite. **Watch for
  collateral change (G235) if you take it**: `ImportedComponent` is read by the
  round trip, by `tests/circuits/*` and by the stripboard importers, and a field
  added there reaches all of them. **And separate the two** - R54 is explicit
  that bundling pin symmetry with the `libId` spelling is part of why it waits.
  For THREE, the cheap half is a test asserting the two unions' kind lists are
  equal - which does not unify them but makes a divergence loud - and the real
  settlement is M2 choosing one provenance channel. **What is NOT a mechanism for
  any of the three: a permitted delta.** See the blockquote under item ONE.

### G244 - A TRUE CONCLUSION REACHED BY A SEARCH DESCRIBED MORE THOROUGHLY THAN IT WAS PERFORMED, and the reason the test it licensed survives anyway

**THIS IS G237's SHAPE APPLIED TO A SEARCH RATHER THAN TO A DRIVE, and it is the
harder instance because the conclusion was RIGHT.** **G237** records three prose
claims about the author's own drives that did not reproduce. This records a prose
claim about the author's own **investigation** that did not hold - and **nothing
downstream broke, because the answer was correct.** That is what makes it worth
its own entry rather than a line in G237: a wrong conclusion gets caught by the
next person who tries the thing; **a right conclusion with an overstated search
behind it gets adopted.**

**THE CLAIM.** Asked whether the register's unreachable-input warning licensed a
hand-built graph as a test input, this writer reported having *"gone looking for
text that would contradict you and found the opposite."*

**WHAT WAS ACTUALLY DONE: one grep, over five phrasings** -
`unreachable|cannot produce|no pipeline can produce|input no|a shape the production` -
and two passages read from its hits (**G196** and **G213**(6)). **Contrary text
exists in two entries and neither was found**, `[RELAYED]` from the closing
re-review which located both:

| entry | the contrary line |
| --- | --- |
| **G236** | *"**THE FIXTURE IS TEST DATA IN TEST CODE AND NOT A HAND-BUILT OBJECT.** `blockCircuit` goes through `buildCircuit`... **The real corpus cannot drive this term**"* |
| **G100** | *"`kind: "bus"` is a real authoring option - declared at `lib/schgen/ir/types.ts:145`, validated at `lib/schgen/ir/validate.ts:89`, rendered by `lib/schgen/render/bus.ts` - so this is a **reachable declaration and not a hand-built object**"* |

**THE SEARCH MISSED THEM FOR A BORING AND INSTRUCTIVE REASON: it searched for the
CONCLUSION's vocabulary and not the OBJECTION's.** Both passages turn on
*"hand-built object"*, which was in none of the five phrasings. A grep for the
words you expect to find cannot find the words somebody else used to say the
opposite. **And the miss has a sharp edge: G241 opens *"THIS IS G236's CLASS"*,
so the contrary line sits inside the entry G241 names as its own class, about 650
lines above the text that needed it.**

**WHY THE RULING AND THE TEST SURVIVE, AND THIS IS THE ACTUAL JUSTIFICATION -
NOT THE ONE ORIGINALLY GIVEN.** `[RELAYED]` from the re-review, and adopted here
because it is better than either the controller's reasoning or this writer's:

- **It cuts both ways, and the pro half is stronger.** G236's own defence of its
  fixture is *"the real corpus cannot drive this term"* - **precisely the hub's
  situation**, and precisely what licenses a constructed input.
- **But in both passages what LICENSES the constructed input is that it goes
  THROUGH THE PRODUCTION CONSTRUCTOR** - `blockCircuit` through `buildCircuit`, a
  `bus` rendering through the real validator - **and *"hand-built object"* is the
  pejorative they distance themselves from.** The hub does **not** go through
  `graphFromNetlist`. **So on the register's own phrasing the hub sits on the
  WRONG side of that line**, and the original justification - which rested on
  **G213**(6)'s *input that cannot exist* - was answering a narrower objection
  than the one the register actually raises.
- **What saves it is a mitigation neither G236 nor G100 required of itself:** the
  committed test **asserts the clique beside the hub**, **asserts that the
  production path catches the flip**, and **labels the hub as outside what
  `graphFromNetlist` emits.** A reader cannot take the hub for a reachable input,
  because the test itself shows what the reachable one does. That is the defence,
  and it is stronger than the precedents it leans on.

**AND G196 IS A GENUINE PRECEDENT WITH ONE HONEST DIFFERENCE, `[RELAYED]` and
worth carrying.** It is not a recruitment: a hand-built fixture driving an arm
real data could not reach is exactly its shape, and its criterion - evaluated on
real data **or recorded as unreachable with the reason** - is exactly what R61
plus **G241** do. **The difference: in G196 the unreachability was INCIDENTAL** -
a defect (**G188**'s sub-grid jogs) masked the arm, and once the options changed
the arm ran and fired on `oc-audio` - **while the hub's is STRUCTURAL and
probably permanent**, because a net expands to a clique and that is what
`graphFromNetlist` is. **So G196 is weak as *"this will matter one day"* and
exactly as strong as what R61 actually claims**, which is that a hand-built input
inside an algorithm's declared domain is a legitimate unit test. Neither the test
comment nor G241 claims the first thing; this entry records why they must not.

- **Found** 2026-10-21, Task 18's closing re-review, which went looking for
  contrary text where this writer had reported there was none.
- **Evidence** the two quoted passages, read in full at `docs/known-gaps.md`
  G236 and G100; the grep that missed them is reconstructed above from what it
  searched for. **A check that could have failed:** the two passages were
  resolved against their entries here rather than taken from the review's quote,
  and **G100**'s three source citations (`ir/types.ts:145`,
  `ir/validate.ts:89`, `render/bus.ts`) are what make its *"reachable
  declaration"* claim checkable rather than asserted - which is the standard the
  hub test now meets by asserting the clique.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the miss - this writer made the claim, ran the one
  grep, and re-read both passages after being shown them. **RELAYED** for the
  re-review's location of both entries and for its licensing analysis, which is
  adopted above rather than re-derived.
- **Why it is open** **the conclusion was right, so nothing failed, so nothing
  would have caught this.** That is the whole finding. The register has no
  mechanism that notices an overstated search, and unlike a wrong figure there is
  no downstream artifact to contradict it.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a claim about one's own search states
  what was searched FOR, not only what was found** - so a reader can judge the
  coverage rather than trusting the conclusion. This entry does that for the
  grep that missed. **MECHANISM, untried and weak for the same reason G237's is:**
  there is nothing to run. **A better-than-nothing habit, and it is the one thing
  here with any mechanism behind it: search for the OBJECTION's vocabulary as
  well as the conclusion's** - had *"hand-built"* been one of the five phrasings,
  both passages would have surfaced immediately. That is a checkable omission
  after the fact, which is more than *"search harder"* offers.

**ONE SMALL THING FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE, because the comment claimed
precision it did not have.** The restoration's comment says `refineBoth` is
*"lifted verbatim"* from `f57c5dd^` and that *"a reader diffing against
`f57c5dd^` sees an identical block"*. `[RAN]` it was one newline longer - **2071
characters against 2070** - so a reader diffing would have seen a whitespace
hunk. The extra newline is removed and the block is now byte-identical, driven
with a control that the comparison detects a one-character change.

### G245 - OWNER DECISION: the BOM requirement is a property of the CONSUMER of an artifact, so the drawing path stopped asking - and `transistor-preamp`'s blocker MOVED rather than cleared

**THE OWNER'S WORDS, VERBATIM, AND THEY ARE THE CRITERION.** He asked first:

> *"why does a schematic need bom-level specificity?"*

and then, when the answer came back that it does not:

> *"the gate you describe \*is\* important for pcb layout intended for outsourced
> manufacture-but a fully specified BOM isn't needed for schematics, stripboard
> layout, and, in many cases, tht pcbs."*

So: **the BOM requirement is a property of the CONSUMER of an artifact rather
than of the circuit.** It binds when a part has to be sourced and placed by
somebody else. **A schematic is never that artifact** - it is upstream of every
one of those decisions. **A stripboard layout built by hand is not either**, and
**a through-hole board the owner stuffs himself usually is not** - those are the
three cases he excluded, by name.

**WHAT WAS WRONG, AND WHERE.** `lib/schgen/ir/validate-parts.ts`'s `bomFields`
requires `Manufacturer`, `MPN`, `Supplier` and `SupplierPart` non-empty on every
part whose `refPrefix` is not `TP`, `H` or `FID`. `lib/schgen/ir/validate.ts`
had it in `validateCircuit`'s single `RULES` list, and
`tools/schgen/generate.ts` calls `validateCircuit` and throws on any problem
before it emits anything. **So four purchasing fields per part gated the
emission of a drawing**, and for one circuit that was the ONLY thing gating it:
`[RAN]` `bun tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` before the change reported
`transistor-preamp` at **101** gate-1 problems - 1 header and **100**
`bomFields` - with nothing else wrong with the circuit.

**THE FIX IS A COMPOSITION AND NOT A RULE CHANGE.** `validateCircuit` now runs
`DRAWING_RULES`, the eleven rules a drawing depends on; a new `validateSourcing`
runs `SOURCING_RULES`, which is `[bomFields]`. **`bomFields` itself is
untouched** - `validate-parts.ts` is still in the port's `files[]` and still
byte-checked, the four keys and `BOM_EXEMPT_PREFIXES` are unchanged, and no
flag, mode or widened exemption relaxes it in place. The split is a **declared
divergence** from the port (`tools/schgen/port-manifest.json`, `Task 20`, with
the upstream `sourceSha`), because a `cuts` entry is deletion-only and could not
carry the half of the ruling that has to survive: the consumer the rule still
binds for.

**WHY THE EARLIER DECISION DID NOT CATCH THIS, WHICH IS THE BETTER LESSON.**
`lib/schgen/authoring.ts`'s `BomSource` comment is an honest, well-reasoned
decision - **G149** - that weighed four options: declaring the fields per
component, blanking them with no declaration, widening `BOM_EXEMPT_PREFIXES`,
and writing plausible manufacturers and supplier part numbers. **All four accept
that a purchasing rule gates a drawing.** The option the owner's question raises
- that the gate is in the wrong PLACE - was not among them, and the plausible
reason is structural: `validate-parts.ts` is port-managed and its header says
*"Edit the pedals source and re-run the port rather than hand-editing this
file"*, so changing the rule was outside the frame the decision was made in.
**A port's edit rule can quietly bound what a decision is allowed to consider**,
and that is worth more than the fix.

**THE PORT'S EDIT RULE REINFORCED THE FRAME; IT DID NOT CAUSE IT. THE CAUSE IS
UPSTREAM OF IT, AND IT IS THE BRIEF** - controller ruling **R69**, which accepts
this diagnosis over its own and asks for the attribution recorded against the
brief rather than against the implementer who followed it. `[RAN]`
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-schematic-authoring-m1.md`, Task 9 Step 4,
verbatim: *"**`BomFields` has no source in this model**: `BOM_EXEMPT_PREFIXES`
covers `TP`/`H`/`FID` and nothing else, so **either the authoring file declares
them or `bomFields` refuses** - do not default them to empty strings and do not
widen the exemption list silently. Decide, implement, and record which."*

Both branches of that *"either … or"* are about what the CIRCUIT supplies, and
the two things it forbids by name are the two ways of making the rule stop
asking. **So the move space was enumerated, the fifth option was not in it, and
an implementer obeying the brief exactly COULD NOT REACH *"the gate is in the
wrong place"* without stepping outside its instructions.** That brief is the
controller's, and R69 records the correction as landing there.

**THE GENERALISABLE FORM, in the ruling's own terms: a brief that offers a binary
and forbids the alternatives cannot be escaped by an obedient implementer.** The
more precisely a brief enumerates the options, the more completely it forecloses
the one nobody thought of - and an implementer following it faithfully will
produce the best of the LISTED answers and **never signal that the list was
wrong**. That is a cost of a well-specified brief rather than a defect in one,
and it is the inverse of the usual failure: here the instructions were good
enough to be followed exactly, and being followed exactly is what hid the
option.

**THE MECHANISM IS THE CONTROLLER'S AND IT IS UNTRIED, SO IT IS MARKED AS SUCH
AT ITS AUTHOR'S INSISTENCE: a brief that enumerates options should say what
QUESTION the options answer**, so an implementer can report that the question is
wrong rather than only choosing among answers. **There is no evidence that
works.** It asks an implementer to challenge its own brief, which is the
class of remedy this branch has watched fail: **a discipline stated, accepted,
and then broken by the author who had just stated it.** `[RAN]` three citations,
each from the entry itself rather than characterised: **G235** records that the
implementer put a pattern in a hand-back message and did not write it down *"one
message after writing G234, the entry about exactly that failure"*; **G236**
counts *"three instances in one task - four, counting the one inside the test
written to fix this third"*; **G237**'s own title is *"THE PATTERN THAT SURVIVED
FIVE ROUNDS OF FIXING"*. **Untried, and weak for a known reason** rather than
untried and promising.

**THE MEASUREMENT, PER CIRCUIT.** `[RAN]` a scratch script over
`circuitSpecFrom` + `buildCircuit`, calling both compositions:

| circuit | DRAWING problems (`validateCircuit`) | the classes | SOURCING problems (`validateSourcing`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer` | **3** | 3 `pinsDeclared` (**G151**) | **36** |
| `optical-compressor` | **14** | 14 `netNames` (**G150**) | **148** |
| `pt2399-core` | **18** | 17 `netNames`; 1 `singlePinNets` (**G159**) | **96** |
| `transistor-preamp` | **0** | - | **100** |

`[RAN]` `bun tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` after the change agrees, off by the
one `header` line each as **G178** explains: **4 / 15 / 19** for the first three.
The sourcing figures are **the same 36 / 148 / 96 / 100** the register and
`tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts` carried as `bomFields` counts before
the split, which is the check that the rule still runs on all four circuits.

**AND THIS IS EXACTLY THE FIGURE G178's MECHANISM PREDICTED, BY A ROUTE IT DID
NOT CONSIDER.** That entry's untried mechanism was *"a `bom` entry in
`ComponentOverride` (or a per-circuit BOM beside the authoring declaration)
would drop the remaining refusals to **3 / 14 / 18 / 0**"*. Task 20 supplied no
BOM data at all and the drawing refusals are **3 / 14 / 18 / 0**. The entry also
said *"that would NOT by itself satisfy the criterion"*, and it was right -
see the next paragraph.

**WHAT THE TWO ROUTES AGREEING ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES, and it is evidence FOR the
owner's criterion that nobody set out to produce** (controller ruling, Task 20
review). **G178** predicted those four numbers for a route that SUPPLIES the
purchasing data; Task 20 reached them by a route that supplies none and asks for
none. Two independently-written predictions landing on one figure means **the BOM
demand was ORTHOGONAL to every other rule in the set** - not one of the 380
purchasing refusals was entangled with a net name, a no-connect or a single-pin
net, so satisfying the demand and withdrawing it are indistinguishable in the
arithmetic. **A purchasing requirement that shares nothing with any rule a
drawing depends on is a requirement a drawing does not depend on.** That is the
criterion restated as a measurement, and it is stronger than the argument that
preceded it because the figure was published before this task existed.

**GATE 8's FIRST RUN AGAINST A GENERATED DRAWING IS STILL NOT REACHABLE, AND
THE BLOCKER MOVED RATHER THAN CLEARING. THIS IS THE RESULT WORTH READING.**
`[RAN]` a scratch probe that builds each parity design exactly as
`tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`'s `parityDesign` does and calls `generate` with
`initLock: true` into a `mkdtemp` directory (the committed census forces
`initLock: false`, so it cannot get past the reference lock):

| circuit | where `generate` refuses now |
| --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer` | validation: `part U1: pin 5 (+) is neither on a net nor declared not connected`, and two more |
| `optical-compressor` | validation: 14 net names, `"+9V_PROTECTED"` first |
| `pt2399-core` | validation: 17 net names and the one single-pin net, `"+5V"` first |
| `transistor-preamp` | **validates clean and refuses at LAYOUT**: `block tp-leg-emitter-bypass: ... JP5#1 (Jumper:Jumper_2_Open): no place for its Reference and Value` |

So for `transistor-preamp` the wall is now **one defect** - the field-placement
refusal **G232** records and **G238**'s block table already measured - instead
of four classes of authoring work. **Nothing here attempted it**: ruling R46
reserves **G232** as an owner-visible scope decision, and the brief for this
task says to report this rather than pursue it. **Gate 8 was NOT run**; the
reachability answer above is read off `generate`'s own refusal, which is the
thing that has to stop happening first.

**COLLATERAL DAMAGE FROM A CORRECT FIX: THE CENSUS BECAME LESS INFORMATIVE FOR
THE ONE CIRCUIT THIS CHANGE UNBLOCKED. PARKED UNDER RULING R68, AND IT IS
G235's PATTERN EXACTLY.** That entry names *a change whose PRIMARY effect is
correct and whose COLLATERAL effect is wrong, so a reviewer checking the changed
behaviour passes it* - and the changed behaviour here is right by every check
that was run.

**BEFORE this change**, `transistor-preamp`'s gate-1 census row reported **the
circuit's own validation refusal**: 1 header and 100 `bomFields`. **AFTER it**,
the row reports
`1 other: <tmpdir>/refs.lock.json not found; run pnpm schgen generate --init transistor-preamp.design.ts to create it`
- **a HARNESS artifact**, because `runGates` forces `initLock: false` so the
generation only reads and the reference lock the circuit needs is never created.
Two consequences, and the first is the dangerous one.

**THE ROW MUST NOT BE READ AS THE CIRCUIT'S STATE.** A reader comparing censuses
across this commit sees `transistor-preamp`'s gate-1 refusal **move from 101 to
1 rather than disappear**, and the obvious reading of a surviving refusal is that
the fix did not work. It did: the circuit has **0** `validateCircuit` problems,
which the probe table above drives directly and which
`tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts` pins. **What the row now measures is
the census's own `initLock` choice**, and nothing in the row says so - which is
why it is said here and in `tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`'s header.

**AND THAT LINE IS NOW NON-DETERMINISTIC.** It carries an absolute `mkdtemp`
path, so it differs on every run where every other line of the census output is
stable. A census whose purpose is to be re-run and compared has one line that
never compares equal.

**NOTHING IS FIXED HERE AND NOTHING IS PRESCRIBED.** Changing `initLock` is a
change to `tools/schgen/verify.ts`'s contract rather than to the census, and it
would make a census run write a lock file; whether that is the right route is
not judged here. The criterion is below as (c).

**WHAT MUST SURVIVE TWO OPPOSITE FUTURE ERRORS.** `bomFields` is **not dead
code and must not be deleted**: it is correct and load-bearing for a consumer
that has to source and place parts, which is the case the owner named -
*"pcb layout intended for outsourced manufacture"*. **G241** on this branch is a
safeguard deleted precisely because no check could fail on it, and restored a
round later. Equally, **it must not be put back into `DRAWING_RULES` to make
validation uniform**: uniformity is what the ruling refuses, and the price is
measured above. `lib/schgen/ir/validate.ts`'s header states both, and
`tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts` asserts that no BOM problem reaches
the drawing path.

**THE UPSTREAM OBSERVATION, FOR THE OWNER, NOT ACTED ON.** This decision is
about THIS repository. `digital-pedal-platform`'s generator may legitimately
require sourcing data before it emits, if what its output feeds is a board going
out for assembly - the divergence here is declared and does not ask upstream to
change. **Nothing in the sibling tree was touched** and it was left clean; this
writer has not read its board process and has no view on whether its gate is in
the right place for it.

  | form | what the exclusion is applied to | hits |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `broken` | the output LINE (`grep -v` after a pipe) | **6** |
  | `excludeFile` | the register FILE (`--exclude`), which is what was meant | **9** |
  | `none` | nothing - **the control, which must be the largest** | **12** |

- **What would settle it** three criteria, kept apart from their mechanisms.
  **(a) CRITERION: the first consumer in this repository that emits an artifact
  somebody else sources and places refuses on `validateSourcing` before it
  emits.** **MECHANISM, untried:** whatever produces a fabrication or assembly
  package calls it the way `generate` calls `validateCircuit`.

  **THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF G226's PATTERN AND IS DECLARED AS ONE RATHER THAN
  ARRIVING AS A FRESH CASE FOR SOMEBODY TO REDISCOVER** - controller ruling
  **R67**, which also rules that `validateSourcing` **STAYS and is not to be
  collapsed into its two test callers.** **G226**'s claim, adopted there under
  ruling R35, is that *"a mechanism exercised only by its own tests is a
  mechanism whose first real use is its first test; that is acceptable when the
  precondition for wiring it is NAMED and the price is RECORDED, and it is the
  G201 failure when it is not."* So, both halves, explicitly:

  - **THE PRECONDITION, in one sentence: something in this repository must emit
    an artifact that a third party sources and places** - a fabrication or
    assembly package, a board going out for outsourced assembly, an orderable
    BOM. Nothing does today. When one does, `validateSourcing` is what it calls,
    and that is the whole of what wires this.
  - **THE PRICE: `bomFields` runs in tests and in no pipeline.** Until that
    consumer exists, the rule's four keys are checked on the four parity
    circuits by `tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts` and on two hand-built
    cases by `tests/schgen/ir/validate.test.ts`, and by nothing a person running
    `schgen` would ever reach. **A circuit whose purchasing data silently
    regressed would be caught by those tests and by no artifact**, which is
    acceptable precisely because no artifact here needs the data yet - and stops
    being acceptable the moment one does.

  **WHY THE NAMED COMPOSITION IS LOAD-BEARING AND COLLAPSING IT WOULD COST
  SOMETHING, which is R67's reasoning rather than this writer's:** folding the
  rule back into two test call sites would lose the NAME, and **the name is what
  tells a future fabrication path what to call.** The local half of the argument
  is **G152**'s own untried mechanism - *"a rule outside `validateCircuit`, run
  by the consumers that need footprints"* - which is the same shape for the same
  reason; the durable half is this pattern citation. **G201** is what it costs to
  leave a precondition unnamed: five rounds in which the real pipeline could not
  emit a single ELK block, with a test pinning the gap in place.

  **(b) CRITERION:
  `bun tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` reports zero gate-1 problems for a reference
  AND `bun tools/schgen/remeasure-coverage.ts` reports every block of that
  reference as DRAWS** - **G238**'s criterion, unchanged, with the first half now
  met for `transistor-preamp` and the second half not. **MECHANISM, untried and
  it is not this task's:** **G232**'s defect, which ruling R46 reserves.
  **(c) CRITERION: the gate census reports the CIRCUIT's own state for every
  circuit it lists, and no row of it reports an artifact of the harness** - so
  the one circuit that validates is legible in the committed census, and so no
  line of a tool built to be re-run and compared differs on every run.
  **MECHANISM, untried, and deliberately not prescribed under ruling R68:** one
  route is a census that can create a reference lock in its own scratch
  directory, which today means changing what `runGates` forces about `initLock`
  and letting a census run write a file; **whether that is the right route is
  unjudged here**, and the criterion is met by any route that satisfies it.
  Parked, not deferred: **R68** parks it loudly rather than ruling it
  acceptable.

### G248 - "SUPERSEDE MEANS DELETE" IS DELIBERATELY UNSATISFIED HERE: the stub writer's INVITATION is deleted and the writer itself is KEPT, because it carries this repository's only `kicad-cli` proof that KiCad reads a stub as the circuit means it

**THE PRICE FIRST, IN THE SENTENCE THE CONTROLLER SAID NOT TO SOFTEN: the
pathology G81 describes remains in the tree, reachable by import, for as long as
this stands.** `lib/kicad/schematic.ts` still carries every pin to a net label by
a short wire, still puts connectivity entirely in labels, and still takes
`newUuid: () => string` - so its output cannot be compared by content. **G81**
records that this is the exact thing a third-party review blocked another project
from shipping, and that the blocking review cites THIS repository as where the
pathology was first seen.

**WHAT WAS DELETED, which is what the rule is actually protecting.** Controller
ruling **R65** split the deletion on the grounds that *"supersede means delete"*
exists so nobody finds a superseded pattern and trusts it - *"that is an argument
about somebody REACHING it, not about a test fixture existing"*. So the
invitation went:

| `tests/cli/schematic-stub.test.ts` | `f5a22f2c2a74b0b6c81738a97b8775a5d3911563` |
| the `schematic-stub` script in `package.json` | - |
| `README.md`'s instructions for running it | - |

After this there is no supported path to the pathology: no script, no verb, no
documented command. What remains is a library function three test files import.

**WHAT WAS KEPT, AND WHY DELETING IT WOULD HAVE COST A MEASURED CAPABILITY.**
`lib/kicad/schematic.ts`, `tests/kicad/schematic.test.ts`,
`tests/circuits/kicad-round-trip.ts` and the five `transistor-preamp-*.test.ts`
files stay. **G247** measures why they cannot move: `generate` refuses `lab` at
layout on **G232**'s field-placement defect, and the other four boards have no
`SchematicAuthoring` declaration at all, so `generate` cannot be invoked on them.
`[RAN]` `grep -c 'kicadRoundTrip(' tests/circuits/transistor-preamp-*.test.ts`
returns `1` for each of the five: **five tests, one per board**, each named *"KiCad
reads the generated stub as the same circuit"*, and
`tests/circuits/kicad-round-trip.ts`'s own header is the claim they rest on -
*"the only proof KiCad reads a stub the way the circuit means it, so a missing
kicad-cli FAILS them rather than skipping"*. Deleting the writer deletes those
five and nothing in this repository replaces them today.

**THE TEST THAT DECIDED IT, AND IT IS RECORDED SO A LATER READER CAN DISAGREE ON
THE MERITS RATHER THAN ON THE CONCLUSION** (controller ruling **R71**). The
question asked was: **is the coverage at stake coverage of the STUB, or of the
CIRCUITS?** If it is the stub's, it dies with the stub and the argument for
deleting the writer whole wins. **It is the circuits'.** Those five tests
establish that five transistor-preamp board MODELS produce KiCad-valid netlists
with the connectivity the model intends; the stub is merely the vehicle that
gets them there. **That claim is covered nowhere else, because the generator
refuses these circuits** - which is the same fact that stopped this task doing
what it was written to do. Deleting them would discard a measured fact about the
hardware to satisfy a rule about discoverability, **and the rule's own text is
about discoverability**: *"left as a stub for somebody to find and TRUST"*.

**AND THE SIZE OF THAT COVERAGE IS SMALLER THAN THE BRIEF'S WORDING SUGGESTS,
WHICH DOES NOT CHANGE THE CONCLUSION.** It is five TESTS, not five files:
`[RAN]` `grep -c 'kicadRoundTrip(' tests/circuits/transistor-preamp-*.test.ts`
returns `1` for each file, and the other 59 of the 64 tests in those files are
independent of the writer (**G247** has the per-file counts). **Five, and still
irreplaceable** - that second clause is what carries the ruling, not the first.

**THE NON-DELETION IS THE CHOICE AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE RATHER THAN AS AN
OVERSIGHT.** `CLAUDE.md` says a pattern replaced by a better one *"is removed in
the same change, not left as a stub for somebody to find and trust"*. That is not
what happened here. The rule is unsatisfied, knowingly, with the precondition
named below, and the reason is that the alternative trades a measured capability
for a tidier tree.

**THE PRECONDITION, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN THE ADDENDUM STATED AND WIDER THAN

validate, so the five tests can move onto `generate` and `roundTrip`"*.

`tests/kicad/schematic.test.ts` and the tripwire itself, move what moves onto

**IT WAS WRITTEN BECAUSE THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THIS ENTRY IS A GOOD ONE AND IT IS
ONLY ANSWERED BY ENFORCEABILITY.** The argument: *"supersede means delete" exists
BECAUSE "we'll delete it when X" has failed before, and **G81** IS that failure* -
its criterion said the stub goes when the replacement lands, the replacement
landed, nothing noticed, and this entry is a second promise of the same thing.
**Prose is exactly what failed as G81.** Controller ruling **R72**: the split is
*"only defensible if the promise is enforceable"*.

**THE CRITERION IS THE CONTROLLER'S AND NOT THE IMPLEMENTER'S, WHICH IS WHAT
DISPOSES OF THE INVARIANT OBJECTION.** `CLAUDE.md` forbids an agent authoring the
acceptance criteria for the artifact it produces, and a guard deciding when an
artifact may be deleted is such a criterion. So it was authored elsewhere, in
**R72**, verbatim: *"the writer, its test and the five preamp tests may be
deleted when `generate` accepts a preamp board."* The test transcribes it and its
header says not to refine it.

**AND THE OTHER OBJECTION - that it makes the suite fail on the day somebody
fixes a defect - IS ANSWERED BY WHAT KIND OF TEST IT IS.** It does not assert
that a defect persists. **It fires when a PRECONDITION IS MET, and its message is
an instruction rather than an obstacle.** Ruling **R72**: *"The cost is one
annoyed afternoon; the cost of the alternative is G81 again, and we have the
receipt."* That is this repository's refusals-teach rule applied to a deletion
obligation.

**TWO THINGS THE TRIPWIRE DOES NOT COVER, SAID HERE SO IT IS NOT OVER-READ.**

1. **IT COVERS THE FIELD-PLACEMENT HALF, FOR `lab` ONLY. THE FOUR MISSING
   DECLARATIONS ARE COVERED BY NO CHECK AND CANNOT BE.** `buffered`, `feedback`,
   `loop` and `staged` have no `SchematicAuthoring`, so `circuitSpecFrom` has
   nothing to build from and `generate` cannot be offered them at all - **a test
   cannot fire on a file nobody has written.** So the day **G232** is fixed the
   tripwire fires on `lab` and says nothing about the other four, and the person
   it fires at still has **G247**'s second mechanism to do. **That gap is honest
   and it is smaller than the one being closed**, which was the whole precondition.
2. **IT IS GREEN WHENEVER `generate` REFUSES, FOR ANY REASON.** A broken symbol
   library or a changed KiCad would hold it green exactly as **G232** does. It
   fires on ACCEPTANCE and not on the absence of a particular defect. That is the
   criterion as authored and the test's header says so.

### G249 - M1's CLOSING DRAWING COMPARISON, AND IT IS AN OBSERVATION WITH NO VERDICT: the comparison the step asked for could not be made, because `generate` refuses the circuit whose hand-arranged drawing is the reference

**WHAT THIS IS NOT.** It is not a gate-8 result, it is not a pass, and it is not
a readability finding under spec §3.5. **No gate was run.** Controller rulings
**R56** and **R66** both exist because this step is the single most likely place
on this plan to read an empty `undeclared` list as a verdict, and that list is
empty because nothing generated. §3.3 gives no threshold, and §3.5's reviewer
gets the criterion and never a list.

**WHAT THE STEP ASKED FOR AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE DONE.** Task 19 Step 8 asks for
a `transistor-preamp` board generated through `schgen`, printed, read, and set
beside the committed hand-arranged `circuits/transistor-preamp/lab-board.kicad_sch`
printed the same way. **G247** measures why there is no generated side:
`generate` refuses `lab` at layout on **G232**'s field-placement defect and
cannot be invoked at all on the other four boards. R66 governs that case - *"say
that the comparison could not be made on a generated drawing and compare what you
have ... named for what it is"*.

**SO WHAT IS COMPARED, NAMED FOR WHAT IT IS: TWO DIFFERENT CIRCUITS.** The human
side is `lab-board.kicad_sch`, 32 components, one A3 sheet, arranged by hand. The
generated side is the ported `mini` fixture - the only design in this repository
that generates - whose `signal` sheet is A3 and whose `power` sheet is A4.
**`mini` is used here as A DRAWING TO LOOK AT and not as a comparison subject**;
ruling **R50** forbids pointing gate 8 at it to obtain a row, and nothing here
runs a gate. **Every difference below could be a difference between the circuits
rather than between the drawers, and nothing here separates the two.**

`[RAN]` `kicad-cli` 10.0.5 `sch export pdf` on both, `pdftoppm -r 170 -png`, read
with the Read tool. `[RAN]` greps over the two `.kicad_sch` files:

| | `lab-board` (human) | `signal` (generated) | `power` (generated) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| paper | A3 | A3 | A4 |
| placed symbols (`^\t(symbol`) | **40** | 23 | 21 |
| of those, `power:GND` | 8 | 7 | 6 |
| wire segments | **89** | 39 | 17 |
| junctions | 21 | 5 | 7 |
| block frames (`^\t(rectangle`) | **0** | **7** | **4** |
| label glyphs | **43** | 17 | **1** |
| distinct net names labelled | 18 | 9 | 1 |

**THE ONE NUMBER WORTH READING TWICE, AND IT IS THE ONE G81 IS ABOUT.** Of the
human drawing's 43 label glyphs, **`GND` appears 11 times and `BASE` nine**, on
top of 8 separate `power:GND` arrows; `IN_EXT` and `COLLECTOR` appear three times
each. Of the generated `signal` sheet's 17, **every repeated name appears exactly
twice** - `SIG_IN`, `AMP_OUT`, `XI`, `XO`, `FL_CS`, `FL_CLK`, `FL_DI`, `FL_DO` -
once on each side of the block boundary it crosses, and the `power` sheet carries
**one label on the whole page**. That is the rev-2 requirement **G81** quotes
(*"Generated schematics SHALL show local circuit topology using wires. Net labels
SHALL primarily identify rails, interfaces, and connections crossing
functional-block or sheet boundaries"*) visible in the artifact. **It is NOT a
claim that the generator would do better on the lab board**, which it refuses.

**WHAT THE HUMAN DRAWING LOOKS LIKE.** Signal flows left to right across the
middle - `J1` into `C2` into the `BASE` rail, `Q1` at centre, `C3` out to `J2` -
with `VCC` as one horizontal wire along the top and the bias legs hung off the
`BASE` rail as six vertical columns, each jumper then resistor then trim-pot. The
four divider legs are drawn as four aligned instances of one shape, so a reader
sees immediately that they are four of the same thing, which is what they are.
Twelve lines of bench settings sit in the lower left. **Where it is worse:** the
drawing occupies roughly the top-left half of the A3 and the right third and
bottom quarter are empty; it has **no `title_block` at all** - `[RAN]`
`grep -A 6 title_block` on it returns nothing, so the printed Title, Date and Rev
fields are blank; and the repeated `BASE` and `GND` labels mean that tracing the
base node means finding nine glyphs rather than following a wire.

**WHAT THE GENERATED DRAWING LOOKS LIKE.** Seven dashed blue frames on the
`signal` sheet, each titled in its own top-left corner - *Spare op-amp channel*,
*Op-amp supply*, *Input connector*, *Input buffer*, *Crystal*, *SPI flash*,
*Output connector*. Inside each, local topology is wires: `R3` into the node
`C6` hangs off, into `U2A`'s `+` input, with the feedback wire drawn round the
body. The title block carries its own provenance - *"Generated by schgen from
tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/mini/index.ts; do not edit"* and *"KiCad
10.0.5; stock libraries 895cc96749279fdc"* - which the human drawing has no
equivalent of and which is the thing that makes a generated artifact auditable.
**Where it is worse, and these are the observations the step owes:**

1. **The blocks descend in a staircase and leave a large diagonal of white
   space.** *Crystal*, *SPI flash* and *Output connector* step down and right
   instead of filling the row, so the drawing uses roughly the top-left half of
   an A3 while crowding the blocks into a narrow column. The human drawing wastes
   paper too, so this is not a difference between them - it is a defect both have.
2. **`Op-amp supply` is a tall thin frame with its text set vertically.** `3V3`,
   `V+`, `V-` and `GND` are rotated 90 degrees, which is harder to read than the
   human drawing's horizontal `VCC` rail, and the frame is barely wider than the
   glyphs it holds.
3. **Rails are per-block arrows rather than one rail across the sheet.** `3V3`
   and `GND` appear as separate arrows inside *3V3 regulator*, *3V3 decoupling*,
   *VIN sense divider* and *Power flags*, so following the supply means hopping
   between glyphs. The human drawing's single `VCC` wire along the top is easier
   to follow, and this is the one place where the label-versus-wire comparison
   runs the OTHER way.
4. **`Spare op-amp channel` sits hard against the left frame margin**, with
   `U2B`'s pin numbers 5 and 6 touching the sheet border, and the X on the unused
   output sits over the pin-7 number.
5. **There is no flow direction across blocks.** Inside a block the convention is
   left to right; between blocks there is none, so the eye has no path from
   `Input connector` to `Output connector`.

- **Found** 2026-10-21, Task 19 Step 8.
- **Evidence** `[RAN]` `tools/schgen/kicad-run.ts`'s own `exportPdf` on both
  files with `kicad-cli` 10.0.5, `pdftoppm -r 170 -png`, and the images read with
  the Read tool - not described from the s-expressions. The table's figures are
  greps over the two files, stated above with their patterns so they can be
  re-run. **A check that could have failed:** the `power` sheet's label count is
  **1** and the human board's is **43** against similar symbol counts (21 and
  40), so the measurement distinguishes the two styles rather than returning a
  figure proportional to size; a count that tracked only part count would have
  returned similar numbers. The refusal that removed the generated side is
  **G247**'s, driven there with its own control.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer exported, converted and read both
  drawings and ran every grep in the table.
- **Why it is open** **it is open because it is not a finding to fix.** It is the
  closing measurement M1 owes, recorded so the next reader does not have to
  re-derive what the generator's output looks like, and so that the comparison
  the step actually wanted is visibly still outstanding.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: the same comparison taken on ONE circuit

### G250 - MEASURED: 300 tests across 27 files - 8.2% of the suite - NEVER REGISTER when one of five documented local prerequisites is absent, and 144 of them leave no name, no failure and no `testsuite` element; the VeroRoute binary is 48 of the 300

**THE FIGURE IN THIS HEADING WAS 48 UNTIL 2026-10-21, AND THE OLD ONE IS LEFT
VISIBLE RATHER THAN OVERWRITTEN**, because the way it was wrong is the finding:
48 was one arm of a five-arm phenomenon, measured correctly, generalised
cautiously, and **six times too small.** Everything below the six-arm block is
the original entry, unchanged except where it is marked, and its 48 still
reproduces exactly.

**THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS A PROPERTY OF AN UNVERSIONED LOCAL PREREQUISITE
RATHER THAN OF THE SUITE.** `[RAN]` **300 tests across 27 files - 8.2% of the
3672 - fail to REGISTER under at least one of the five prerequisite absences
measured here.** None of them is reported as a skip, a failure or a name; the
union is taken as the worst arm per file, and the per-file table is below.
**The prerequisites are the ones `README.md` documents**, so this is not an
exotic tree: it is what a reader who followed the Prerequisites section
imperfectly gets.

`--reporter=junit`, run **sequentially** (several files carry wall-clock budgets
sized for full-suite contention, so two concurrent suites would turn a timeout
into a confound). `SCHGEN_SOURCE` was set in five of the six; unsetting it is

**4650** against the root element's own **3672**. The figures below count only
**top-level `<testsuite>` elements** - direct children of `<testsuites>`, whose
`name` is the file path - and count `<testcase>` elements by **walking the
tree**, never trusting a `tests=` attribute. Loss is a per-file diff of two
reports rather than a difference of two totals.

**THE PATTERN IS NOT "A PREREQUISITE". IT IS WHERE THE RESOLUTION SITS - AND IT
IS A TRICHOTOMY, NOT THE DICHOTOMY THE WHOLE-BRANCH REVIEW NAMED.**

1. **Resolved inside a test, or inside a function a test calls: it FAILS LOUDLY
   and loses nothing.** Chrome, `SCHGEN_SOURCE` and qt@5. Three arms, zero
   registration loss.
2. **Resolved at MODULE SCOPE in a test file: the file loses everything after
   the throw.** `kicad-cli` and the VeroRoute binary. Two arms, 294 and 48.
3. **Resolved at module scope and handed to `describe.skipIf`: the tests
   REGISTER and SKIP.** `[RAN]` 50 testcases skip in the `nokicad` arm and in no

**AND CLASS 3's OWN GUARD AGAINST BEING INVISIBLE EXHIBITS CLASS 2.**
`tests/schgen/__fixtures__/require-tool.ts`'s `skipWithout` throws instead of
skipping when `CI` is set, and its comment states the reason exactly: *"a test
that skips when its tool is missing cannot be told apart from one that passed,
so in CI the job that provides the tool is the proof that the test ran."* **The
throw lands at module scope**, because `describe.skipIf(skipWithout(...))`
evaluates there. `[RAN]` over those three files, with two controls:

| arm | result |
| --- | --- |
| `KICAD_CLI` masked, `CI` unset | 0 pass / **50 skip** / 0 fail, `Ran 50 tests across 3 files` |
| `KICAD_CLI` masked, **`CI=1`** | 0 pass / **3 fail, 3 errors**, `Ran 3 tests across 3 files` - **the guard erases 47 of the 50 instead of failing them by name** |
| **CONTROL**: `kicad-cli` present, `CI=1` | **50 pass / 0 fail**, 118 `expect()` calls |

**So the designed remedy for an invisible skip produces an invisible erasure**,
and the control rules out the alternative reading that `CI=1` reddens these
files for some unrelated reason: with the binary present and `CI` set they all
pass.

**THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS COULD HAVE ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY AND DID, WHICH IS WHAT
MAKES THE TWO LOUD ARMS MEAN ANYTHING.** Three arms show **zero** registration
loss and one of them (`noqt`) **exits 0 with no failure at all** - a
prerequisite `README.md` calls required is completely invisible to the suite
once the binary it builds exists. A method that found every prerequisite
destructive, or none, would have failed this comparison.

count can tell a 48-test change in what RAN from a 48-test change in what PASSED.**

### G251 - MEASURED: the repository root's `make check` does NOT pass, and has not for at least this branch - FOUR of the eleven declared boards refuse, in TWO different cause classes, identically before and after Task 19

treat KiCad *"the way you would a compiler"*. **An agent that runs it at the
root as a final check gets exit 2 and has to decide, with nothing to consult,
whether it broke something.** Task 19 had to make that decision and measured it
rather than reasoning about it, and the next agent should not have to repeat the
measurement.

`[RAN]` `make -C boards/<board> check` per board, at `8813c6c` (before this task,
in a `git worktree` with `node_modules` and `.tools` linked) and at this commit:

listed ten and left out the one whose cause is DIFFERENT, which defeated the
entry's whole purpose: a reader found three of four refusals explained and would
reasonably have concluded the fourth was theirs:

| **`pt2399-core`** | **exit 2, 1 `FAIL`** | **exit 2, 1 `FAIL`** | **a MISSING EXPORT** |

**The passing boards are the control and they could have answered differently**:
a change that broke the board checks generally would have taken `pultec-mid`,

Its layout is not the problem; the circuit module does not export what the BOM
conditions check requires. **A reader who knows only about the mid-layout class
will not recognise this one**, which is the reason it is named here rather than
folded into a count.

**WHAT THE THREE MID-LAYOUT BOARDS REFUSE ON.** Not a toolchain problem and not
the lead-span whitelist the message's tail talks about: **the committed layouts
are unfinished.** `transistor-preamp-lab`'s
reports `BASE incomplete`, `BYPASS_CAP incomplete`, `COLLECTOR incomplete`,

here reaches a state called 'done'."* **G62** already records that
`boards/transistor-preamp-lab`'s layout *"has 19 strips joining two different

the board is reported as failing rather than as passing. A constraint whose check

forever by construction, and the only honest thing to do with it is say so in a
committed file rather than leave a reader to discover the gap.

### G255 - MEASURED: NINE files on this branch exceed `CLAUDE.md`'s 300-500 line ceiling, up to 705 lines, and nothing recorded any of them - because every per-task verification checked only its own range, which a cap on an accumulating total cannot be checked by

**THE STRUCTURAL POINT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE LIST, so it goes first.**
`CLAUDE.md`: *"Code files should be no larger than 300-500 lines long. Anything
larger than that should be refactored."* Task 17's and Task 18's closing
verifications each measured the files their own range touched and each correctly
found them inside the band. **Both were right, and nine files are over the cap,
because a per-range check cannot see an accumulating total.** Nothing on this
branch ever swept the tree. The register tracks this rule elsewhere - **G20**
records a 557-line file in the pinned FORK and **G222** records one forced
deviation - so the absence is not that the rule is untracked; it is that the
only checks run were scoped to a diff.

**THE SWEEP, DRIVEN AT `e3baa03` OVER EVERY TRACKED `.ts` FILE.** `[RAN]` 846
tracked `.ts` files, of which **11** exceed 500 lines:

| 739 | `tests/sim/netlist.test.ts` | on `main` at 739 - **pre-existing** |
| **639** | `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts` | **new** |
| **606** | `tools/stripboard/run-dir.ts` | **new** |
| **576** | `tests/stripboard/rules.test.ts` | **new** |
| **576** | `tests/stripboard/materialize-run-perturbed.test.ts` | **new** |
| **566** | `lib/schgen/render/compose.ts` | **new** |

| **528** | `tests/schgen/elk/junctions.test.ts` | **new** |

**NINE, NOT EIGHT, AND THE NINTH IS THE ONE A "NEW FILES" METHOD MISSES.**
The whole-branch review reported eight, counting files absent from `main`.
`circuits/pultec/physical/parts.ts` **existed on `main` at 395 lines - inside
the band - and is 530 at HEAD**, so this branch is what put it over. `[RAN]`
`git show main:<file> | wc -l` against `wc -l` for all three pre-existing
files: 739→739, 538→538, **395→530**. **The lesson is the same one the
structural point makes, one level up: a method scoped to new files cannot see a
cap crossed by growth**, which is exactly how a per-range check cannot see a
cap crossed by accumulation.

**THE TWO PRE-EXISTING BREACHES ARE RECORDED HERE TOO** - 739 and 538 lines,
both on `main` before this branch and neither in this file. They are not this
branch's doing and they are not nothing: a reader who met the nine would

correct primary effect and the stale pointers are the wrong collateral one.
**Nine splits in one round is nine chances at that**, with no round after this
